enslavers, for up to forty-five hours each week

enslavers for up to forty-five hours each week;
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "under which ... week"는 관계절이지만, 이를 포함한 앞 문장은 "it created a system"을 중심으로 한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤의 "this arrangement ... collapsed early"도 삽입구 때문에 주어와 동사가 떨어져 있을 뿐 독립절이다. 따라서 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 연결한 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 시간 표현 앞에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣고, 두 절 사이에는 아무 부호도 두지 않아 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 등위접속사 but을 쓴 점은 맞지만 but 뒤에 쉼표를 붙여, 접속사와 그 뒤 절을 잘못 끊어 놓았다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank form an independent clause built on "it created a system," even though they contain the relative clause "under which...". The words after the blank, "this arrangement ... collapsed early," are also an independent clause; the inserted phrase "originally intended to last until 1840" just separates its subject from its verb. So you need a semicolon between the two clauses, which makes D correct. A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, so it creates a comma splice. B adds an unneeded comma before the time phrase and puts no punctuation between the two clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence. C is right to use the conjunction "but," but the comma after "but" wrongly cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞("it created a system ... under which ... week")과 뒤("this arrangement ... collapsed early ... and full emancipation came in 1838")가 모두 독립절이므로 세미콜론(D)이 유일하게 적합. A는 comma splice, B는 run-on, C는 "but," 뒤 쉼표가 접속사와 절을 잘못 분리. 역사적 사실(1833년 법, 도제제도, 주 45시간 무급 노동, 1840년 예정→1838년 조기 종료)도 정확. 관계절과 삽입구로 절 구조를 가려 두 단계 판단을 요구하므로 medium에 적합하며, A·C는 부분적 타당성을 지닌 오답.

advisory.note: 관계절과 삽입구 때문에 두 독립절을 바로 알아보기 어려워 medium 난이도에 맞음. 역사적 사실(1833년 법, 주당 45시간, 1840년 예정이던 도제 제도가 1838년에 조기 종료)도 정확함.

problem.stimulus: The Boland Amendment, a series of measures that Congress passed between 1982 and 1984 to restrict US involvement in Nicaragua's civil war, had banned federal agencies from funding the Contra rebels ______ the Reagan administration's secret diversion of profits from covert arms sales to Iran into Contra accounts, revealed to the public in November 1986, therefore directly defied the will of the legislature.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'The Boland Amendment ... had banned ... rebels'는 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 'the Reagan administration's secret diversion ... therefore directly defied the will of the legislature'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이므로, 두 절을 잇는 세미콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절 두 개를 이어 comma splice가 된다. B는 'which'가 'defied'의 목적어 역할을 해야 하는데 'defied' 뒤에 이미 목적어 'the will'이 있어 관계절이 성립하지 않는다. problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, "The Boland Amendment ... had banned federal agencies from funding the Contra rebels," is an independent clause. The text after it, "the Reagan administration's secret diversion ... therefore directly defied the will of the legislature," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb, so C is correct: a semicolon joins the two clauses. A connects the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B doesn't work because "which" would have to be the object of "defied," but "defied" already has an object, "the will." D leaves out the comma that should come before "and" when it joins two long independent clauses, and "therefore" in the second clause already shows how the ideas connect, so the joined sentence is awkward and run-on.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검산 완료: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절(주어 'The Boland Amendment'/동사 'had banned'; 주어 'diversion'/동사 'defied')이므로 세미콜론이 적절. A는 comma splice, B는 'which'의 문법적 역할 부재, D는 쉼표 없는 'and'로 긴 독립절 결합 및 'therefore'와의 어색한 결합. 역사적 사실(Boland Amendment 1982–84, 1986년 11월 공개) 정확. 긴 삽입구와 'therefore'가 훑어 읽기를 방해하도록 설계되어 medium 적합.

problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank, 'demonstrators twice tried ... Highway 80', is an independent clause, even with the long appositive attached. A joins the clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice; the comma only seems natural because it follows the long appositive. B puts no punctuation between the clauses, which makes a run-on sentence. problem.passage:
On July 14, 1789, crowds of Parisian artisans, shopkeepers, and laborers converged on the Bastille, a medieval fortress that had long held prisoners detained by royal order without trial. The attackers were seeking gunpowder stored inside, but the fortress's fall carried a meaning far greater than its military value. The Bastille, a symbol of the arbitrary power wielded by King Louis XVI and his ______ within days, citizens had begun dismantling its walls stone by stone.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: On July 14, 1789, crowds of Parisian artisans, shopkeepers, and laborers converged on the Bastille, a medieval fortress that had long held prisoners detained by royal order without trial. The attackers were seeking gunpowder stored inside, but the fortress's fall carried a meaning far greater than its military value. The Bastille, a symbol of the arbitrary power wielded by King Louis XVI and his ______ within days, citizens had begun dismantling its walls stone by stone.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: ministers, was quickly targeted for demolition;
ministers was quickly targeted for demolition;
ministers, was quickly targeted for demolition,
ministers; was quickly targeted for demolition,
problem.explanation: "a symbol of ... ministers"는 주어 The Bastille에 대한 비필수 동격구이므로 앞뒤에 쉼표가 짝을 이뤄야 하고, 이어지는 "within days, citizens had begun..."은 독립절이므로 두 독립절 사이에 세미콜론이 필요하다. A가 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. B는 세미콜론은 맞지만 동격구를 닫는 쉼표가 빠졌다. C는 동격구는 올바르게 닫았으나 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. D는 주어와 동사 사이에 세미콜론을 넣어 문장을 끊고 뒤에서 쉼표 스플라이스까지 만든다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "a symbol of ... ministers" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, The Bastille, so it needs a comma on both sides. After that, "within days, citizens had begun..." is an independent clause, so you need a semicolon between the two independent clauses. A meets both requirements. B has the correct semicolon but leaves out the comma that closes the appositive. C closes the appositive correctly, but it joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. D puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, splitting the sentence, and then adds a comma splice later on.

B(닫는 쉼표 누락), C(콤마 스플라이스)는 각각 한 조건만 충족하는 부분적 오답이고 D(주어-동사 사이 세미콜론)도 겉보기엔 그럴듯함. 두 단계 판단(동격구 경계 + 절 경계)이 요구되어 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 글자 참조와 일치하며 모순 없음. 역사적 사실(1789년 7월 14일, 왕명 구금, 함락 직후 철거 시작) 정확. 저작권 문제 징후 없음.

advisory.note: 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. 하나는 동격구를 닫는 쉼표, 다른 하나는 독립절 사이의 세미콜론이다. B와 C는 각각 한 가지 조건만 충족해서 비교해 봐야 배제된다. D는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 역사적 사실에도 문제가 없다.

problem.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, claims about how many enslaved Africans died during the Middle Passage, the forced voyage across the Atlantic, rested on scattered travelers' accounts and rough guesses that varied widely. Beginning in the 1990s, researchers compiled ship manifests, port records, and insurance documents from tens of thousands of voyages into a single searchable database. By comparing the number of captives recorded at embarkation with the number recorded on arrival, historians could finally ______ the mortality of the crossing with a precision that earlier scholars had lacked.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: For much of the twentieth century, claims about how many enslaved Africans died during the Middle Passage, the forced voyage across the Atlantic, rested on scattered travelers' accounts and rough guesses that varied widely. Beginning in the 1990s, researchers compiled ship manifests, port records, and insurance documents from tens of thousands of voyages into a single searchable database. By comparing the number of captives recorded at embarkation with the number recorded on arrival, historians could finally ______ the mortality of the crossing with a precision that earlier scholars had lacked.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 이 글은 이전의 대략적인 추정과 대비해, 승선 인원과 도착 인원의 기록을 비교하는 방법을 써서 결과가 '정밀하다(precision)'고 강조한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 사망률을 수치로 측정한다는 뜻의 C 'quantify'가 들어가야 한다. A 'dispute'는 이전 추정을 수정했다는 점과 일부 맞지만, 숫자를 비교해 정밀하게 얻는 결과물을 나타내지 못한다. B 'publicize'는 연구를 널리 알렸다는 그럴듯한 의미이지만 기록을 비교하는 방법이나 정밀성과 연결되지 않는다. D 'diminish'는 사망률을 줄이거나 축소한다는 뜻이 되어, 정확한 측정을 말하는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text contrasts earlier rough guesses with a new method: comparing the recorded numbers of captives at departure and at arrival. It also stresses that the result had "precision." So the blank needs a word meaning "measure in numbers," which makes C, "quantify," the answer. A, "dispute," fits partly because the new work did challenge older estimates, but it doesn't describe the precise result that comes from comparing numbers. B, "publicize," sounds plausible for research, but it has nothing to do with the method of comparing records or with precision. D, "diminish," would mean reducing or downplaying the death toll, which goes against a passage about measuring it accurately.

advisory.note: 정답 C(quantify)는 'comparing the number... with a precision' 문맥으로 확실히 뒷받침됨. 오답 A(dispute)는 이전 추정과의 대비로 부분 근거가 있고, B(publicize)도 그럴듯함. D는 비교적 쉽게 배제됨. 다만 'number'와 'precision'이 강한 단서여서 medium 범위 중 쉬운 쪽에 가까움. 대체로 적합함. Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database(1990년대 구축) 관련 사실 진술도 정확함.

problem.passage:
Historians once portrayed the Meiji Restoration of 1868 as a clean break in which Japan's new leaders swept away feudal society almost overnight. More recent scholarship complicates that picture. While the government did abolish the samurai class's hereditary stipends and build a conscript army on European models, many former samurai found new roles as bureaucrats, police officers, and factory managers, carrying older habits of hierarchy and discipline into modern institutions. In this view, the Restoration did not erase the feudal order so much as ______ it, turning its personnel and values toward new purposes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Historians once portrayed the Meiji Restoration of 1868 as a clean break in which Japan's new leaders swept away feudal society almost overnight. More recent scholarship complicates that picture. While the government did abolish the samurai class's hereditary stipends and build a conscript army on European models, many former samurai found new roles as bureaucrats, police officers, and factory managers, carrying older habits of hierarchy and discipline into modern institutions. In this view, the Restoration did not erase the feudal order so much as ______ it, turning its personnel and values toward new purposes.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 메이지 유신이 봉건 질서를 지운 것이 아니라 그 인력과 가치를 새로운 목적으로 돌렸다고 말하므로, '다른 용도로 바꿔 쓰다'라는 뜻의 C가 정답이다. A는 '해체하다'로, 'not erase … so much as' 구조가 요구하는 대조를 만들지 못하고 지워 버렸다는 옛 견해를 되풀이한다. B는 옛 관습이 이어졌다는 점에서 일부 맞지만, 그것들이 '새로운 목적'으로 돌려졌다는 변화를 담지 못한다. D는 유럽식 군대 모델에서 연상되는 단어이지만, 봉건 질서를 '모방'했다는 것은 같은 사람과 가치를 직접 다시 썼다는 내용과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the Restoration took the feudal order's people and values and turned them "toward new purposes," so C, "repurpose," is the most precise choice. A, "dismantle," would mean the same thing as "erase," but the sentence structure "not erase... so much as" needs a contrast, and A just repeats the older view the passage argues against. B, "preserve," fits the idea that old habits carried on, but it misses the key point that those habits were put to new uses. D, "imitate," may bring to mind the European military models, but the government didn't copy feudalism. It reused feudalism's actual people and values directly.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 'repurpose'는 'not erase … so much as' 대조 구조와 뒤따르는 'turning its personnel and values toward new purposes'에 의해 명확히 뒷받침된다. A는 erase와 동의어라 대조 구조에서 배제되고, B는 연속성 측면에서 부분적으로 맞지만 '새 목적'을 놓치며, D는 유럽 모델 언급에서 유인되는 그럴듯한 오답이다. 두 단계 판단(구조 파악 + 후속 절 확인)이 필요하여 medium에 부합한다. 다만 'repurpose'가 지문의 'new purposes'와 어근을 공유해 다소 힌트가 되는 점은 참고. 역사적 사실(가록 폐지, 징병제, 사족의 관료·경찰 진출)도 정확하며, 한·영 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 'turning ... toward new purposes'가 repurpose를 거의 그대로 풀어 쓰고 있어 약간 쉬운 편이지만, preserve가 그럴듯한 오답 역할을 해서 medium 범위 안에 있다. 사실 관계(1868년, 녹봉 폐지, 징병제)는 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Historians often describe Britain's Factory Act of 1833 as a turning point in labor law, but its early effect on mill floors was limited. The act barred children under nine from textile mills and capped the hours of older children, yet it appointed only four inspectors to cover thousands of factories. Many mill owners, aware that a visit was unlikely, kept children at work well past the legal limit. Later acts, which added inspectors and required certified proof of age, were needed before the 1833 restrictions could be said to have been meaningfully ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Historians often describe Britain's Factory Act of 1833 as a turning point in labor law, but its early effect on mill floors was limited. The act barred children under nine from textile mills and capped the hours of older children, yet it appointed only four inspectors to cover thousands of factories. Many mill owners, aware that a visit was unlikely, kept children at work well past the legal limit. Later acts, which added inspectors and required certified proof of age, were needed before the 1833 restrictions could be said to have been meaningfully ______.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문의 핵심은 1833년 법이 이미 제정되었지만 감독관이 너무 적어 공장주들이 법을 어겼고, 이후 감독관을 늘리고 연령 증명을 의무화한 뒤에야 법이 실제로 지켜지게 되었다는 점이다. 따라서 '실제로 집행되다'를 뜻하는 D가 정답이다. A는 법의 초안 작성을 뜻하는데, 1833년 규정은 이미 작성되어 통과된 상태였으므로 맞지 않는다. B는 알리는 것을 뜻하지만, 지문은 공장주들이 법을 알고도 단속이 없어서 어겼다고 하므로 문제는 홍보가 아니었다. C는 '이의를 제기하다'라는 뜻인데, 추가 감독관과 연령 증명은 법에 맞서는 것이 아니라 법을 뒷받침하는 조치이다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the 1833 act had already been passed, but with only four inspectors, mill owners could break it without much risk. Only later acts that added inspectors and required proof of age made the limits actually work in practice, so D, "enforced," is correct. A doesn't fit because the restrictions had already been drafted and passed in 1833. B is wrong because the problem wasn't that people didn't know about the law; the owners knew about it and ignored it because inspections were unlikely. C is wrong because more inspectors and proof-of-age rules supported the law instead of opposing it.

advisory.note: 정답 D가 맞고, 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 일치하며 정확하다. 사실관계: 9세 미만 금지와 감독관 4명은 사실이다. 다만 1833년 법에도 이미 의사의 연령 증명서 규정이 있었으므로 '이후 법이 공인 연령 증명을 요구했다'는 서술은 단순화된 것이다. 이후 1844년 법 등이 이를 강화한 것은 사실이라 오류로 보지는 않았다. 난이도는 medium 하한선에 가깝다. 단서 'four inspectors', 'visit was unlikely', 'added inspectors'가 강해 D가 비교적 쉽게 보인다. 그래도 drafted/publicized는 훑어 읽으면 끌릴 수 있어 적합으로 판정했다.

problem.passage:
When the Union Navy began its blockade of Southern ports in 1861, it had too few ships to seal more than 3,500 miles of coastline, and fast blockade runners slipped through often. Historians who judge the strategy only by how many runners were caught miss its broader effect, however. Because the risk of capture drove up shipping insurance and freight costs, imported goods such as salt, medicine, and railroad iron became scarce and expensive across the Confederacy. The blockade did not have to stop every vessel to work; by steadily raising the cost of trade, it ______ the Southern economy over four years rather than defeating it in a single stroke.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When the Union Navy began its blockade of Southern ports in 1861, it had too few ships to seal more than 3,500 miles of coastline, and fast blockade runners slipped through often. Historians who judge the strategy only by how many runners were caught miss its broader effect, however. Because the risk of capture drove up shipping insurance and freight costs, imported goods such as salt, medicine, and railroad iron became scarce and expensive across the Confederacy. The blockade did not have to stop every vessel to work; by steadily raising the cost of trade, it ______ the Southern economy over four years rather than defeating it in a single stroke.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 봉쇄가 모든 배를 막지는 못했지만 무역 비용을 '꾸준히' 올려 '4년에 걸쳐' 효과를 냈고, '한 번에 무찌른' 것은 아니라고 설명한다. 따라서 점진적으로 약화시켰다는 뜻의 A(wore down)가 가장 정확하다. B(cut off)는 봉쇄와 관련된 말이라 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 배들이 자주 빠져나갔다고 하므로 완전한 차단을 뜻하는 표현과 맞지 않는다. C(took over)는 연방이 남부 경제를 장악했다는 뜻으로, 지문에 나오지 않는 통제를 암시한다. D(stirred up)는 경제를 자극하거나 활성화한다는 뜻이라 물자 부족과 가격 상승이라는 내용과 반대된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the blockade didn't stop every ship but kept "steadily raising the cost of trade" "over four years," and it didn't defeat the economy "in a single stroke." So you need a phrase meaning gradual weakening, and choice A, "wore down," fits that best. Choice B, "cut off," is tempting because it sounds like what a blockade does, but the text says runners got through often, so the South wasn't fully cut off. Choice C, "took over," suggests the Union took control of the Southern economy, and nothing in the text supports that. Choice D, "stirred up," means stimulating or agitating something, which goes against the scarcity and high prices the text describes.

problem.passage:
At the Berlin Conference of 1884–1885, delegates from fourteen states, most of them European, set rules for claiming territory in Africa. No African ruler or representative was invited to take part. Historians often point out that the conference did not actually hand out most of the land; that division came later, through treaties and military campaigns. Even so, the meeting's principle of "effective occupation," which held that a claim was valid only if the claiming power kept a real presence there, ______ the scramble that followed: it encouraged rival powers to rush officials and troops inland to secure territory before their competitors could get there.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: At the Berlin Conference of 1884–1885, delegates from fourteen states, most of them European, set rules for claiming territory in Africa. Historians often point out that the conference did not actually hand out most of the land; that division came later, through treaties and military campaigns. Even so, the meeting's principle of "effective occupation," which held that a claim was valid only if the claiming power kept a real presence there, ______ the scramble that followed: it encouraged rival powers to rush officials and troops inland to secure territory before their competitors could get there.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 콜론 뒤 문장은 이 원칙 때문에 경쟁국들이 경쟁자보다 먼저 영토를 차지하려고 서둘렀다고 설명하므로, 원칙이 쟁탈전을 '가속화했다'는 B가 정답이다. A(끝냈다)는 회의 이후 분할이 이어졌다는 문맥과 반대이다. C(기록했다)는 회의가 원칙을 문서로 정했다는 점에서 그럴듯해 보이지만, 원칙이 이후 행동을 부추겼다는 인과 관계는 담지 못한다. D(예견했다)는 원칙이 나중의 쟁탈전보다 먼저 나왔다는 순서와는 맞지만, '부추겼다'는 능동적 영향은 표현하지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: The clause after the colon says the principle pushed rival powers to rush inland before their competitors could, so the principle sped up the scramble. That makes B, "accelerated," correct. A ("concluded") contradicts the text, which says the division continued after the conference. C ("documented") sounds plausible because the conference did write down rules, but it misses the cause-and-effect link: the principle drove what came next. D ("anticipated") fits the timeline, since the principle came before the scramble, but it only means the principle predicted the scramble, not that it actively encouraged it.

problem.passage:
Popular accounts often describe the Bolsheviks' seizure of power in October 1917 as the moment that ended tsarist autocracy in Russia. Historian Sheila Fitzpatrick has noted that this framing ______ two distinct episodes: Tsar Nicholas II had already abdicated months earlier, during the February Revolution, and the Bolsheviks took control not from the monarchy but from the Provisional Government that had replaced it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Popular accounts often describe the Bolsheviks' seizure of power in October 1917 as the moment that ended tsarist autocracy in Russia. Historian Sheila Fitzpatrick has noted that this framing ______ two distinct episodes: Tsar Nicholas II had already abdicated months earlier, during the February Revolution, and the Bolsheviks took control not from the monarchy but from the Provisional Government that had replaced it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 대중적 서술이 2월의 차르 퇴위와 10월 볼셰비키의 임시정부 전복이라는 '서로 다른 두 사건'을 하나로 합쳐 버린다고 지적하므로, 별개의 것을 혼동해 하나로 묶는다는 뜻의 C(conflates)가 정답이다. A는 서술이 사실을 과장한다는 뜻이라 그럴듯하지만, 지문이 문제 삼는 것은 규모의 과장이 아니라 두 사건을 하나로 뭉뚱그린 점이다. D는 순서 문제처럼 보이지만, 대중적 서술은 사건의 순서를 뒤바꾸는 것이 아니라 앞선 사건을 뒤의 사건 속에 섞어 버린다. B는 두 사건을 구분한다는 뜻이어서, 지문이 비판하는 내용과 정반대이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says popular accounts treat October 1917 as the end of tsarist rule, even though the tsar's abdication (February) and the Bolsheviks' takeover from the Provisional Government (October) were "two distinct episodes." So the framing merges separate events into one, and that is exactly what C (conflates) means. A may look right because the framing does give October too much credit, but the text's complaint is about blending two events together, not about overstating how big one event was. D suggests the order of events is flipped, but the accounts don't reverse the sequence; they fold the earlier event into the later one. B means the framing keeps the events apart, which is the opposite of the text's criticism.

advisory.note: 사실관계(2월 혁명 때 니콜라이 2세 퇴위, 10월 임시정부 전복) 정확함. Fitzpatrick 귀속은 일반적인 수준이라 문제없음. 'two distinct episodes'가 단서이고, exaggerates가 부분적으로 맞는 함정으로 작동해 medium 수준에 맞음.

problem.passage:
Textbooks often credit the Peace of Westphalia (1648) with creating the modern system of sovereign states, but some historians argue that this account overstates the treaties' novelty. The agreements did end decades of religious warfare in central Europe, yet many of the principles later associated with them, such as rulers' authority over religion within their own territories, had already been stated in the Peace of Augsburg nearly a century earlier. On this view, Westphalia did less to invent sovereignty than to ______ arrangements that earlier settlements had outlined but had failed to secure.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Textbooks often credit the Peace of Westphalia (1648) with creating the modern system of sovereign states, but some historians argue that this account overstates the treaties' novelty. The agreements did end decades of religious warfare in central Europe, yet many of the principles later associated with them, such as rulers' authority over religion within their own territories, had already been stated in the Peace of Augsburg nearly a century earlier. On this view, Westphalia did less to invent sovereignty than to ______ arrangements that earlier settlements had outlined but had failed to secure.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 웨스트팔리아가 주권을 새로 '발명'했다기보다, 이전 조약이 제시했지만 확고히 하지 못한 질서를 굳혔다고 본다. 따라서 '강화하다, 공고히 하다'를 뜻하는 D가 정답이다. A는 웨스트팔리아가 종교 전쟁을 끝냈다는 점에서 무언가를 없앤 듯 보이지만, 이전 원칙을 계승했다는 맥락과 정반대다. B는 시간 순서가 틀렸다. 그 질서는 이미 이전에 제시되었으므로 '예견했다'고 할 수 없다. C는 '새로 만들어 내다'라는 뜻이어서, 지문이 부정하는 '발명'과 같은 의미가 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text argues that Westphalia didn't invent sovereignty. Instead, it made firm the arrangements that earlier treaties had outlined but failed to secure, so "consolidate" in D is correct. A might seem tempting because the treaties ended religious wars, but the text says Westphalia carried earlier principles forward, which is the opposite of abolishing them. B gets the time order backward: the arrangements already existed, so Westphalia couldn't have anticipated them. C means "to create something new," which is just another way of saying "invent," and the text rejects that idea.

'did less to X than to Y' 구문 해석 + 문맥 대비라는 두 단계 판단이 필요해 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 글자와 결론이 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D(consolidate)는 'outlined but failed to secure'와 정확히 맞물린다. C는 'less to invent'와 같은 뜻이라 대비 구조를 이해해야 배제되고, B는 시간 순서를 확인해야 배제되므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. A는 상대적으로 쉽게 걸러진다. 아우크스부르크 화의(1555, cuius regio 원칙)에 관한 사실 관계도 정확하다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 옥수수·감자가 여러 대륙의 주식이 되고 말과 소가 아메리카 경제를 재편했다는 근본적이고 광범위한 변화를 예로 든다. 따라서 '근본적으로 바꾸었다'는 뜻의 A가 가장 정확하다. B는 이동 자체가 생활을 '기록했다'는 뜻이 되어 주어와 맞지 않는다. C는 유럽의 이익 중심 서술을 반박하는 맥락에서 긍정적 결과만 가리키므로 양쪽 모두의 변화라는 중립적 요지를 담지 못한다. D는 질병 등을 떠올리면 그럴듯하지만, 지문의 예는 새 주식과 경제 재편이라는 구조 변화이지 단순한 혼란이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The text's examples show deep, lasting change: maize and potatoes became staples across several continents, and horses and cattle remade economies in the Americas. That is exactly what A means: they fundamentally changed daily life. B doesn't work because the transfers themselves didn't record anything. C is only about positive outcomes, but the text is pushing back against a story of European gain and stresses neutral, sweeping change on both sides. D might seem right if you think of disease, but the examples given describe new staples and rebuilt economies, which is a restructuring, not just a disturbance.

problem.stimulus: Between 1405 and 1433, the Ming admiral Zheng He led seven expeditions across the Indian Ocean, reaching ports from Southeast Asia to the coast of East Africa. problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: Dreyer은 원정의 주된 목적이 정복이 아니라 조공 수집과 위세 과시였다고 보므로, '정복 원정'이라는 견해는 함대의 목적을 잘못 묘사한다(C). A는 부정적 평가라 그럴듯하지만, '과장하다'는 정복이 실제 목적이었는데 규모만 부풀렸다는 뜻이 되어, 목적 자체가 달랐다는 지문의 논지와 맞지 않는다. B는 그 견해가 목적을 정확히 기록한다는 의미가 되어 Dreyer의 반박과 모순된다. D는 견해 자체가 목적을 의심한다는 뜻이 되는데, 그 견해는 목적에 대해 확신에 찬 주장을 할 뿐 의심하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Dreyer argues that the voyages mainly aimed to collect tribute and display Ming power, not to conquer, so the "conquest" view gets the fleet's purpose wrong. That makes C, "misrepresents," the right answer. A sounds tempting because it's also critical, but "exaggerates" would mean conquest really was the purpose and the view just overstates it, while the text says the purpose was something else entirely. B would mean the view records the purpose accurately, which contradicts Dreyer's rebuttal. D doesn't work either: the conquest view makes a confident claim about the fleet's purpose rather than casting doubt on it.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 옳다. 오답 A(exaggerates)는 C처럼 부정적 평가라서 매력적인 오답이다. '규모 과장'과 '목적이 아예 다름'을 구별해야 배제할 수 있어 medium 난이도에 맞다. 다만 A는 '전투가 드물었다'는 근거와 일부 맞물리므로 약간의 논란 여지는 있다. 사실관계(1405–1433년, 7회 원정, Dreyer의 견해)는 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Before 1804, France had no single body of private law: northern regions followed hundreds of local customs, while the south relied on adaptations of Roman law, so a contract valid in one province might be unenforceable in the next. The Napoleonic Civil Code replaced this patchwork with one set of written rules applied uniformly across the nation. Historians note that the code's influence did not stop at France's borders; jurisdictions as varied as Belgium, Louisiana, and Quebec later adopted versions of it, making its principles ______ in much of the continental legal tradition that persists today.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

problem.explanation: 지문은 이 법전이 여러 법역에 채택되었고 그 원칙이 오늘날까지 이어지는 대륙법 전통 안에 남아 있다고 말하므로, 그 원칙이 이 전통의 '토대가 되는' 것이라는 뜻의 A가 정답이다. B는 1804년 이전 지역별 관습을 다룬 지문 앞부분과 연결되어 그럴듯해 보이지만, 이 법전이 국경을 넘어 퍼졌다는 내용과 모순된다. C는 법전이 여러 법역에 채택되었다는 점에서 논쟁이 있었을 것처럼 보이지만, 지문 어디에도 반대나 논란은 언급되지 않는다. D는 '오늘날까지 지속되는(persists today)' 전통이라는 표현과 정면으로 충돌한다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the code was adopted in many places and that its principles remain part of a continental legal tradition that still exists today, so A, "foundational," fits best: the code's principles form the base of that tradition. B might catch your eye because the passage opens by describing France's local customs, but the point here is that the code spread beyond France, which is the opposite of provincial. C might seem possible since the code was adopted by different jurisdictions, but the text never mentions any dispute or opposition. D directly contradicts the statement that the tradition "persists today."

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 완료: 국경을 넘어 채택되어 오늘까지 지속되는 대륙법 전통의 '토대'라는 맥락에 부합. B는 앞부분의 지역 관습과 연결되어 매력적 오답, C는 채택/도입 과정의 논쟁 가능성으로 부분적 근거, D는 'persists today'와 충돌. 역사적 사실(1804년 법전, 벨기에·루이지애나·퀘벡 영향) 문제 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 결론과 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움. 두 단계 판단(국경 확장 + 지속성) 요구로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 오답이 약함: provincial은 '국경을 넘어'와, temporary는 'persists today'와 바로 충돌하고, contested는 근거가 없음. 비교해야만 배제되는 매력적인 오답이 거의 없어 medium 기준(부분 근거를 가진 오답 2개 이상)을 충족하지 못함. 사실관계(벨기에·루이지애나·퀘벡의 영향)는 대체로 타당함.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The First Opium War (1839–1842) began after Qing official Lin Zexu seized and destroyed more than 20,000 chests of British-held opium at Humen.

problem.question: The student wants to emphasize how the terms imposed in 1860 expanded on those imposed in 1842. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Whereas the First Opium War began when Lin Zexu destroyed over 20,000 chests of opium, it ended with the Treaty of Nanjing, which opened five ports and ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain.
Whereas the First Opium War was fought against Britain alone, the Second Opium War also involved France, and both conflicts ended in what historians call "unequal treaties."

Whereas the Treaty of Nanjing had opened five ports and surrendered Hong Kong Island, the Convention of Peking went further, opening still more ports, legalizing opium, and installing foreign diplomats in Beijing.
Whereas many agreements of the era gave China few reciprocal rights, the Convention of Peking opened additional ports, legalized the opium trade, and let foreign diplomats live in Beijing.
problem.explanation: 목표는 1860년 조약 조건이 1842년 조건보다 확대되었음을 강조하는 것이므로 두 조약의 조건을 모두 제시하고 후자가 더 나아갔음을 보여야 한다. C는 난징 조약의 조건과 베이징 조약의 추가 조건을 대비하며 'went further'로 확대를 드러내므로 정답이다. A는 1842년 조약만 다루고 1860년 조건이 없다. B는 참전국의 차이와 '불평등 조약'이라는 공통점만 말할 뿐 조약 조건 비교가 없다. D는 1860년 조건은 정확히 쓰지만 1842년 조건과 비교하지 않아 확대를 보여주지 못한다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to show that the 1860 terms expanded on the 1842 terms, so the sentence needs the terms of both treaties and a signal that the later one went further. C does exactly this: it lists the Treaty of Nanjing's terms, then shows the Convention of Peking adding more ports, legal opium, and diplomats in Beijing. A covers only the 1842 treaty and never mentions the 1860 terms. B compares who fought each war and notes that both ended in "unequal treaties," but it never compares what the treaties actually required. D gives the 1860 terms correctly but sets them against unequal treaties in general instead of the 1842 terms, so it can't show any expansion.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C 검산 완료: 1842년 난징 조약 조건(5개 항구, 홍콩섬)과 1860년 베이징 협약 조건(추가 항구, 아편 합법화, 외교관 상주)을 모두 제시하고 'went further'로 확대를 명시해 목표에 부합. A는 1842년 조건만, B는 참전국·'불평등 조약' 공통점만, D는 1860년 조건만 제시하여 확대 비교가 불가능. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 사실 관계(아편 2만여 상자 소각, 난징 조약 5개 항구·홍콩섬 할양, 영·프 연합, 베이징 협약 조건)는 노트 수준에서 정확(아편 합법화·외교관 상주는 톈진 조약에서 유래해 베이징 협약으로 확정된 것이나 단순화로 허용 가능). 오답 A·D가 부분적 근거(각각 1842년·1860년 조건)를 가져 비교가 필요하고 B도 'Whereas' 대비 구조로 그럴듯하여 medium 적합.

advisory.note: C의 'installing foreign diplomats'는 노트의 'permitted ... to reside'를 다소 강하게 바꿔 쓴 표현이지만 허용 범위다. A는 1842년 조건만, D는 1860년 조건만 정확히 담고 있어 각각 부분적인 근거를 가진 오답이다. 그래서 두 조약을 연결해야 하는 medium 난이도에 맞다.

A gives only the founding date, membership, and headquarters, with no weakness. B states that the US never joined but never explains how that hurt the League's mission. advisory.note: B가 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 강한 오답이고, C도 목적을 다루고 있어 비교해 봐야 배제된다. A는 쉽게 배제된다. D만 목적과 약점을 연결한다. medium 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.explanationEn: To meet this goal, a choice has to include two things: the charter's early failure (the pope voiding it) and the influence it kept having afterward (the reissues and Coke's argument). B joins the two with "Although," so it directly shows that the influence lasted longer than the failure. A only describes where the charter came from and one of its clauses, so it mentions neither the failure nor any later influence. C mentions the failure but nothing about what came after. D shows the charter lasting through its reissues, but it leaves out the early failure, so the contrast the goal asks for never appears.

problem.explanation: 목표는 '법적 판결'이 '헌법상 보장'을 약화시킨 과정을 설명하는 것이므로, 수정헌법 14조(보장)와 Cruikshank 판결(판결)을 연결해야 한다. D는 두 정보를 결합해 판결이 보장을 어떻게 약화시켰는지 보여 준다. A는 법률(Enforcement Acts)과 군대 철수를 다룰 뿐 판결이나 헌법 보장이 없다. B는 헌법 보장은 언급하지만 판결이 빠져 있다. C는 판결을 언급하지만 연대 비교에 그치고 헌법 보장을 어떻게 약화시켰는지 설명하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to show how a court decision weakened a constitutional guarantee, so you need to connect the Fourteenth Amendment (the guarantee) with the Cruikshank ruling (the decision). D does exactly that: it explains that the ruling narrowed the amendment's protection, which weakened federal prosecution. A covers a statute and the troop withdrawal, but it mentions no court ruling and no constitutional guarantee. B mentions the guarantee but leaves out the decision. C names the ruling but only compares dates, so it never explains how the ruling affected the guarantee.

A connects their withdrawal under US pressure and Egypt keeping the canal with the historians' view that the two countries could no longer act as independent imperial powers, so it is the correct answer. B covers only the cause and background of the nationalization, not the outcome. C focuses on US motives and Cold War tensions and never addresses the two European nations' standing. D describes the military intervention but leaves out its result and what that result meant.

advisory.note: A에는 사소한 확대가 있다. 노트에서는 미국이 영국에만 재정 압력을 가했는데, A는 그 압력 때문에 영국과 프랑스가 함께 철수했다고 연결한다. 그래도 정답 판단에는 영향이 없다. C는 오답 선택지로서 노트에 없는 '냉전 긴장' 해석을 덧붙였는데, 이는 허용 범위다. 오답 B·C·D는 모두 영국·프랑스·운하와 관련이 있어 그럴듯하다. 다만 '결과'와 '지위'를 함께 다루는 선택지는 A 하나뿐이라서 medium 중에서도 쉬운 편이다.

problem.passage:
Popular accounts often portray the opening of the Berlin Wall on November 9, 1989, as the direct result of mass street protests in East Germany. Historian Mary Elise Sarotte, however, has argued that the precise timing of the opening owed much to bureaucratic confusion: according to this view, a poorly prepared announcement by East German official Günter Schabowski, who mistakenly stated that new travel rules took effect "immediately," prompted crowds to gather at the border crossings that very night, before the government had any plan for how the rules would actually be carried out.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support the view about the timing of the Wall's opening described in the text?
problem.stimulus: Popular accounts often portray the opening of the Berlin Wall on November 9, 1989, as the direct result of mass street protests in East Germany. Historian Mary Elise Sarotte, however, has argued that the precise timing of the opening owed much to bureaucratic confusion: according to this view, a poorly prepared announcement by East German official Günter Schabowski, who mistakenly stated that new travel rules took effect "immediately," prompted crowds to gather at the border crossings that very night, before the government had any plan for how the rules would actually be carried out.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the view about the timing of the Wall's opening described in the text?
options: Internal East German documents show that the travel regulations had been scheduled to begin the following morning, with border guards receiving no instructions about them before crowds appeared at the checkpoints.

Internal East German documents show that the number of protesters in Leipzig had grown steadily during the weeks before November 9, with officials expressing alarm about the size of the demonstrations.

Internal East German documents show that Schabowski had been given the text of the new travel regulations only shortly before his press conference, though he read it aloud exactly as it had been written.
Internal East German documents show that the government had spent months preparing detailed procedures for processing exit visas, which border guards began applying on the evening of November 9.
problem.explanation: 이 견해의 핵심은 샤보프스키의 잘못된 '즉시' 발표 때문에 정부가 실행 계획을 세우기 전에 군중이 국경에 모였다는 것이다. A는 규정이 원래 다음 날 아침부터 시행될 예정이었고 경비병이 지침을 받지 못했다고 보여 주므로, 발표 실수와 계획 부재를 모두 뒷받침한다. B는 시위대의 영향력을 강조하는 대중적 설명에 더 가깝다. C는 준비가 부족했음을 보여 주지만, 발표문을 그대로 읽었다면 '실수'라는 핵심 요소가 약해진다. D는 정부가 철저히 준비했다는 내용이라 오히려 이 견해를 약화한다.
problem.explanationEn: The view claims two things: Schabowski made a mistake when he said the rules took effect "immediately," and crowds showed up before the government had any plan for carrying the rules out. Choice A backs up both points. The rules were really meant to start the next morning, so "immediately" was an error, and the guards had no instructions, so there was no plan. Choice B is about protest crowds, which fits the popular account instead. Choice C does show poor preparation, but if Schabowski read the text exactly as written, he made no mistake, and that is the core of the claim. Choice D describes careful planning, so it would actually weaken the view.

advisory.note: A는 '즉시'라는 발표 실수와 계획 부재를 함께 뒷받침한다. C는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가진 매력적 오답이다. B는 대중적 설명 쪽이고 D는 견해를 약화하는 선택지다. 역사적 사실(다음 날 시행 예정, 경비병 지침 없음)과도 맞는다. 다만 오답 중 비교가 필요한 것이 사실상 C 하나뿐이어서 medium 기준의 '최소 2개'에는 다소 못 미칠 수 있다. 그래도 전체적으로 medium 수준에 맞는다고 본다.

problem.passage:
Many European observers in the mid-nineteenth century treated the Ottoman Tanzimat reforms (1839–1876) as proof that the sultan was losing control of his empire, since the reforms brought new provincial councils and legal guarantees for subjects. Historian Ali Yaycıoğlu and others have challenged this reading. They argue that the reforms were not a dilution of imperial authority but rather its ______: by replacing semi-independent tax farmers with salaried officials who answered to Istanbul, and by putting provincial courts under codified imperial law, the reformers pulled power that had long been spread among local notables back toward the center.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Many European observers in the mid-nineteenth century treated the Ottoman Tanzimat reforms (1839–1876) as proof that the sultan was losing control of his empire, since the reforms brought new provincial councils and legal guarantees for subjects. Historian Ali Yaycıoğlu and others have challenged this reading. They argue that the reforms were not a dilution of imperial authority but rather its ______: by replacing semi-independent tax farmers with salaried officials who answered to Istanbul, and by putting provincial courts under codified imperial law, the reformers pulled power that had long been spread among local notables back toward the center.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation:
정답 C(consolidation, 강화·통합). 'not A but rather B' 구조라서 빈칸에는 부정된 '권위의 희석(dilution)'과 반대되는 말이 와야 한다. 콜론 뒤의 근거도 이를 뒷받침한다. 징세청부인을 이스탄불에 보고하는 봉급 관리로 바꾸고, 지방 법원을 성문화된 제국법 아래 두어 흩어져 있던 권력을 중앙으로 다시 모았다고 했으므로 '권위의 강화·통합'이 맞다.
A(attenuation, 약화): 부정어 not을 무시하고 dilution과 같은 뜻의 단어를 고른 경우다. 지문이 부정한 해석을 그대로 되풀이한다.
B(decentralization, 분권화): 부정을 한 번 더 뒤집어 읽은 오류다. 지문 앞부분의 '지방 의회'에 이끌리면 고르기 쉽지만, 권력이 중앙으로 다시 모였다는 근거와 정면으로 충돌한다.
D(consolation, 위로): 철자와 발음이 정답과 비슷할 뿐 대조 구조와 아무 관련이 없다. '권위의 위로'라는 표현은 말이 되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn:
Choice C is correct. The "not A but rather B" structure means the blank must be the opposite of the rejected idea, a "dilution" of imperial authority. The evidence after the colon supports this. Tax farmers were replaced with salaried officials who answered to Istanbul, and provincial courts were put under imperial law. Both changes pulled scattered power "back toward the center," which is a consolidation of authority.
Choice A ("attenuation") ignores the word "not." It means about the same thing as "dilution," so it repeats the very reading the historians reject.
Choice B ("decentralization") flips the meaning back again. The earlier mention of provincial councils might pull you toward it, but it contradicts the evidence that power moved to the center.
Choice D ("consolation") only looks and sounds like "consolidation." It has nothing to do with the contrast, and "its consolation" makes no sense when applied to authority.

hardJudge.note: 'not a dilution ... but rather its ______' 구조와 콜론 뒤 중앙집권화 근거(징세청부인→봉급 관리, 성문 제국법)가 consolidation을 명확히 지지. 유럽 관찰자의 통념(통제력 상실)을 역사학자가 뒤집는 논리 구조를 파악해야 하므로 hard 적합. 오답 설계: A는 dilution 동의어(부정 무시), B는 지방 의회라는 표면 단서에 끌리는 분권화(극성 재역전), D는 철자 유사어. Tanzimat 연대·세제 개혁 내용은 사실과 부합. 체크리스트 4의 B 설명('이중 역전')은 표현이 다소 느슨하나 기능상 충족.

advisory.note: 'not A but rather B' 구조가 한 문장 안에 바로 드러나 있어 극성 판단이 쉽다. 콜론 뒤의 근거도 정답을 직접 확인해 준다. 따라서 전형적인 medium 수준이다. A와 B는 둘 다 부정된 개념과 같은 극성의 오답이고, 극성을 이중으로 뒤집은 오답은 사실상 없다. D는 철자만 비슷한 오답이다.

problem.passage:
Medieval chroniclers such as Thomas Walsingham described the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 as a sudden outburst of rage: a crowd with no real leaders, angered by a third poll tax, that followed Wat Tyler toward London. Many later historians repeated this picture and focused on the burned manors and the royal officials who were killed. Yet this account ______ what the rebels actually demanded at Mile End and Smithfield: an end to serfdom, an end to forced labor for lords, and land rents fixed at fourpence an acre. These were demands of a coherent challenge to the feudal order, not just fury.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: Medieval chroniclers such as Thomas Walsingham described the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 as a sudden outburst of rage: a crowd with no real leaders, angered by a third poll tax, that followed Wat Tyler toward London. Many later historians repeated this picture and focused on the burned manors and the royal officials who were killed. Yet this account ______ what the rebels actually demanded at Mile End and Smithfield: an end to serfdom, an end to forced labor for lords, and land rents fixed at fourpence an acre. These were demands of a coherent challenge to the feudal order, not just fury.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation:
지문은 두 단계로 되어 있다. 앞부분은 연대기 작가와 후대 역사가들이 반란을 '분노의 폭발'로 그린 기존 서술을 소개하고, 'Yet'부터는 저자가 이를 반박한다. 빈칸 뒤에는 농노제 폐지, 강제 노역 폐지, 지대 고정 같은 구체적인 요구가 나오고, 이를 근거로 반란이 '단순한 분노'가 아니었다고 결론짓는다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기존 서술이 이 요구들을 '가려 버린다'는 비판이 들어가야 하므로 D 'obscures'가 정답이다.
A 'documents'(기록하다)는 앞 단계의 묘사에 어울리는 단어이다. 하지만 기존 서술이 요구를 기록했다면 저자가 반박할 이유가 없어진다.
B 'concerns'(~에 관한 것이다)는 중립적인 단어라서 'Yet'이 요구하는 반박의 기능을 하지 못한다.
C 'dismissive of'는 '무시하는'이라는 비슷한 뜻을 담고 있지만 형용사구이다. 주어 'this account' 뒤에는 동사가 와야 하므로 문법적으로 들어갈 수 없다.
problem.explanationEn:
The text has two stages. First, it presents the traditional view of chroniclers and later historians, who described the revolt as an outburst of rage. Then, starting with "Yet," the author pushes back against that view. After the blank, the author lists the rebels' specific demands (an end to serfdom, an end to forced labor, fixed rents) and uses them to argue that the revolt was more than fury. So the blank needs a verb showing that the traditional account hides these demands. That makes "obscures" (D) the answer.
(A) "Documents" fits the first, descriptive stage. But if the account recorded the demands, the author would have no reason to object.
(B) "Concerns" is neutral and doesn't do the critical work that "Yet" calls for.
(C) "Dismissive of" has a similar meaning, but it's an adjective phrase. The subject "this account" needs a verb after it, so this choice doesn't work grammatically.

hardJudge.note: 지문은 '연대기·후대 역사가의 분노 폭발 서술' → 'Yet' 이후 저자의 반박(구체적 요구 제시, 'not just fury')이라는 두 단계가 뚜렷하고, 빈칸은 반박 단계의 첫 문장 동사 자리에 있다. 'obscures'는 기존 서술이 실제 요구를 가렸다는 반박 기능에 정확히 부합하며, 마지막 문장 'coherent challenge... not just fury'가 이를 확정한다. 오답 구성도 레시피대로다: 'documents'는 첫 단계(묘사·기록)에 어울리는 표면적 유사 어휘로 관계 방향이 반대이고, 'dismissive of'는 의미는 근접하나 형용사구라 주어 뒤 동사 자리에 올 수 없으며, 'concerns'는 중립어로 'Yet'의 대조 기능을 수행하지 못한다. 역사적 사실(Walsingham, 제3차 인두세, Mile End·Smithfield 요구, 에이커당 4펜스 지대)도 정확하다. 단순 어휘 매칭이 아니라 'Yet'에 의한 관계 역전과 서술 단계 구분을 요구하므로 hard 적합. 미세한 점: 'a crowd with no real leaders'와 'followed Wat Tyler'가 다소 긴장되나 당대 연대기의 '폭도' 묘사로 수용 가능.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 맞다. 'Yet'으로 시작하는 반박 다음에, 기존 서술이 반란자들의 구체적 요구를 가린다는 의미가 자연스럽게 이어진다. C는 형용사구라 동사 자리에 들어갈 수 없어 문법적으로 탈락한다. 역사적 사실(Walsingham, 세 번째 인두세, Mile End/Smithfield에서의 요구, 에이커당 4펜스 지대)에도 오류가 없다. 다만 'Yet'이라는 명시적 대조 신호와 빈칸 뒤의 근거만으로 답이 바로 정해진다. 오답 중 C는 문법으로, B는 중립성 때문에 쉽게 제거되므로 전형적인 medium 수준이다. 관계 역전이나 다중 증거 종합을 진짜로 요구하지 않아 hard 변별력이 부족하다.

problem.passage:
In the 1790s, the United States paid tribute to the Barbary states of North Africa so that pirates would not seize American merchant ships. Thomas Jefferson, unlike many members of Congress, who considered the payments cheap insurance, had condemned the practice since the 1780s. When he became president in 1801 and Tripoli demanded more money, he sent warships to the Mediterranean instead. ______ his decision continued a position he had long held rather than marking a change of heart.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: In the 1790s, the United States paid tribute to the Barbary states of North Africa so that pirates would not seize American merchant ships. Thomas Jefferson, unlike many members of Congress, who considered the payments cheap insurance, had condemned the practice since the 1780s. When he became president in 1801 and Tripoli demanded more money, he sent warships to the Mediterranean instead. ______ his decision continued a position he had long held rather than marking a change of heart.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: "had condemned the practice since the 1780s"의 주어는 바로 옆 명사 Congress가 아니라 문장 앞의 Jefferson이다. 'unlike many members of Congress' 삽입구는 Jefferson과 의회를 대비하는 말이다. 따라서 Jefferson은 오래전부터 공납에 반대해 왔고, 1801년 함대를 보낸 결정은 그 입장을 이어간 것이므로 결론을 이끄는 "Thus,"가 맞다. A "Surprisingly,"는 공납을 값싼 보험으로 여긴 쪽(의회)의 견해를 Jefferson의 견해로 잘못 본 선택이다. 그렇게 읽으면 함대 파견이 뜻밖의 방향 전환처럼 보인다. B "In contrast,"는 앞 문장에 대비 표현(unlike)이 있어 문법적으로는 자연스러워 보인다. 하지만 마지막 문장은 앞 내용과 대조되지 않고 앞 내용에서 따라 나오는 결론이므로 틀리다. D "Even so,"는 지시 대상을 Tripoli의 추가 요구라는 전혀 다른 요소로 잡은 선택이다. 그 요구에도 '불구하고'라는 양보 관계를 만들지만, 지문에는 그런 양보 관계가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "had condemned the practice since the 1780s" belongs to Jefferson, the subject at the start of the sentence. It does not describe Congress, the noun right next to it. The phrase "unlike many members of Congress" sets Jefferson against Congress. So Jefferson had opposed tribute for a long time, and sending warships in 1801 carried that view forward. The last sentence is a conclusion drawn from these facts, so "Thus," is correct. A ("Surprisingly,") gives Jefferson the view of the nearby noun, Congress, which saw tribute as cheap insurance. Read that way, the warships would look like an unexpected reversal. B ("In contrast,") sounds natural because the sentence before it uses "unlike." But the final sentence agrees with what comes before it and does not contrast with it. D ("Even so,") links the final sentence to a different element, Tripoli's demand. That creates a "despite this" relationship that the passage doesn't support.

hardJudge.note: "had condemned"의 주어가 삽입구(unlike many members of Congress, who considered...) 너머의 Jefferson임을 추적해야 마지막 문장이 '결론'임을 알 수 있고, Thus가 유일하게 성립. A는 의회 견해를 Jefferson 견해로 오독한 경우, B는 앞 문장의 unlike에 끌린 표면적 대조, D는 Tripoli 요구를 지시 대상으로 잘못 잡은 양보. 역사적 사실(1790년대 공납, Jefferson의 1780년대 반대, 1801년 함대 파견) 모두 정확. 두 번째 문장은 중첩 삽입구로 다소 길지만 설계상 필요한 구조이며 전체 지문은 간결함.

advisory.note: 삽입구(unlike ... Congress, who ...)를 사이에 두고 떨어져 있는 주어 Jefferson을 찾아야 정답 Thus를 고를 수 있다. A는 의회의 견해를 Jefferson의 것으로 읽은 경우를 노린 오답이고, B는 unlike에 끌린 문법적으로만 자연스러운 오답이다. 역사적 사실(바르바리 공납, 1801년 함대 파견, Jefferson의 반대 입장)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
Historians of the Scottish Enlightenment (roughly 1707–1790) often contrast its thinkers with continental rationalists, who tried to derive knowledge from first principles through reasoning alone. One historian goes further and proposes a graded relationship: the more heavily a moral philosopher grounded arguments in recorded observation of actual human conduct, the more readily that philosopher treated conclusions as provisional and open to change when new cases emerged. To test this, the historian compares surviving lecture notes from two eighteenth-century Edinburgh professors. The first professor's notes are filled with detailed accounts of merchants' bargaining, parish disputes, and travelers' reports, while the second professor's notes proceed almost entirely by deduction from a few stated axioms. If the historian's proposal is correct, then a comparison of successive versions of each professor's lectures over several decades should reveal that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Historians of the Scottish Enlightenment (roughly 1707–1790) often contrast its thinkers with continental rationalists, who tried to derive knowledge from first principles through reasoning alone. One historian goes further and proposes a graded relationship: the more heavily a moral philosopher grounded arguments in recorded observation of actual human conduct, the more readily that philosopher treated conclusions as provisional and open to change when new cases emerged. To test this, the historian compares surviving lecture notes from two eighteenth-century Edinburgh professors. The first professor's notes are filled with detailed accounts of merchants' bargaining, parish disputes, and travelers' reports, while the second professor's notes proceed almost entirely by deduction from a few stated axioms. If the historian's proposal is correct, then a comparison of successive versions of each professor's lectures over several decades should reveal that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the second professor's conclusions changed more often from one version to the next than the first professor's conclusions did.
the first professor's habit of frequently changing conclusions was what led that professor to start filling the notes with recorded observations.
the professor whose university received more funding from Edinburgh's merchant community changed conclusions more often between versions.
the first professor's conclusions changed more often from one version to the next than the second professor's conclusions did.
problem.explanation: 이 역사가의 가설은 관찰에 더 많이 의존할수록 결론을 잠정적인 것으로 보고 더 쉽게 고친다는 것이다. 관찰 기록이 풍부한 사람은 첫 번째 교수이므로, 강의 판본이 바뀔 때마다 결론이 더 자주 달라지는 쪽도 첫 번째 교수여야 한다. 그래서 정답은 D이다. A는 관계의 방향을 뒤집어 연역 위주인 두 번째 교수가 더 자주 바꾼다고 말한다. B는 원인과 결과를 바꾸었다. 가설에서는 관찰 의존이 원인이고 결론 수정이 결과인데, B는 결론 수정이 관찰을 낳았다고 한다. 게다가 B는 두 교수를 비교하지도 않는다. C는 상인 공동체의 재정 지원이라는 이 이론과 무관한 요인을 결론으로 내세운다. 지문에는 이 요인에 대한 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The historian's claim is that the more a philosopher relies on recorded observation, the more readily that philosopher treats conclusions as provisional and revises them. The first professor relies heavily on observation, so the first professor should show more changes across versions. That makes D correct. A reverses the direction of the relationship by giving the deductive professor more revisions. B swaps cause and effect: in the theory, relying on observation is the cause and revising is the effect, but B says revising caused the observing. B also doesn't compare the two professors. C points to an outside factor, merchant funding, which the theory never mentions and the text gives no support for.

hardJudge.note: 이론(관찰 의존↑ → 결론의 잠정성↑)을 두 교수 사례에 매핑해 '강의 판본 간 결론 변경 빈도'라는 새로운 관측 가능 지표로 변환해야 하는 2단계 적용 과제. 정답 D는 방향을 유지하고, A는 방향 반전, B는 인과 역전(+비교 부재), C는 무관 요인으로 오답 설계가 체크리스트에 부합. 해설은 정답과 오답 사유를 정확히 서술하며 모순 없음. 역사적 배경(1707–1790, 대륙 합리론 대비)은 통상적 서술이며 교수는 가상 인물로 사실 오류 없음. 다만 첫 교수=관찰형이 매우 명시적이어서 난이도는 hard 중 하위권.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 맞다. 다만 적용 과정이 한 단계에 불과하다(관찰이 많은 쪽이 첫 번째 교수이므로 결론을 더 자주 바꾸는 쪽도 첫 번째 교수). A와 D는 거울상이고 B와 C는 쉽게 배제된다. 어려움은 어휘와 길이에서만 오며, 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Historians have long described the Tokugawa shogunate's sakoku policies (1633–1853) as a near-total closure of Japan. Some scholars, however, argue that the restrictions were less about shutting out foreign goods than about controlling who profited from them: by confining Dutch and Chinese trade to Nagasaki under direct shogunal supervision, the regime kept wealthy regional lords (daimyo) from building independent commercial ties that could fund challenges to central authority. If this argument is correct, then the strongest support for it would come from evidence showing that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Historians have long described the Tokugawa shogunate's sakoku policies (1633–1853) as a near-total closure of Japan. Some scholars, however, argue that the restrictions were less about shutting out foreign goods than about controlling who profited from them: by confining Dutch and Chinese trade to Nagasaki under direct shogunal supervision, the regime kept wealthy regional lords (daimyo) from building independent commercial ties that could fund challenges to central authority. If this argument is correct, then the strongest support for it would come from evidence showing that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: imported Chinese silk and medicinal herbs continued to be sold in Edo markets throughout the period, often at prices well above those of domestic equivalents.
daimyo whose domains lay near Nagasaki were barred from trading directly with Dutch or Chinese merchants, while the shogunate's own officials set prices and collected the proceeds.
the number of Dutch ships allowed to dock at Nagasaki each year was gradually reduced, which lowered the total volume of foreign goods reaching Japan.
Japanese scholars of 'Dutch learning' (rangaku) studied European medicine and astronomy from books obtained through the Nagasaki trade.
problem.explanation: 이 가설의 핵심은 무역 제한의 목적이 외국 물품 차단이 아니라 이익의 통제, 즉 다이묘가 독자적인 무역 관계를 맺지 못하게 하고 수익을 막부가 갖는 데 있었다는 것이다. B는 나가사키 인근 다이묘까지 직접 거래를 금지당했고 가격 결정과 수익 징수는 막부 관리가 맡았다는 내용이다. 가설의 두 조건(다이묘 배제, 중앙의 이익 독점)을 모두 직접 충족하므로 정답이다. A: 외국 물품이 계속 유통되었다는 사실은 '완전 폐쇄'가 아니었다는 점만 보여 준다. 누가 이익을 얻었는지는 말해 주지 않으므로 겉으로만 관련 있어 보이는 사실이다. C: 무역량이 줄었다는 것은 물품 자체를 차단했다는 전통적 해석 쪽을 가리킨다. 가설과 반대 방향으로 작용하는 사실을 지지 근거처럼 제시한 오답이다. D: 난학(蘭學)은 무역의 문화적 배경 정보일 뿐, 이익을 누가 통제했는지와는 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis says the main goal of the restrictions was to control who profited from foreign trade, not to keep foreign goods out. Under this view, the shogunate kept regional lords (daimyo) from forming their own trade ties and kept the profits for itself. Choice B shows both parts directly: even daimyo near Nagasaki were barred from trading with foreigners, and shogunal officials set the prices and collected the proceeds. That makes B the correct answer. Choice A only shows that foreign goods still reached Japan. It says nothing about who controlled the profits, so it's related on the surface but doesn't test the claim. Choice C, a falling trade volume, fits the traditional "keep goods out" reading better, so it actually works against the hypothesis even though it's worded like support. Choice D is cultural background about Dutch learning and has nothing to do with control of trade profits.

hardJudge.note: 가설이 '물품 차단이 아님'과 '이익 통제(다이묘 배제·막부 독점)'의 두 요소로 구성되어 있고, A가 전자만 부분적으로 충족하는 매력적 오답으로 기능하므로 수험생은 가설의 핵심 조건을 분해해 어느 증거가 가장 강한지 판별해야 함. B는 두 조건을 직접 충족해 정답으로 타당. C는 전통적 '폐쇄' 해석 쪽으로 작용하는 반대 방향 사실, D는 무관한 문화적 배경. 연도(1633–1853)와 나가사키의 막부 직할 무역 구조 등 사실관계도 문제 없음. 질문 문두 "If this argument is correct, then the strongest support..."가 다소 어색하지만 SAT 완성형 틀 내에서 허용 가능.

advisory.note: B만 다이묘 배제와 막부의 이익 통제를 함께 다룬다. A는 그럴듯하지만 무관하고(유통만 보여줌), C는 반대 방향(물품 차단)이며, D는 무관하다. 지지 증거를 따지는 정도는 보통보다 어렵지만, B가 가설의 표현을 거의 그대로 반영해 다소 쉬운 편이다.

problem.passage:
Maroon communities were settlements founded by people who escaped slavery in the Americas between the 1500s and the 1800s. Historians studying one maroon community in the mountains of Jamaica have found that its founders chose a site surrounded by steep cliffs and thick forest, reachable only by a single narrow trail. Colonial soldiers sent to recapture the residents could approach only in a slow single-file line, which made them easy to spot from far away. Because of these features, historians conclude that the founders most likely picked the location in order to ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Maroon communities were settlements founded by people who escaped slavery in the Americas between the 1500s and the 1800s. Historians studying one maroon community in the mountains of Jamaica have found that its founders chose a site surrounded by steep cliffs and thick forest, reachable only by a single narrow trail. Colonial soldiers sent to recapture the residents could approach only in a slow single-file line, which made them easy to spot from far away. Because of these features, historians conclude that the founders most likely picked the location in order to ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: make it easier to trade crops with nearby colonial towns.
make it easier to grow large plantations of sugarcane.
make it easier to defend themselves against attackers.
make it easier to welcome visitors arriving by sea.
problem.explanation: 지문은 가파른 절벽, 울창한 숲, 좁은 길 하나 때문에 병사들이 한 줄로 천천히 다가와야 했고 멀리서도 쉽게 보였다고 설명한다. 이런 특징은 모두 공격을 막는 데 유리하므로, 정착지는 방어를 위해 선택되었다는 C가 정답이다. A는 고립된 지형이 이웃 마을과의 교역을 오히려 어렵게 만드므로 틀렸다. B는 절벽과 숲이 대규모 농장에 맞지 않고 지문에 농업 이야기가 없으므로 틀렸다. D는 산속 지형이 바다로 오는 방문객과 관련이 없고, 지문은 사람들을 막는 것에 초점을 두므로 틀렸다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the site had steep cliffs, thick forest, and only one narrow trail, so soldiers had to come slowly in single file and could be spotted from far away. All of these features help people protect themselves, so C is correct: the founders picked the site for defense. A is wrong because an isolated site would make trade with colonial towns harder, not easier. B is wrong because cliffs and forest don't suit large plantations, and the passage never mentions farming. D is wrong because a mountain site has nothing to do with visitors arriving by sea, and the passage is about keeping people out.

quality.seed: history and civics — African diaspora slave trade resistance 1518-1865 and maroon settlements established by escaped enslaved peoples

hardJudge.note: 지문의 단서(절벽·숲·단일 좁은 길·단열 접근·원거리 식별)가 모두 방어 이점을 직접 가리키므로 C가 유일하게 논리적으로 완성됨. 오답 A·B·D는 각각 교역·농업·해상 접근이라는 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯하되 지문의 고립·산악 지형 단서에 의해 즉시 배제됨. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 역사적 배경(자메이카 마룬, 산악 요새 입지) 사실관계 문제 없음. 추론 한 단계, 어휘 평이 — easy 적합.

advisory.note: 단서가 직접 드러나 있고 추론은 한 단계뿐이다. 오답들은 쉽게 배제되지만 지나치게 엉뚱하지는 않다. B는 카리브해 지역의 사탕수수 맥락 때문에 어느 정도 그럴듯하게 보인다. 사소한 점: A의 'crops'는 B의 농업 주제와 겹치지만 문제는 되지 않는다.

problem.passage:
In 1610, Galileo Galilei pointed his telescope at Jupiter and saw four small moons circling the planet. At the time, the Catholic Church supported the traditional view that every object in the heavens moves around Earth. Galileo's observation was important because it showed something that this view said could not happen: objects in the sky orbiting a body other than Earth. Therefore, the moons of Jupiter suggested that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In 1610, Galileo Galilei pointed his telescope at Jupiter and saw four small moons circling the planet. At the time, the Catholic Church supported the traditional view that every object in the heavens moves around Earth. Galileo's observation was important because it showed something that this view said could not happen: objects in the sky orbiting a body other than Earth. Therefore, the moons of Jupiter suggested that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: Earth must be the only planet in the solar system that has moons of its own.
Jupiter must be located much closer to Earth than astronomers had once believed.
the telescope must have been too weak to show the heavens as they really are.
Earth might not be the center around which all heavenly bodies move.
problem.explanation: 지문은 교회가 지지한 전통적 견해가 '모든 천체는 지구 주위를 돈다'는 것이었고, 목성의 위성은 지구가 아닌 다른 천체를 도는 물체였다고 말한다. 따라서 이 관측은 지구가 모든 천체 운동의 중심이 아닐 수 있음을 시사하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 목성에도 위성이 있다는 관측 내용과 정면으로 모순된다. B는 거리에 관한 내용으로, 지문은 목성까지의 거리를 전혀 언급하지 않는다. C는 관측을 신뢰하지 않는 결론인데, 지문은 이 관측을 전통적 견해에 맞선 중요한 증거로 제시한다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the traditional view held that every heavenly object moves around Earth, but Jupiter's moons were objects orbiting something other than Earth. So the observation suggests that Earth might not be the center of all heavenly motion, which makes D correct. A contradicts the observation itself, since Jupiter was seen to have moons. B is about distance, and the passage never discusses how far away Jupiter is. C throws out the observation, but the passage treats it as important evidence against the traditional view.

quality.seed: history and civics — Scientific Revolution telescopic observations 1610-1687 and heliocentric model challenging Catholic Church astronomical doctrine

hardJudge.note: 지문이 '전통 견해: 모든 천체가 지구를 돈다' → '목성 위성은 지구 아닌 천체를 돈다'를 직접 제시하므로 D가 한 단계 추론으로 도출된다. A는 관측과 정면 모순, B는 거리 미언급, C는 지문이 관측을 '중요한 증거'로 다루는 것과 충돌하여 규칙을 알면 바로 배제되지만 그럴듯한 오개념이다. 역사적 사실(1610년 갈릴레오의 목성 위성 관측, 지구중심설 지지)도 정확. 한·영 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: 추론이 한 단계이고 단서가 지문에 직접 드러난다. 다만 오답 A와 C는 꽤 쉽게 배제된다. 사실 관계는 정확하다(1610년 갈릴레이 위성 관측).

problem.passage:
From the late fourteenth century onward, the Ottoman state filled the ranks of its elite Janissary infantry through the devshirme, a system that took boys from Christian families in the Balkans, converted them to Islam, and trained them as soldiers. Because these recruits were separated from their birth families and were legally considered servants of the sultan, they had no local family ties or inherited estates to draw their loyalty elsewhere. Historians therefore argue that the sultans valued the devshirme largely because it ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: From the late fourteenth century onward, the Ottoman state filled the ranks of its elite Janissary infantry through the devshirme, a system that took boys from Christian families in the Balkans, converted them to Islam, and trained them as soldiers. Because these recruits were separated from their birth families and were legally considered servants of the sultan, they had no local family ties or inherited estates to draw their loyalty elsewhere. Historians therefore argue that the sultans valued the devshirme largely because it ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: produced soldiers whose allegiance was owed to the ruler rather than to any rival power base.
produced soldiers who remained closely connected to the villages where they had been born.
produced soldiers who could pass their military positions and lands on to their own sons.
produced soldiers who were recruited mainly from established Muslim noble families.
problem.explanation: 지문은 신병들이 가족과 분리되었고 술탄의 종으로 간주되어 충성심을 다른 곳으로 돌릴 가족 유대나 상속 재산이 없었다고 말한다. 따라서 술탄이 이 제도를 중시한 이유는 통치자에게만 충성하는 병사를 얻었기 때문이라는 A가 논리적이다. B는 출신 마을과의 분리라는 진술과 모순된다. C는 상속 재산이 없었다는 점과 어긋나며, D는 기독교 가정 출신이라는 사실과 모순된다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says the recruits were cut off from their families and counted as the sultan's servants, so they had no family ties or inherited estates to pull their loyalty elsewhere. That means the sultans would value the system because it gave them soldiers loyal only to the ruler, which is choice A. Choice B is wrong because the boys were separated from their home communities. Choice C is wrong because the recruits had no inherited estates, and choice D is wrong because they came from Christian families, not Muslim noble ones.

quality.seed: history and civics — Janissary corps Ottoman military institution 1363-1826 and devshirme recruitment system converting Christian boys into elite soldiers

hardJudge.note: 지문의 "no local family ties or inherited estates to draw their loyalty elsewhere"가 A를 직접 뒷받침하며, B·C·D는 각각 지문의 명시적 진술(가족과 분리, 상속 재산 없음, 기독교 가정 출신)과 직접 모순되어 규칙을 알면 바로 배제된다. 데브시르메에 대한 역사적 서술도 정확하다. 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 원문 지문으로 보이며 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 단서가 직접 드러나 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답 B·C·D는 각각 지문 진술과 바로 모순되며, 데브시르메 제도를 모르는 학생에게는 그럴듯해 보인다. 다만 C는 '상속 재산이 없었다'는 진술을 근거로 배제되는 것으로, 엄밀히 말하면 상속 금지가 명시된 것은 아니지만 easy 수준에서는 무리가 없다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Historians tracing the spread of democratic revolutions after 1776 often credit the Declaration of Independence as their spark. Its claim that all people possess unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, this view holds, gave reformers from Paris to Caracas a universal principle to invoke, and the document's influence can therefore be measured by how often later revolutionaries quoted or echoed its language.

Text 2
Historian David Armitage, examining foreign printings of the Declaration, notes that readers abroad were drawn less to its opening philosophy of rights than to its closing assertion that the colonies were "Free and Independent States." For many later movements, the document served chiefly as a model of how a people might announce sovereignty to other nations, a template copied in dozens of independence declarations that said little about individual rights.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the method of gauging influence described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Historians tracing the spread of democratic revolutions after 1776 often credit the Declaration of Independence as their spark. Its claim that all people possess unalienable rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, this view holds, gave reformers from Paris to Caracas a universal principle to invoke, and the document's influence can therefore be measured by how often later revolutionaries quoted or echoed its language.

Text 2
Historian David Armitage, examining foreign printings of the Declaration, notes that readers abroad were drawn less to its opening philosophy of rights than to its closing assertion that the colonies were "Free and Independent States." For many later movements, the document served chiefly as a model of how a people might announce sovereignty to other nations, a template copied in dozens of independence declarations that said little about individual rights.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the method of gauging influence described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that counting echoes of the Declaration's rights language is the most reliable way to show that natural rights philosophy inspired revolutions from Paris to Caracas
By cautioning that tracking only echoes of the rights passage would miss the document's widest influence, which came through imitation of its announcement of statehood
By insisting that later declarations of independence were copied from the Declaration and therefore said little about individual rights
By arguing that the Declaration's influence abroad was weakened because foreign translations often distorted the meaning of its original wording
problem.explanation: 정답 B: Text 2는 해외 독자들이 권리 철학보다 '독립국가' 선언 부분에 주목했고, 주권 선언의 틀로 모방되었다고 본다. 이 전제에서 보면 Text 1처럼 권리 문구의 인용 빈도로 영향력을 재는 방법은 가장 널리 퍼진 영향 경로(주권 선언 형식의 모방)를 놓친다. A: Text 1의 주장을 그대로 반복할 뿐이고 Text 2의 관점과 충돌한다. C: Text 2의 결론을 되풀이할 뿐 Text 1의 측정 방법에 대한 반응이 아니다. D: 번역의 왜곡은 Text 2가 다루지 않은 쟁점이며, Text 2는 영향력이 약했다고 말하지도 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: B is correct. Text 2 says readers abroad cared less about the Declaration's rights philosophy than about its claim to statehood, and that later movements copied it as a way to announce sovereignty. From that starting point, measuring influence only by echoes of the rights language would miss the main way the document spread, so the author of Text 2 would warn that Text 1's method leaves things out. A just repeats Text 1's view, which Text 2's evidence undercuts. C restates Text 2's own conclusion without responding to how Text 1 measures influence. D brings in distorted translations, which Text 2 never mentions, and it wrongly says the document's influence was weakened.

hardJudge.note: Text 2(Armitage: 해외 독자는 권리 철학보다 '자유롭고 독립된 국가' 선언에 주목, 주권 선언 템플릿으로 모방됨)의 전제를 유지한 채 Text 1의 측정법(권리 문구 인용 빈도)을 평가해야 B가 도출된다. Text 2는 측정법 자체를 언급하지 않으므로 반응을 스스로 추론해야 함. A는 Text 1 반복, C는 Text 2 내용을 되풀이하되 인과를 왜곡하고 측정법에 대한 반응이 아님, D는 번역 왜곡이라는 본문 외 쟁점. 'widest/chiefly' 강도도 Text 2의 'chiefly', 'dozens'와 부합. Armitage의 실제 논지(The Declaration of Independence: A Global History)와도 일치하며 사실 오류 없음.

advisory.note: Text 2는 Text 1의 측정 방법을 직접 언급하지 않으므로, 그 방법에 어떻게 반응할지는 독자가 스스로 추론해야 함. C는 Text 2의 내용을 인과관계(therefore)로 왜곡해 그럴듯한 함정 역할을 함. B의 'widest influence'는 'dozens', 'many later movements'로 뒷받침되나 강도가 약간 높은 편임. 전반적으로 hard의 하한선 수준.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Historians often describe the Trans-Siberian Railway, built between 1891 and 1916, as an engine of imperial expansion. Because Russian settlement in Siberia surged in the years after the line's sections opened, many scholars conclude that the railway itself drew millions of peasants eastward. On this view, the state's decision to link Moscow with Pacific ports such as Vladivostok was what turned Siberia into a settled frontier of the empire.

Text 2
Records of migration from European Russia show that the eastward flow of peasants had already begun to rise sharply in the 1880s, years before construction started. Many migrants traveled by river boat and cart, and surveys of new villages found that most families chose sites far from the tracks, near arable land that had been opened through the 1889 resettlement law and the expanded land allotments that followed. The railway clearly carried freight and officials, but its link to peasant settlement is less obvious.

Based on the texts, which part of the reasoning described in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Historians often describe the Trans-Siberian Railway, built between 1891 and 1916, as an engine of imperial expansion. Because Russian settlement in Siberia surged in the years after the line's sections opened, many scholars conclude that the railway itself drew millions of peasants eastward. On this view, the state's decision to link Moscow with Pacific ports such as Vladivostok was what turned Siberia into a settled frontier of the empire.

Text 2
Records of migration from European Russia show that the eastward flow of peasants had already begun to rise sharply in the 1880s, years before construction started. Many migrants traveled by river boat and cart, and surveys of new villages found that most families chose sites far from the tracks, near arable land that had been opened through the 1889 resettlement law and the expanded land allotments that followed. The railway clearly carried freight and officials, but its link to peasant settlement is less obvious.
problem.question: Based on the texts, which part of the reasoning described in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?
options: The claim that the railway turned Siberia into a settled frontier of the Russian Empire
The claim that the railway connected Moscow with Pacific ports such as Vladivostok
The claim that the timing of the settlement surge shows the railway caused it
The claim that Russian settlement in Siberia increased greatly around the time the line opened
problem.explanation:
정답 C: Text 1은 '노선 개통 이후 정착이 급증했다'는 시간적 순서를 근거로 철도가 이주를 일으켰다고 추론한다. Text 2는 이주 증가가 착공 전인 1880년대에 이미 시작됐고, 이주민은 강·마차로 이동해 철로와 먼 곳에 정착했으며 1889년 재정착법 등 다른 요인이 있었다고 제시해, 바로 이 '시기 일치=인과' 가정을 약화시킨다.
A: 결론 자체이다. Text 2는 철도의 역할을 '덜 분명하다'고 할 뿐 시베리아가 정착지가 되었다는 사실을 부정하지 않으며, 핵심 공격 대상은 결론이 기대는 추론 고리이다.
B: 부수적 세부이다. Text 2는 노선 경로를 문제 삼지 않고 오히려 철도가 화물과 관리를 실어 날랐다고 인정한다.
D: Text 2가 오히려 동의하는 부분이다. Text 2도 이주가 급격히 늘었다고 기록하며, 다만 그 시작 시점과 원인을 다르게 본다.
problem.explanationEn:
Correct answer, C: Text 1 reasons from timing. Settlement surged after sections of the line opened, so the railway must have caused it. Text 2 attacks that link directly. It shows the surge started in the 1880s, before construction began. It also notes that migrants traveled by river and cart, that they settled far from the tracks, and that other causes existed, such as the 1889 resettlement law.
A is wrong because it's the conclusion. Text 2 doesn't deny that Siberia became settled. It disputes the reasoning that credits the railway for it.
B is wrong because it's a side detail. Text 2 never questions the route, and it even agrees that the railway carried freight and officials.
D is wrong because Text 2 agrees with it. Text 2 also reports a sharp rise in migration. It only disagrees about when the rise began and what caused it.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 separates evidence(개통 후 정착 급증)와 결론(철도가 이주를 유발)을 'Because… conclude' 구조로 명확히 구분. Text 2는 1880년대 선행 증가, 철로와 먼 정착지, 1889 재정착법이라는 대안 원인으로 '시기 일치=인과' 가정(C)만 직접 공격하며, 이주 급증 자체(D)와 노선 경로(B)는 인정. A는 결론이라 끌리는 오답이나 Text 2가 'less obvious'로 유보적 표현을 써 결론 부정이 아닌 추론 고리 공격임이 판별 가능. 1889 재정착법, 1891–1916 건설 연대 등 사실 오류 없음. 해설은 선택지별 배제 근거가 본문과 일치. 사소한 점: A와 C 사이 경계가 약간 좁지만 'which part of the reasoning' 발문으로 C가 최적답임이 충분히 뒷받침됨.

advisory.note: C가 정답이다. Text 2의 1880년대 선행 증가, 철로와 떨어진 정착지, 1889년 법 같은 근거는 '시기 일치 = 인과'라는 가정을 직접 겨냥한다. D는 Text 2도 동의하는 부분(이주 급증)이고, B도 Text 2가 인정하는 부분이다. A는 Text 2의 'less obvious'라는 유보적 표현 때문에 매력적인 오답이 된다. 이 경우 결론보다 추론 고리를 공격한다는 점을 가려내야 해서 hard 수준의 사고가 필요하다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Historians who explain the Cherokee removal of 1838–1839 often credit a single cause, such as Andrew Jackson's personal hostility toward Native nations. In my view, an explanation of the Trail of Tears is persuasive only if it accounts for why removal happened when it did. Causes that existed for decades before 1830 cannot, by themselves, explain why forced displacement suddenly became federal policy in that particular decade.

Text 2
The roots of Cherokee removal lie in a settler hunger for land that stretched back to the colonial era. From the 1700s onward, white Americans steadily pressed westward, and each generation demanded more Cherokee territory. The Indian Removal Act of 1830 and the march west that followed were, in this sense, simply the culmination of a long-standing desire that had shaped frontier politics for nearly a century.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the explanation offered in Text 2?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Historians who explain the Cherokee removal of 1838–1839 often credit a single cause, such as Andrew Jackson's personal hostility toward Native nations. In my view, an explanation of the Trail of Tears is persuasive only if it accounts for why removal happened when it did. Causes that existed for decades before 1830 cannot, by themselves, explain why forced displacement suddenly became federal policy in that particular decade.

Text 2
The roots of Cherokee removal lie in a settler hunger for land that stretched back to the colonial era. From the 1700s onward, white Americans steadily pressed westward, and each generation demanded more Cherokee territory. The Indian Removal Act of 1830 and the march west that followed were, in this sense, simply the culmination of a long-standing desire that had shaped frontier politics for nearly a century.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely evaluate the explanation offered in Text 2?
options: As convincing, because tracing settler demand across several generations shows that the Removal Act grew out of deep and lasting pressures rather than one leader's attitudes
As partly convincing, because it avoids blaming a single individual, though it would be stronger if it also included Jackson's personal hostility as one of the causes
As convincing, because demand for land is widely recognized as the central force behind westward expansion and the conflicts it produced
As insufficient, because a desire that persisted for nearly a century does not by itself show why forced removal became federal policy in the 1830s
problem.explanation: Text 1 저자의 기준은 '왜 하필 그 시점에 일어났는가'를 설명해야 한다는 것이며, 1830년 이전 수십 년간 존재한 원인만으로는 부족하다고 명시한다. Text 2는 거의 한 세기 지속된 토지 욕구를 원인으로 제시하므로, 바로 그 기준에 미달한다(D). A는 Text 2 저자 자신의 기준(장기적 뿌리의 깊이)으로 평가한 것이다. B는 두 기준을 섞은 평가로, Text 1이 단일 원인론을 비판한 점만 취하고 시기 기준은 빠뜨린 채 오히려 잭슨 요인을 더하라고 한다. C는 '토지 욕구가 서부 팽창의 핵심'이라는 일반 상식에 기댄 평가로 Text 1의 기준과 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn:
Text 1's author sets a clear test: a good explanation of the Trail of Tears has to account for why removal happened when it did. The author also says that causes present for decades before 1830 can't explain the timing on their own. Text 2 points to land hunger that lasted nearly a century. That is exactly the kind of long-running cause Text 1 calls insufficient, so D is correct.
- A judges Text 2 by Text 2's own standard, which values deep, long-term roots.
- B mixes the two authors' standards. It picks up Text 1's criticism of single-cause explanations but drops the timing test, and it even suggests adding Jackson's hostility.
- C relies on common knowledge that land demand drove westward expansion, not on Text 1's stated test.

hardJudge.note: Text 1의 기준(시점 설명 요구, 수십 년 전부터 존재한 원인만으로는 불충분)이 명시되어 있고, Text 2의 '한 세기에 걸친 토지 욕구의 culmination' 설명은 그 기준에 직접 저촉되므로 D가 유일하게 Text 1 관점에서 도출된다. A는 Text 2 저자의 기준(장기적 뿌리), B는 단일 원인 비판만 취하고 시기 기준을 빠뜨린 혼합 평가, C는 외부 상식 기반. 다만 Text 1이 '단일 원인' 비판처럼 읽히는 첫 문장이 B의 매력도를 높이는데, 저자가 실제로 요구하는 것은 시점 설명이지 다원인이 아니므로 B는 명확한 오답. 역사적 사실(1830 Indian Removal Act, 1838–39 removal) 오류 없음. 해설은 정답을 정확히 뒷받침하고 오답 각각의 함정 구조도 일치.

advisory.note: Text 1이 기준("causes that existed for decades before 1830 cannot, by themselves...")을 거의 그대로 적어 두었고 D가 그 문구를 바꿔 말한 수준이라 추론할 거리가 적다. 오답 A·B·C도 Text 1의 시기 기준과 바로 충돌해 쉽게 걸러진다. 구조는 레시피에 맞지만 난이도는 전형적인 medium 수준이다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
