hardJudge.note: Text 2의 '포식률 차이 없음'이 Text 1의 위장 가설을 직접 반박하므로 D가 유일한 정답. A는 결과와 정반대, B는 지문에 없는 지역 구분, C는 두 지문 모두와 모순되나 규칙을 모르는 학생에겐 그럴듯한 전형적 오답. 한·영 해설 모두 결론과 글자 참조가 일치하고 한글 혼입 없음. Levey et al. 2004 연구를 원문 인용 없이 요약한 독창적 지문으로 저작권 우려 없음. 단서가 명시적이고 추론 한 단계라 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: Levey 외(2004, Nature) 연구 내용과 일치함. Text 2의 "no difference in predation rates"라는 단서 하나로 직접 풀린다. 오답 A·B·C도 전형적인 오개념이라 easy 난이도에 맞다. 다만 Text 2의 "placed dung at some owl burrows"라는 설정 때문에 C의 근거가 '올빼미가 배설물을 이용한다는 전제'로 다소 간접적인 점은 경미한 사항이다.

problem.passage:
Click beetles of the genus Pyrophorus carry a pair of glowing spots, called photophores, on the thorax. Some researchers have proposed that these photophores serve mainly to startle predators: a beetle seized by a predator suddenly brightens its glow, and the startled attacker loosens its grip. To test this idea, a team offered Pyrophorus beetles to captive toads in two conditions. In complete darkness, toads released glowing beetles far more often than they released beetles whose photophores had been painted over. Under bright artificial light, however, toads released glowing and painted beetles at about the same low rate, even though the glowing beetles still brightened their photophores when grabbed. These results suggest that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Click beetles of the genus Pyrophorus carry a pair of glowing spots, called photophores, on the thorax. Some researchers have proposed that these photophores serve mainly to startle predators: a beetle seized by a predator suddenly brightens its glow, and the startled attacker loosens its grip. To test this idea, a team offered Pyrophorus beetles to captive toads in two conditions. In complete darkness, toads released glowing beetles far more often than they released beetles whose photophores had been painted over. Under bright artificial light, however, toads released glowing and painted beetles at about the same low rate, even though the glowing beetles still brightened their photophores when grabbed. These results suggest that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the photophores protect beetles in any lighting condition, because the beetles brighten them whenever a predator grabs them.
toads are less likely to attack click beetles in darkness than in bright light, because the glow makes the beetles harder to find.
the photophores' defensive effect, if any, depends on the flash standing out against a dark background rather than on the flash itself.
painting over the photophores made the beetles less appealing to toads, so the toads released those beetles more often.
problem.explanation: 어둠 속에서는 빛나는 딱정벌레가 더 자주 풀려났지만, 밝은 조명 아래에서는 딱정벌레가 똑같이 빛을 밝혔는데도 차이가 없었다. 따라서 섬광 자체보다는 어두운 배경과의 대비가 방어 효과를 만든다는 결론, 즉 C가 정답이다. A는 섬광이 밝은 곳에서도 일어났다는 사실은 맞게 짚었지만, 밝은 곳에서는 효과가 없었다는 결과와 어긋난다. B는 공격 빈도를 다루는데, 실험이 측정한 것은 공격 빈도가 아니라 풀어 주는 비율이다. D는 칠한 딱정벌레가 더 자주 풀려났다고 하는데, 이는 실제 결과와 정반대다.
problem.explanationEn: In darkness, the glowing beetles were released much more often. Under bright light, they made no difference, even though the beetles still brightened their glow when grabbed. That pattern points to C: what matters is the contrast between the flash and a dark background, not the flash alone. A is right that the beetles flashed in bright light too, but it ignores the result that the flash didn't help them there. B is about how often toads attack, but the study measured how often toads let go, not attack rates. D gets the result backward, since the painted beetles were released less often, not more.

hardJudge.note: Correct answer verified: darkness → glowing beetles released more; bright light → no difference despite flashing, so the protective effect depends on contrast with a dark background (C). A is contradicted by the bright-light result; B concerns attack frequency, which was not measured; D reverses the darkness result. Explanations in both languages support C with consistent reasoning. Two-step inference (compare two conditions + note flash still occurred) fits medium; A and B have partial grounding, D is a plausible misread.

advisory.note: The answer requires comparing the two conditions (dark vs. bright light) and connecting that comparison to the fact that the beetles still flashed in bright light. That makes it a proper two-step inference. A uses a true detail but leads to the wrong conclusion, and B shifts from release rates to attack rates. Both are plausible distractors. D reverses the result, so it is easy to eliminate, but it still reads sensibly. The difficulty fits medium.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Poison dart frogs of the family Dendrobatidae carry potent alkaloids in their skin, yet captive-bred individuals raised on fruit flies and crickets are nearly toxin-free. Researchers have therefore concluded that the frogs make none of these compounds themselves; every alkaloid is acquired from wild prey such as ants and mites and simply stored, unchanged, in skin glands.

Text 2
Feeding experiments confirm that dendrobatids depend on dietary alkaloids: frogs given no toxic prey stay harmless. But when biologist Ralph Saporito and colleagues fed frogs the alkaloid pumiliotoxin 251D, some species converted it into allopumiliotoxin 267A, a compound several times more toxic and not found in their prey. For these species, the skin is a site of chemical modification, not merely storage.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the researchers' conclusion in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Poison dart frogs of the family Dendrobatidae carry potent alkaloids in their skin, yet captive-bred individuals raised on fruit flies and crickets are nearly toxin-free. Researchers have therefore concluded that the frogs make none of these compounds themselves; every alkaloid is acquired from wild prey such as ants and mites and simply stored, unchanged, in skin glands.

Text 2
Feeding experiments confirm that dendrobatids depend on dietary alkaloids: frogs given no toxic prey stay harmless. But when biologist Ralph Saporito and colleagues fed frogs the alkaloid pumiliotoxin 251D, some species converted it into allopumiliotoxin 267A, a compound several times more toxic and not found in their prey. For these species, the skin is a site of chemical modification, not merely storage.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the researchers' conclusion in Text 1?
options: By rejecting it, since the experiments show that dendrobatids can synthesize their skin alkaloids without eating toxic prey.
By accepting it, since the experiments show that frogs fed no toxic prey remain harmless, as captive-bred frogs do.
By questioning it, since the experiments show that captive diets of fruit flies and crickets in fact contain small amounts of alkaloids.
By accepting part of it, since the frogs do rely on prey for alkaloids, but objecting that some species alter those compounds rather than keeping them unchanged.
problem.explanation: Text 2는 개구리가 먹이에서 알칼로이드를 얻는다는 점(독성 먹이 없으면 무해)은 인정하지만, 일부 종이 그것을 더 강한 화합물로 변환한다는 점을 들어 '변화 없이 저장한다'는 Text 1의 주장을 반박한다. 따라서 부분 수용·부분 반박인 D가 정답이다. A는 개구리가 먹이 없이 스스로 합성한다고 하지만 Text 2는 먹이 의존을 확인한다. B는 먹이 의존 부분만 보고 '변화 없음' 주장에 대한 반박을 놓친다. C의 사육 먹이 속 알칼로이드는 어느 글에도 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 2 agrees that the frogs depend on prey for alkaloids (frogs without toxic prey stay harmless), but it shows that some species turn pumiliotoxin 251D into a stronger compound. That goes against Text 1's claim that the alkaloids are stored "unchanged." So D, which accepts part of the conclusion and objects to the rest, is correct. A is wrong because Text 2 confirms the frogs need their diet; it never says they make alkaloids from scratch. B only sees the agreement about diet and misses the objection about modification. C is wrong because neither text says captive diets contain alkaloids.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검증: Text 2는 먹이 의존(Text 1의 '먹이에서 획득' 부분)을 확인하면서 '변화 없이 저장'은 pumiliotoxin 251D→allopumiliotoxin 267A 변환 사례로 반박하므로 부분 수용·부분 반박이 정확함. A는 '먹이 없이 합성'이 Text 2 첫 문장과 모순, B는 Text 2의 반박('not merely storage')을 무시, C는 근거 없음. 해설(한/영) 모두 선택지 글자와 결론이 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 사실 관계: Saporito 등의 251D→267A 변환 연구는 실제 존재(Daly et al. 2003/Saporito 2012 등), 과장 없음. 난이도: Text 1의 두 부분(획득+불변) 중 어느 부분을 Text 2가 지지/반박하는지 분리해야 하므로 두 단계 판단이 필요하며, B가 매력적 오답, A도 부분 근거(독성 화합물이 먹이에 없음)를 가져 medium 적합. 형식: 선택지 4개, 정답 표기, 해설 완비.

advisory.note: Saporito et al. (2003 PNAS)의 251D→267A 수산화 연구와 사실관계가 일치함. B가 부분 근거를 가진 유력 오답이고, A는 '합성'이라는 말이 '변환'과 혼동되기 쉬움. C는 약한 오답이지만 말은 됨. medium 난이도에 적합.

problem.passage:
Text 1
African lungfish can survive years of drought by burrowing into mud and entering estivation, a dormant state in which metabolism drops sharply. Researchers studying this state have proposed that the fish's brain actively shuts itself down, releasing inhibitory compounds that act almost like a self-administered toxin and push the animal into a coma-like stupor. On this view, the brain functions as the master switch: it triggers dormancy first, and the rest of the body's slowdown follows from that neural command.

Text 2
In a recent study, physiologist Dana Okafor monitored lungfish as they entered estivation. She found that levels of inhibitory neurochemicals in the brain did rise sharply, producing the deep stupor others had described. However, this rise came only after the fish's oxygen consumption and heart rate had already fallen for several days. Okafor concludes that the neural shutdown is real but is better understood as a response to bodily changes already under way than as the event that sets dormancy in motion.

Based on the texts, how would Okafor (Text 2) most likely respond to the view of the researchers described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
African lungfish can survive years of drought by burrowing into mud and entering estivation, a dormant state in which metabolism drops sharply. Researchers studying this state have proposed that the fish's brain actively shuts itself down, releasing inhibitory compounds that act almost like a self-administered toxin and push the animal into a coma-like stupor. On this view, the brain functions as the master switch: it triggers dormancy first, and the rest of the body's slowdown follows from that neural command.

Text 2
In a recent study, physiologist Dana Okafor monitored lungfish as they entered estivation. She found that levels of inhibitory neurochemicals in the brain did rise sharply, producing the deep stupor others had described. However, this rise came only after the fish's oxygen consumption and heart rate had already fallen for several days. Okafor concludes that the neural shutdown is real but is better understood as a response to bodily changes already under way than as the event that sets dormancy in motion.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would Okafor (Text 2) most likely respond to the view of the researchers described in Text 1?
options: She would accept that the brain produces a coma-like state but dispute that this neural change is what initiates dormancy.
She would accept that metabolism drops during estivation but dispute that the brain releases inhibitory compounds at all.
She would accept that the brain initiates dormancy but dispute that the resulting stupor resembles a coma.
She would accept that inhibitory compounds act like a toxin but dispute that lungfish can remain dormant for years.
problem.explanation: Text 1은 뇌가 억제 물질을 분비해 휴면을 '먼저' 유발한다고 보고, Okafor는 억제 신경화학물질 증가와 깊은 혼수는 확인했지만 그것이 산소 소비·심박 감소 이후에 나타났다고 보고한다. 따라서 그녀는 신경적 혼수 상태는 인정하되 그것이 휴면의 시작 원인이라는 점은 반박할 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Okafor가 억제 물질 증가를 직접 관찰했으므로 틀리다. C는 순서가 뒤집혔다. 그녀는 혼수 같은 상태는 인정하고 뇌가 시작한다는 점을 부정한다. D는 수년간의 휴면 기간에 대해 Text 2가 다루지 않으므로 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Text 1 claims the brain releases inhibitory compounds that trigger dormancy first, and the body's slowdown follows. Okafor confirms that inhibitory neurochemicals rise and cause deep stupor, but she finds that this happens only after oxygen use and heart rate have already dropped, so she would accept the coma-like state while rejecting the idea that it starts dormancy. That makes A correct. B is wrong because Okafor actually observed the inhibitory compounds rise. C reverses her position: she accepts the stupor and disputes that the brain starts the process. options: Because the Yucatán Peninsula has very few rivers or lakes, the ancient Maya depended on cenotes, which expose underground water, for much of their drinking water.
Because the Yucatán Peninsula is made largely of limestone, slightly acidic rainwater has slowly dissolved the rock over thousands of years.
Because the dissolving limestone created underground channels, the Yucatán Peninsula now holds a vast store of fresh groundwater.
Because the ground collapsed above underground channels, natural sinkholes called cenotes formed in some places on the Yucatán Peninsula.
problem.explanation: 목표는 세노테가 고대 마야인에게 왜 중요했는지 설명하는 것이다. A는 강과 호수가 거의 없어서 마야인이 지하수를 드러내는 세노테에 식수를 의존했다고 말하므로 목표에 맞는다. B는 석회암이 녹는 과정만 설명하고 마야인은 언급하지 않는다. C는 지하수 저장에 대한 정보뿐이고 마야인에게 왜 중요했는지는 말하지 않는다. D는 세노테가 생긴 과정을 설명할 뿐, 마야인에게 왜 중요했는지는 다루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain why cenotes mattered to the ancient Maya. A does this: it says the region had very few rivers or lakes, so the Maya relied on cenotes, which expose underground water, for drinking water. B only describes how limestone dissolves and never mentions the Maya. C tells you about the groundwater supply but doesn't explain why cenotes were important to people. D explains how cenotes formed, not why they were important to the Maya.

problem.explanation: 빈칸이 있는 절의 주어는 복수 명사 'the geostrophic winds'이며, 'along this boundary'와 삽입된 분사구 'concentrated into ... surface'는 수식어일 뿐이다. 이 절에는 정동사가 없으므로 빈칸에는 복수 주어와 일치하는 정동사가 필요하고, 따라서 D가 정답이다. problem.explanationEn: The subject of the clause with the blank is the plural noun "the geostrophic winds." The phrase "along this boundary" and the inserted participial phrase "concentrated into ... surface" are only modifiers. Since this clause has no main verb yet, the blank needs a finite verb that agrees with a plural subject, so D is correct. A and B are participle forms, so they leave the clause without a main verb and the sentence is incomplete. C is a finite verb, but it is singular, so it is the trap you fall into if you mistake the nearby "surface" or "boundary" for the subject.

problem.stimulus: The fine, loosely packed silt that blankets China's Loess Plateau, deposited over hundreds of thousands of years by winds sweeping in from the deserts to the northwest, ______ easily lifted back into the air once spring gusts strip away the sparse grasses whose roots hold the surface grains in place, a process that helps feed the region's dust storms.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'silt'이며, 'that blankets...'와 'deposited over...'는 주어를 꾸며 주는 수식어구일 뿐이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 C 'is'가 정답이다. A 'are'는 정동사이긴 하지만 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'years', 'winds', 'deserts'에 수를 맞춘 것이어서 단수 주어와 일치하지 않는다. B 'being'과 D 'having been'은 분사형이라 정동사 역할을 하지 못해 문장이 완성되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "silt." The phrases "that blankets..." and "deposited over..." just modify that subject. So the sentence needs a singular main verb, which makes C, "is," the correct answer. A, "are," is a main verb, but it's plural: it agrees with nearby nouns like "years," "winds," and "deserts" instead of the actual subject. B, "being," and D, "having been," are participles, which can't act as the main verb, so with either one the sentence is incomplete.

problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The leading front." The phrase "together with ... behind it" is an interrupting modifier, and it doesn't make the subject plural. The sentence also has no other main verb, so the blank needs a singular present-tense finite verb, which makes D correct. A and C are plural forms, so they only work if you mistake "waves" or the "together with" phrase for the subject. B is a participle, which would leave the sentence with no main verb at all.

C는 뒤 문장이 일반 원리의 구체적 사례처럼 보이게 하지만, 실제로는 특정 사례가 아니라 원리에서 도출된 귀결이다. D는 유사한 별개의 현상을 소개할 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 같은 메커니즘의 결과이지 비슷한 다른 현상이 아니다.

The sentence after the blank describes what follows from that mechanism, which is longer methane lifetimes. That is a cause-and-effect relationship, so A is correct. B signals contrast, but the second sentence doesn't go against the first; it follows from it. C would make the second sentence a specific instance, but it is really a consequence drawn from the principle, not an example of it. D would introduce a separate but comparable phenomenon, while the second sentence describes the result of the same process.

D treats the two sentences as parallel, but the final sentence points in the opposite direction from the limitation instead of adding a similar point.

Over a decade of fieldwork in Louisiana's Barataria Basin, geologist Lena Okafor uncovered a striking contrast in accretion rates______ marshes fed by nearby river diversions gained nearly a centimeter of elevation per year, while isolated marshes gained only a few millimeters.

problem.stimulus: Salt marshes can keep pace with rising seas only if sediment deposition, the gradual settling of silt and clay carried in by tides and rivers, raises the marsh surface quickly enough. Over a decade of fieldwork in Louisiana's Barataria Basin, geologist Lena Okafor uncovered a striking contrast in accretion rates______ marshes fed by nearby river diversions gained nearly a centimeter of elevation per year, while isolated marshes gained only a few millimeters.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Over a decade ... in accretion rates"는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "marshes ... gained ... per year, while ..."도 동사 gained를 가진 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 앞에서 말한 '뚜렷한 차이'의 구체적 내용이므로 두 독립절을 잇고 설명을 덧붙이는 콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 아무 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 with가 뒤를 전치사구로 만들려 하지만 정동사 gained가 남아 있어 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "Over a decade ... in accretion rates," is an independent clause, and the part after it, "marshes ... gained ... per year, while ...," is also an independent clause because it has its own main verb, gained. The second clause spells out the "striking contrast" mentioned in the first, so a colon, which joins two independent clauses and introduces an explanation, works best, which makes C correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B puts the clauses together with no punctuation at all, which is a run-on sentence. D adds "with," which should turn the second part into a prepositional phrase, but the main verb "gained" is still there, so the sentence doesn't work grammatically.

problem.passage:
During the day, sunlight warms the ground, and rising plumes of heated air churn the lowest kilometer or so of the atmosphere, a region meteorologists call the boundary layer, until temperature and humidity are nearly uniform from the surface to its top______ after sunset, this turbulence collapses, leaving a shallow, stable layer of cool air near the ground beneath a calmer "residual layer" above.

problem.stimulus: During the day, sunlight warms the ground, and rising plumes of heated air churn the lowest kilometer or so of the atmosphere, a region meteorologists call the boundary layer, until temperature and humidity are nearly uniform from the surface to its top______ after sunset, this turbulence collapses, leaving a shallow, stable layer of cool air near the ground beneath a calmer "residual layer" above.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞(During the day ... to its top)과 뒤(after sunset, this turbulence collapses ...)는 각각 독립절이므로 세미콜론으로 나누고 접속부사 however 뒤에 쉼표를 찍은 D가 정답이다. A는 however 양쪽에 쉼표를 두어 삽입어처럼 보이지만 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. B는 절 사이에 아무 경계 부호가 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C는 세미콜론을 쓰긴 했지만 however 뒤에 두어 however가 앞 절에 붙게 되므로, 대조가 뒤 절을 이끄는 문맥과 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank (During the day ... to its top) and the text after it (after sunset, this turbulence collapses ...) are both independent clauses, so D is correct: it separates them with a semicolon and puts a comma after the conjunctive adverb "however." A sets "however" off with commas as if it were an interrupter, but that joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. B has no punctuation marking the boundary between the clauses, so it creates a run-on sentence. C does use a semicolon, but it puts it after "however," which attaches "however" to the first clause even though the contrast is supposed to introduce the second clause.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "meltwater ... accelerates"와 빈칸 뒤 "once ... the water escapes ... stalls"는 각각 독립절이다. "then"은 등위접속사가 아니라 접속부사이므로 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하며, A가 이를 충족한다. B와 C는 쉼표와 then만으로 두 독립절을 연결해 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("meltwater ... accelerates") and the text after it ("once ... the water escapes ... and the surge stalls") are both independent clauses. "Then" is a conjunctive adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so it can't join two independent clauses by itself. A semicolon has to come before it, and that is what A does. B and C use only a comma with "then," which creates a comma splice. D has no punctuation between the two clauses at all, so it creates a run-on sentence.

A (generate) looks tempting because the mountains do cause rain, but it means creating something new, which clashes with the "do not supply the water themselves" contrast. B (postpone) might seem to fit because the rain comes only after the air travels inland, but the mountains start the release rather than delay it. Martin Ralph의 대기의 강·지형성 강수 연구 언급은 사실과 부합. 한·영 해설 모두 글자 참조 일치, 한글 혼입 없음.

problem.explanation: 목표는 흔한 사구 관리 방식(마람그래스 식재)의 단점을 제시하는 것이다. B는 식재가 모래의 내륙 이동을 막아 희귀 곤충 서식지가 약 70% 줄었다는 부정적 결과를 그 방식과 연결하므로 정답이다. A도 같은 식재 사례를 쓰지만 사구 높이 증가라는 이점만 말한다. C는 단점에 대한 대응책을 설명할 뿐 단점 자체는 밝히지 않는다. D는 사구가 형성되는 과정을 일반적으로 설명할 뿐이다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to present a drawback of a common dune management approach, which here is marram grass planting. B works because it ties the planting to a negative result: sand stopped moving inland, and the bare habitats used by rare insects shrank by about 70 percent. A uses the same Hayle Towans example, but it only gives a benefit, the higher dune crests. C describes a response to the problem but never says what the drawback was. D just explains how dunes form in general.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B 검증: 노트 4번(밀집 식생이 모래 내륙 이동 차단, 희귀 곤충 서식지 약 70% 감소)을 흔한 관리 방식(마람그래스 식재)의 단점으로 정확히 연결함. A는 같은 사례의 이점만, C는 대응책만, D는 일반적 형성 과정만 제시해 목표 불충족. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. Hayle Towans는 실재 지명이며 수치는 노트 내 가상 데이터로 문항 내 일관성에 문제 없음. C·D가 노트에 없는 'and elsewhere', 'as on many coasts'를 덧붙이지만 오답으로서 허용 범위. 난이도: 정답 식별에 '관리 방식 특정 + 부정적 결과 확인' 두 단계가 필요하고 A·C가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: B만 관리 방식(마람그래스 식재)과 그 부정적 결과를 연결한다. A는 같은 사례를 쓰지만 이점만 말하고, C는 단점을 암시하기만 해서 오답들도 그럴듯하다. 작은 문제: C와 D는 노트에 없는 내용을 Hayle Towans에 연결한다(노트는 'some managers'라고만 하고, 사구 형성은 일반적인 설명이다). 오답이라 정답 판정에는 영향이 없지만 해설에서 짚지 않았다. Hayle Towans의 구체적 수치는 실제 자료로 확인되지 않아 가상의 자료일 수 있으나, 노트 기반 문항이라 허용 범위로 본다.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Carbon dioxide (CO2) released at Earth's surface does not stay concentrated near the ground.
- Air in the troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere, becomes vertically well mixed within about one to two months.
- Air in the stratosphere, the layer above the troposphere, exchanges with tropospheric air much more slowly, over roughly four to six years.
- As a result, CO2 levels in the upper stratosphere lag those near the surface by several years.
- An individual CO2 molecule typically remains in the atmosphere about five years before being absorbed by oceans or plants, though the added CO2 as a whole persists for centuries.

The student wants to contrast how quickly the two atmospheric layers become mixed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Carbon dioxide (CO2) released at Earth's surface does not stay concentrated near the ground.
- Air in the troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere, becomes vertically well mixed within about one to two months.
- Air in the stratosphere, the layer above the troposphere, exchanges with tropospheric air much more slowly, over roughly four to six years.
- As a result, CO2 levels in the upper stratosphere lag those near the surface by several years.
- An individual CO2 molecule typically remains in the atmosphere about five years before being absorbed by oceans or plants, though the added CO2 as a whole persists for centuries.
problem.question: The student wants to contrast how quickly the two atmospheric layers become mixed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Carbon dioxide released at Earth's surface does not stay near the ground, and an individual molecule typically remains in the atmosphere about five years.
Because stratospheric air exchanges with tropospheric air over roughly four to six years, CO2 levels in the upper stratosphere lag those near the surface by several years.
An individual CO2 molecule remains airborne for about five years, but the added CO2 as a whole persists in the atmosphere for centuries.
Whereas air in the troposphere becomes vertically well mixed within one to two months, stratospheric air exchanges with the layer below it only over about four to six years.
problem.explanation: 목표는 대류권과 성층권 두 층의 혼합 속도를 대조하는 것이다. D는 대류권의 1~2개월과 성층권의 4~6년을 'Whereas'로 연결해 두 층을 직접 대조한다. B는 성층권의 느린 교환을 정확히 쓰지만 대류권의 혼합 속도는 빠져 있고, 대신 그 결과(농도 지연)를 설명한다. C는 분자 하나의 체류 시간과 CO2 전체의 지속 기간을 대조할 뿐 대기층 비교가 아니다. A는 지표 근처 분포와 체류 시간만 다루어 두 층에 대한 언급이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to contrast how fast the two layers, the troposphere and the stratosphere, get mixed. D does exactly that: it sets the troposphere's one to two months against the stratosphere's four to six years using "Whereas." B gets the stratosphere's slow exchange right, but it never gives the troposphere's mixing speed, and it focuses on a result (the lag in CO2 levels) instead. C sets up a contrast too, but it compares how long one molecule stays airborne with how long added CO2 lasts overall, not the two layers. A only talks about surface CO2 and residence time and never mentions either layer.

quality.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric carbon dioxide stratification vertical mixing timescale and residence time radiative property change

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 노트 2·3을 'Whereas'로 결합해 대류권(1~2개월)과 성층권(4~6년)의 혼합 속도를 직접 대조하므로 유일하게 목표를 충족한다. B는 성층권 교환 속도와 그 결과(농도 지연)를 다루어 부분적으로 관련성이 있고, C는 대조 구조는 갖추었으나 분자 체류 시간 대 전체 지속 기간을 비교해 대상이 다르며, A는 두 층을 언급하지 않는다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 D를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조가 선택지와 일치하며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 과학적 내용(대류권 수개월 내 수직 혼합, 성층권-대류권 교환 수년, CO2 분자 체류 ~5년 vs 추가 CO2 수세기 지속)은 통용되는 수치와 부합. 난이도는 표준 medium에 부합하나, D가 유일하게 두 층을 모두 언급하는 선택지라 다소 쉬운 편에 가까운 경계선 수준.

advisory.note: B가 부분적으로 맞는 근거(성층권 교환)를 가진 유력한 오답이고, C는 대조 구조라 형식상 그럴듯함. A는 약한 오답이지만 medium 기준에 부합.

problem.passage:
Tsunamis travel across the open ocean as shallow-water waves, whose speed depends mainly on water depth: the deeper the water, the faster the wave. As a tsunami approaches a coast, the part of the wave front over shallower water slows down while the part over deeper water keeps moving quickly, so the front bends, or refracts, toward the shallow areas. Oceanographer Lena Marsh has proposed that this bending, not just the overall decrease in depth near shore, explains why some coastal sites see much higher tsunami run-up than nearby sites. In her view, an underwater ridge that extends out from the coast acts like a lens, turning wave energy inward and concentrating it on the stretch of shore where the ridge reaches land.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marsh's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Tsunamis travel across the open ocean as shallow-water waves, whose speed depends mainly on water depth: the deeper the water, the faster the wave. As a tsunami approaches a coast, the part of the wave front over shallower water slows down while the part over deeper water keeps moving quickly, so the front bends, or refracts, toward the shallow areas. Oceanographer Lena Marsh has proposed that this bending, not just the overall decrease in depth near shore, explains why some coastal sites see much higher tsunami run-up than nearby sites. In her view, an underwater ridge that extends out from the coast acts like a lens, turning wave energy inward and concentrating it on the stretch of shore where the ridge reaches land.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Marsh's hypothesis?
options: During a past tsunami, two coastal sites that had similar near-shore depths showed very different wave heights, and the site with the much higher waves sat at the landward end of a long offshore ridge.
During a past tsunami, wave heights rose steadily at every coastal site as the waves moved from deep water onto the continental shelf, whether or not an offshore ridge was present.
During a past tsunami, instruments in the open ocean showed the waves moving at more than 700 kilometers per hour over the deepest parts of the basin, in line with depth-based predictions.
During a past tsunami, a coastal site at the landward end of an offshore ridge had high waves, but so did a nearby site with no ridge and a much shallower, wider shelf.
problem.explanation: Marsh는 수심 감소 자체가 아니라 해저 능선에 의한 굴절 집중이 지역 간 차이를 만든다고 주장한다. A는 근해 수심이 비슷한 두 지점(수심 효과 통제)에서 능선 끝 지점만 파고가 훨씬 높았으므로 가설을 직접 지지한다. B는 능선과 무관하게 수심 감소만으로 파고가 높아졌다는 내용이라 오히려 수심 설명에 부합한다. C는 수심-속도 관계를 확인할 뿐 해안 간 차이나 능선 효과와는 무관하다. D는 능선 없는 지점도 수심이 얕아 파고가 높았으므로 능선의 고유한 역할을 보여 주지 못하고 오히려 약화시킨다.
problem.explanationEn: Marsh claims that refraction over an offshore ridge, not simply shallowing water, explains why some sites get much higher run-up than nearby sites. A holds near-shore depth roughly constant between two sites and shows that only the site at the end of a ridge had much higher waves, which isolates the ridge effect and directly supports her view. B shows waves growing at every site regardless of ridges, which fits the simple depth explanation instead. C only confirms that speed depends on depth in the open ocean and says nothing about differences between coastal sites. D shows a site without a ridge getting equally high waves because of a shallow shelf, so it fails to show a unique ridge effect and actually weakens the hypothesis.

quality.seed: earth and space science — Tsunami wave speed dispersive propagation and seafloor bathymetry refraction coastal amplification effect

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검산 일치: 근해 수심을 통제한 상태에서 능선 끝 지점만 파고가 높았다는 결과는 "수심 감소가 아니라 능선에 의한 굴절 집중"이라는 Marsh의 핵심 주장을 직접 지지한다. B는 수심 단독 설명에 부합, C는 전제(수심-속도 관계) 확인에 그침, D는 능선 없는 얕은 지점도 높은 파고를 보여 능선 고유 효과를 분리하지 못함(오히려 약화). 한·영 해설 결론 및 선택지 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 과학적 사실(천해파 속도의 수심 의존, 심해 700km/h 전후 속도, 얕은 쪽으로의 굴절) 정확. 가상 학자 사용으로 저작권 문제 없음. "단순 수심 감소가 아닌 능선 효과" 라는 대비를 파악하고 A가 수심을 통제했음을 읽어내야 하며, D가 능선 지점의 높은 파고를 포함해 훑어 읽으면 오답 유인이 있어 medium 적합.

advisory.note: A controls for depth and isolates the ridge effect, so it is clearly the correct answer. D is the strong distractor because it includes a ridge site with high waves. B and C fall fairly easily, but they are plausible. Overall this works at medium difficulty.

problem.passage:
When a burst of dense, fast solar wind strikes Earth, its dynamic pressure squeezes the dayside magnetosphere inward, sometimes pushing the boundary from about ten Earth radii to fewer than seven. Yet space physicists caution that this compression alone does not reliably predict how high a storm will rank on geomagnetic severity scales such as the Kp index. The pressure pulse's influence on storm severity is not self-sufficient but rather ______: only when the interplanetary magnetic field carried by the wind points southward, allowing energy to couple efficiently into the magnetosphere, does a compression typically escalate into a major storm.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: When a burst of dense, fast solar wind strikes Earth, its dynamic pressure squeezes the dayside magnetosphere inward, sometimes pushing the boundary from about ten Earth radii to fewer than seven. Yet space physicists caution that this compression alone does not reliably predict how high a storm will rank on geomagnetic severity scales such as the Kp index. The pressure pulse's influence on storm severity is not self-sufficient but rather ______: only when the interplanetary magnetic field carried by the wind points southward, allowing energy to couple efficiently into the magnetosphere, does a compression typically escalate into a major storm.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 정답 D(conditional): 'not self-sufficient but rather ___' 구조에서 빈칸은 부정된 '자족적(그 자체로 충분함)'과 반대 극성이어야 하며, 콜론 뒤 내용(남향 자기장일 때만 큰 폭풍으로 발전)이 '다른 조건에 달려 있음'을 뒷받침한다. A(self-contained): 부정어를 무시하고 부정된 self-sufficient와 같은 뜻을 고른 오답. B(decisive): 'not'과 'but rather'를 이중 부정으로 잘못 읽어 압력이 다시 결정적이라고 극성을 뒤집은 오답이며, 지문의 '압축만으로는 예측 못 한다'와 모순된다. C(confidential): conditional과 철자·발음만 비슷할 뿐 '기밀의'라는 뜻으로 문맥과 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn: D (conditional) is correct. The sentence uses a "not X but rather Y" structure, so the blank has to mean the opposite of "self-sufficient." The text after the colon backs this up: a compression usually becomes a major storm only when the magnetic field points southward. That means the pressure pulse's effect depends on another condition. A (self-contained) skips over the negation and repeats the meaning of the word being rejected. B (decisive) reads the structure as if it flipped twice, so it makes pressure the deciding factor again. That contradicts the text's point that compression alone doesn't predict severity. C (confidential) only looks and sounds like "conditional." It means "secret," which doesn't fit the context.

hardJudge.note: 'not self-sufficient but rather ___' 구조와 콜론 뒤 'only when... southward' 조건절이 D(conditional)를 일관되게 뒷받침. A는 부정된 개념의 동의어, B는 이중 반전 오답, C는 형태 유사 오답으로 레시피 설계 충족. 지문의 자기권 압축(≈10 Re→<7 Re), 남향 IMF 결합, Kp 지수 서술은 사실과 부합. 통념(압축=폭풍 심각도)을 반박하는 담화 구조와 부정/대조 재구성, 콜론 뒤 조건 증거의 종합이 요구되어 medium 이상의 사고를 요구함.

advisory.note: 정답은 맞고 해설도 일관된다. 다만 쉽다. 'not self-sufficient but rather'와 'only when'이 conditional을 사실상 그대로 알려 준다. C는 뜻이 맞지 않는 철자 유사 오답이라 바로 지워진다. B도 앞 문장 'compression alone does not reliably predict'와 정면으로 어긋나 쉽게 배제된다. 부정 뒤에 대조가 오는 구조가 있지만 극성을 거꾸로 따져 볼 필요가 거의 없다. 난이도는 우주물리 용어와 지문 길이에서만 나온다.

problem.passage:
Haze forms when tiny airborne particles, such as those released by vehicle exhaust and wildfires, scatter and absorb sunlight, making distant objects harder to see. Researchers in one city measured visibility each afternoon for a year and also recorded the concentration of fine particles in the air. They found that on days with higher particle concentrations, the farthest distance at which a landmark could be clearly seen was consistently shorter. Because the city's air quality index is calculated directly from these same particle measurements, the researchers concluded that on days when the index reports poorer air quality, residents should expect that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: Haze forms when tiny airborne particles, such as those released by vehicle exhaust and wildfires, scatter and absorb sunlight, making distant objects harder to see. Researchers in one city measured visibility each afternoon for a year and also recorded the concentration of fine particles in the air. They found that on days with higher particle concentrations, the farthest distance at which a landmark could be clearly seen was consistently shorter. Because the city's air quality index is calculated directly from these same particle measurements, the researchers concluded that on days when the index reports poorer air quality, residents should expect that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: distant landmarks will be visible from farther away than usual.
distant landmarks will be harder to see clearly than usual.
distant landmarks will be equally visible regardless of particle levels.
distant landmarks will be visible only after the particles have fallen to the ground.
problem.explanation: 지문은 미세입자 농도가 높을수록 시정 거리가 짧아진다고 말하고, 대기질 지수가 바로 그 입자 측정값으로 계산된다고 밝힌다. 따라서 지수가 나쁜 날은 입자가 많은 날이므로 먼 지형지물이 잘 보이지 않을 것이라는 B가 정답이다. A는 관계를 거꾸로 뒤집은 것이다. C는 지문에서 찾은 일관된 관계를 무시한다. D는 입자가 땅에 떨어지는 과정을 끌어들이는데, 지문은 그 내용을 다루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage says that higher fine-particle concentrations consistently shortened the distance at which landmarks could be seen, and that the air quality index is calculated from those same particle measurements. So a day with a poorer index is a day with more particles, which means distant landmarks will be harder to see, and B is correct. A flips this relationship backward. C ignores the consistent link the researchers found. D brings in particles falling to the ground, which the passage never discusses.

quality.seed: earth and space science — Atmospheric visibility reduction particulate matter haze formation and air quality index measurement standard

hardJudge.note: 지문의 두 명시적 연결(입자↑→시정↓, 지수=입자 측정값)만으로 B가 도출되는 한 단계 추론. A는 역전, C는 상관 무시, D는 지문 밖 과정 도입으로 전형적 오답 유형. 해설 한·영 모두 글자 참조와 결론 일치, 한글 혼입 없음. 다만 D는 다소 약한 오답이나 easy 수준에서는 허용 범위.

advisory.note: 추론이 한 단계뿐이다(지수가 나쁨 → 입자가 많음 → 시정이 짧음). 오답 A는 관계를 뒤집은 전형적 오개념이다. C, D는 다소 약하지만 easy 수준에서는 받아들일 만하다.

In parts of Sweden's Gulf of Bothnia coast, the land is still rising by about 8 millimeters per year, while the global sea level is rising by only about 3 to 4 millimeters per year. Text 1
Volcanologists often sort pyroclastic density currents into two types: dense flows that hug valley floors and dilute surges that spread more widely. Some hazard planners argue that maps should focus mainly on valleys, since the dense flows carry most of the material and are therefore the greatest danger to nearby towns.

Text 2
Dilute surges may carry less material, but they can move faster than 100 kilometers per hour and reach temperatures above 300 degrees Celsius. Because they are not confined to valleys, surges can climb over ridges and strike communities that seem safely out of the way. For this reason, hazard maps that ignore surges can leave many residents unprepared.

In many estuaries, dense seawater slides upstream along the riverbed beneath lighter freshwater, forming a "salt wedge." Some hydrologists argue that the main factor controlling how far this wedge reaches inland is the daily rise and fall of the tides.

Text 2

When river flow drops during dry seasons, the salt wedge advances far upstream even under ordinary tides. When heavy rains raise river flow, the wedge is pushed back toward the sea. River discharge, not tidal motion, appears to set how far the wedge travels.

problem.passage:
Text 1
After large eruptions, researchers often estimate how much an event will cool global climate by measuring the total volume of ash it ejects. Because fine ash particles can travel thousands of kilometers on high-altitude winds and block incoming sunlight, eruptions that produce the most ash are generally expected to produce the strongest and longest-lasting cooling.

Text 2
Volcanologist Mira Okonjo notes that ash, even the finest grains, tends to clump together and fall out of the atmosphere within days to weeks, so its effect on sunlight doesn't last long. Lasting cooling comes instead from sulfur dioxide that reaches the stratosphere, where it turns into tiny sulfate droplets that can stay aloft for a year or more. An eruption that releases huge amounts of ash but little sulfur, or that never sends its plume high enough, may barely change global temperatures.

Based on the texts, how would Okonjo (Text 2) most likely respond to the approach described in Text 1?

problem.passage:
In making solar cells, engineers often use a process called plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition to coat silicon wafers with a thin film of silicon nitride. The film must cover the entire wafer at the same thickness, because even small gaps or thick patches can reduce how much sunlight the cell turns into electricity. For this reason, technicians check each wafer carefully to make sure the coating is ______ from one edge to the other.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.stimulus: In making solar cells, engineers often use a process called plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition to coat silicon wafers with a thin film of silicon nitride. The film must cover the entire wafer at the same thickness, because even small gaps or thick patches can reduce how much sunlight the cell turns into electricity. For this reason, technicians check each wafer carefully to make sure the coating is ______ from one edge to the other.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
problem.explanation: 지문은 박막이 웨이퍼 전체를 "같은 두께"로 덮어야 하고, 틈이나 두꺼운 부분이 있으면 안 된다고 직접 밝힌다. 따라서 기술자가 확인하는 것은 코팅이 가장자리부터 끝까지 고르다는 점이므로 A가 정답이다. B는 '깨지기 쉬운'이라는 뜻이라 엔지니어가 확인하려는 바람직한 성질이 아니다. C는 '일시적인'이라는 뜻으로 두께가 일정해야 한다는 단서와 관계가 없다. D는 '색이 다채로운'이라는 뜻이며 지문은 색이 아니라 두께의 일관성을 다룬다.
problem.explanationEn: The text says the film has to cover the whole wafer "at the same thickness" and that gaps or thick patches cause problems. So technicians are checking that the coating is even all the way across, which is why A is correct. B means "easily broken," and engineers wouldn't be checking for that, since it's a flaw. C means "lasting only a short time," which has nothing to do with the clue about even thickness. D is about color, but the text is about thickness being consistent, not about color.

PECVD로 실리콘 나이트라이드 반사방지/패시베이션 막을 증착하는 것은 사실에 부합. 해설 한·영 모두 글자 참조·결론 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 오답 fragile/temporary/colorful은 모두 형용사로 문법적으로 들어맞으며 단서를 놓친 학생에게 그럴듯하되 규칙(단서 매칭)을 알면 바로 배제됨. 다만 오답들이 다소 명백히 어긋나 easy 하한에 가깝지만 easy 범위 내.

advisory.note: 단서 'same thickness'가 지문에 직접 나와 있고 한 단계 추론으로 풀린다. 오답들이 다소 약하지만(특히 colorful) 말이 안 되는 수준은 아니다. 다만 오개념을 노린 오답으로서의 매력도는 낮은 편이다.

problem.passage:
Early telescope makers noticed that the images they produced were often fringed with color. The cause is chromatic aberration: the focal length of a simple glass lens ______ with the wavelength of light, so red and blue light come into focus at slightly different points. To correct this, designers later paired two lenses made of different types of glass.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Early telescope makers noticed that the images they produced were often fringed with color. The cause is chromatic aberration: the focal length of a simple glass lens ______ with the wavelength of light, so red and blue light come into focus at slightly different points. To correct this, designers later paired two lenses made of different types of glass.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 동사의 주어는 단수 명사 "the focal length"이며, "of a simple glass lens"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 그러므로 단수 동사가 필요하고, 문맥상 일반적 사실을 말하므로 현재형 단수인 C "varies"가 정답이다. A "vary", B "are varying", D "have varied"는 모두 복수 동사로, 단수 주어와 수가 맞지 않는다. 바로 앞의 "lens"나 뒤의 "wavelength"가 아니라 실제 주어 "length"에 맞춰야 한다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of the verb in the blank is the singular noun "the focal length." The phrase "of a simple glass lens" only modifies that subject. So you need a singular verb, and since the sentence states a general fact, the present-tense singular "varies" in C is correct. A ("vary"), B ("are varying"), and D ("have varied") are all plural verb forms, so none of them agrees with the singular subject. Make the verb agree with the true subject, "length," and not with a nearby noun.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "the focal length"(단수) → "varies"가 유일한 단수 동사. 오답 A·B·D는 모두 복수형으로 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되며, 전형적 오개념(근접 명사/복수 혼동)을 반영. 해설(한·영) 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 단, 인접 명사 "lens"도 단수라 '근접 명사 함정' 언급은 실질적 유인력이 약하나 오류는 아님. 과학 내용(색수차, 파장에 따른 초점거리 변화, 색지움 렌즈) 사실에 부합. 독창 지문으로 저작권 의심 없음.

advisory.note: 주어와 동사의 수 일치를 묻는 단일 규칙 문항이다. 주어와 동사 사이에 복수 명사가 없어서 방해 요소가 약하지만 easy 난이도에는 맞는다. 색수차에 관한 설명은 사실과 맞다.

problem.passage:
Some polymers behave differently depending on how quickly they are deformed. When stretched slowly, their long molecular chains have time to slide past one another, so the material flows and absorbs little energy. When struck suddenly, the chains cannot rearrange fast enough, and the material stiffens and converts much of the impact energy into heat. Materials engineer Priya Natarajan hypothesizes that adding such a strain-rate-sensitive polymer layer to a fiberglass panel will make the panel better at withstanding high-speed impacts, because the layer will dissipate more energy as the impact speed increases.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Natarajan's hypothesis?
problem.stimulus: Some polymers behave differently depending on how quickly they are deformed. When stretched slowly, their long molecular chains have time to slide past one another, so the material flows and absorbs little energy. When struck suddenly, the chains cannot rearrange fast enough, and the material stiffens and converts much of the impact energy into heat. Materials engineer Priya Natarajan hypothesizes that adding such a strain-rate-sensitive polymer layer to a fiberglass panel will make the panel better at withstanding high-speed impacts, because the layer will dissipate more energy as the impact speed increases.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Natarajan's hypothesis?
options: Panels with the polymer layer weighed slightly more than panels without it but cost about the same to manufacture.
Panels with the polymer layer absorbed about the same share of energy at low impact speeds as at high impact speeds.
Panels with the polymer layer looked smoother and were easier to paint than panels without the layer.
Panels with the polymer layer absorbed a larger share of impact energy as test speeds rose and cracked less often than panels without it.
problem.explanation: 가설의 핵심은 충격 속도가 높아질수록 고분자 층이 더 많은 에너지를 흡수해 패널이 고속 충격을 더 잘 견딘다는 것이다. D는 속도가 높아질수록 흡수 에너지 비율이 커지고 균열도 적었다는 발견이므로 가설을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 무게와 비용에 관한 것으로 충격 저항과 무관하다. B는 속도와 관계없이 흡수량이 같다는 것이므로 오히려 가설을 약화한다. C는 외관과 도장 편의성에 관한 것이라 가설과 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The hypothesis says the polymer layer will absorb more energy as impact speed rises, so the panel will hold up better against high-speed hits. D directly supports it: energy absorption went up with test speed, and the panels with the layer cracked less often. A is about weight and cost, which doesn't tell you anything about impact resistance. B shows absorption staying the same at every speed, which actually weakens the hypothesis. C is about appearance and painting, which has nothing to do with the claim.

advisory.note: D는 가설의 두 요소(속도 증가에 따른 에너지 흡수 증가, 고속 충격 저항 향상)를 모두 직접 보여 준다. B는 속도와 관계없이 흡수량이 같다는 그럴듯한 오답이다. A와 C는 가설과 관련 없는 속성이라 쉽게 배제되지만, easy 수준에서는 허용할 만하다.

problem.passage:
Glow-in-the-dark paints keep shining after the lights go off because of phosphorescence. When the paint absorbs light, some electrons in it are pushed into a "triplet state," an energized condition they can leave only slowly. As they gradually return to their normal state, they give off light for minutes or even hours. Chemist Lena Ortiz proposes that adding tiny amounts of oxygen-blocking coating to such paints will make them glow longer, because oxygen molecules can collide with electrons in the triplet state and drain their energy away before it can be released as light.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ortiz's proposal?
problem.stimulus: Glow-in-the-dark paints keep shining after the lights go off because of phosphorescence. When the paint absorbs light, some electrons in it are pushed into a "triplet state," an energized condition they can leave only slowly. As they gradually return to their normal state, they give off light for minutes or even hours. Chemist Lena Ortiz proposes that adding tiny amounts of oxygen-blocking coating to such paints will make them glow longer, because oxygen molecules can collide with electrons in the triplet state and drain their energy away before it can be released as light.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ortiz's proposal?
options: Paint samples sealed under the coating kept glowing visibly for about twice as long as identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
Paint samples sealed under the coating looked the same color in daylight as identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
Paint samples sealed under the coating absorbed light more slowly during charging than identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
Paint samples sealed under the coating cost slightly more to produce than identical uncoated samples exposed to air.
problem.explanation: Ortiz는 산소를 막는 코팅을 하면 산소가 삼중항 상태의 에너지를 빼앗지 못하므로 도료가 더 오래 빛날 것이라고 주장한다. A는 코팅한 시료가 공기에 노출된 시료보다 두 배쯤 오래 빛났다고 하므로 이 예측을 직접 확인해 준다. B는 낮에 보이는 색에 관한 것이라 발광 지속 시간과 관계가 없다. C는 빛을 흡수하는 속도를 말할 뿐 빛이 얼마나 오래 지속되는지는 말하지 않는다. D는 생산 비용에 관한 것으로 주장과 무관하다.
problem.explanationEn: Ortiz claims that an oxygen-blocking coating will make the paint glow longer, because oxygen can no longer drain energy from electrons in the triplet state. Choice A says the coated samples glowed about twice as long as the uncoated ones exposed to air, so it directly confirms her prediction. Choice B is about the paint's color in daylight, which has nothing to do with how long it glows. Choice C is about how fast the paint absorbs light while charging, not how long the glow lasts. Choice D is about production cost, which doesn't relate to her claim.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Most solar cells are made from crystalline silicon.
- Pure silicon conducts electricity poorly, so small amounts of other elements are added in a process called doping.
- Adding phosphorus gives silicon extra electrons, creating "n-type" silicon.

problem.question: The student wants to explain how a solar cell turns sunlight into electricity. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Most solar cells are made from crystalline silicon, a material that conducts electricity poorly unless other elements are added to it.
In a solar cell, an electric field at the boundary between n-type and p-type silicon pushes electrons freed by sunlight in one direction, creating a current.
In a solar cell, adding phosphorus gives silicon extra electrons, while adding boron leaves silicon with missing electrons called holes.
In a solar cell, sunlight adds extra electrons to pure silicon, which then forms a boundary called a p-n junction.
problem.explanation: 목표는 태양전지가 햇빛을 전기로 바꾸는 과정을 설명하는 것이다. B는 p-n 접합의 전기장이 햇빛으로 풀려난 전자를 한 방향으로 밀어 전류를 만든다는 마지막 메모를 활용하므로 정답이다. A는 실리콘 재료와 전도성만 말할 뿐 전기 생성 과정을 설명하지 않는다. C는 도핑 방법만 소개하고 햇빛이나 전류는 언급하지 않는다. D는 여분의 전자가 햇빛이 아니라 인 도핑에서 생긴다는 메모와 어긋나는 부정확한 진술이다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to explain how a solar cell turns sunlight into electricity. B does this by using the last note: the electric field at the p-n junction pushes electrons freed by sunlight in one direction, which produces a current. A only describes the material and how well it conducts, so it never explains how electricity is made. C only explains doping and says nothing about sunlight or current. D is inaccurate, because the notes say extra electrons come from adding phosphorus, not from sunlight.

hardJudge.note: 정답 B는 마지막 메모(p-n 접합 전기장이 햇빛으로 풀려난 전자를 밀어 전류 생성)를 정확히 반영해 '햇빛→전기' 과정을 설명한다. A는 재료·전도성만, C는 도핑만 다루어 목표(전류 생성 과정) 미충족, D는 여분 전자가 햇빛에서 온다고 하고 p-n 접합 형성 순서를 왜곡해 메모와 불일치. 오답들은 메모 내용을 그대로 쓴 것(A, C)이거나 그럴듯한 왜곡(D)으로 전형적 오개념 역할을 한다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어에 한글 없음, 자연스러움. 단서가 메모에 직접 드러나고 한 단계 추론으로 풀리므로 easy 적합. 과학적 사실(인→n형, 붕소→p형, p-n 접합 전기장)도 정확.

advisory.note: 목표와 직접 대응되는 선택지는 B뿐이다. A와 C는 관련은 있지만 목표에서 벗어나 있고, D는 메모 내용을 잘못 옮겼다. 쉬운 난이도에 적합하다.

C does this: it gives the cause (higher-frequency waves weaken faster in soft tissue) and connects it to the result (2 to 5 megahertz is used for deep organs like the liver). A only describes how ultrasound works in general and never mentions frequency. B explains how echoes form, which has nothing to do with choosing a frequency. D defines attenuation but never links it to frequency or to deep organs, so it gives no reason for the choice.

hardJudge.note: C는 원인(고주파 감쇠 빠름)과 결과(2~5MHz로 깊은 장기 검사)를 결합한 유일한 선택지로 정답 확실. A·B·D는 모두 노트의 정확한 재진술이지만 주파수 선택 이유를 제시하지 않아 규칙을 알면 즉시 배제되고, 모르면 그럴듯한 전형적 오답. 한·영 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 의학적 사실(복부 초음파 2~5MHz) 정확. 난이도 easy 적합.

problem.stimulus: In some crystals, electron spins prefer to line up along one particular direction, called the "easy axis." This preference, known as magnetocrystalline anisotropy, makes it hard for an outside magnetic field to turn the spins away ______ materials with strong anisotropy usually have high coercivity and make excellent permanent magnets.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: from that axis, as a result,
from that axis as a result
from that axis, as a result
from that axis. As a result,
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "This preference ... turn the spins away from that axis"와 뒤 "materials with strong anisotropy ... permanent magnets"는 각각 독립절이다. D는 마침표로 두 절을 분리하고 접속부사 "As a result" 뒤에 쉼표를 두므로 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 이어 run-on 문장이 된다. C 역시 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스이다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("This preference ... turn the spins away from that axis") and the words after it ("materials with strong anisotropy ... permanent magnets") are both independent clauses. D is correct because it separates the two clauses with a period and puts a comma after the transition "As a result." A joins the two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B joins them with no punctuation at all, so it is a run-on sentence. C is also a comma splice, since a comma alone can't join two independent clauses.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤가 각각 독립절("...makes it hard ... to turn the spins away from that axis" / "materials with strong anisotropy ... permanent magnets")임을 직접 확인. D만 마침표로 분리하고 접속부사 뒤 쉼표를 두어 옳다. A·C는 쉼표 스플라이스(접속부사는 독립절을 연결할 수 없음), B는 run-on. 해설(한·영) 모두 정답과 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 자기이방성–보자력–영구자석 관계도 사실에 부합. 독립절 경계 규칙 하나로 풀리고 오답은 전형적 오개념(쉼표+접속부사로 연결)이므로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: 독립절 두 개를 접속부사로 잇는 전형적 문항이다. 오답 A·C(쉼표 스플라이스)와 B(run-on)는 규칙을 모르는 학생이 흔히 고르는 오개념이라 easy 난이도에 맞다. 과학 내용(자기결정 이방성과 보자력의 관계)에도 오류가 없다.

problem.stimulus: In a technique known as Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), a donor molecule that has absorbed light can pass its energy to a nearby acceptor molecule instead of glowing itself. This transfer happens only when the two molecules are extremely close, usually less than ten nanometers ______ researchers use FRET signals to tell whether two proteins in a sample are binding to each other.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "This transfer happens only when ... apart"와 빈칸 뒤 "researchers use FRET signals ..."는 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표 등으로 분리해야 하며, B는 마침표로 문장을 끝낸 뒤 접속부사 "As a result,"로 새 문장을 시작하므로 맞다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 스플라이스이다. C는 접속부사 앞에 쉼표만 써서 역시 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. D는 두 절 사이에 아무 경계 표시가 없는 run-on 문장이다.
problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("This transfer happens only when ... apart") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("researchers use FRET signals ..."). Two independent clauses need a proper boundary between them, and B works because it ends the first sentence with a period and then starts a new sentence with "As a result,". A is a comma splice, since a comma alone can't join two independent clauses. C is also a comma splice, because "as a result" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, so the comma before it doesn't fix anything. D is a run-on sentence because there's no boundary at all between the clauses.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞뒤 모두 독립절임을 직접 확인. B(마침표+접속부사)만 올바른 경계. A·C는 쉼표 스플라이스, D는 run-on으로 오답 배제가 명확하며 전형적 오개념(접속부사를 접속사로 착각)을 반영. FRET 10nm 이내 서술도 과학적으로 타당. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스러움.

advisory.note: FRET 거리 약 1–10 nm로 사실관계 정확. 독립절 경계 한 가지 규칙만으로 풀 수 있으며 오답은 전형적인 쉼표 스플라이스/런온 오류임.

problem.stimulus: In electroplating, a thin metal coating forms when dissolved metal ions are reduced at a cathode, the object being plated. The quality of that coating, whether on a gold-plated ring or the copper traces of a circuit board, depends heavily on nucleation, the moment when the first clusters of atoms settle onto the surface. The tiny clusters that appear when a technician raises the current density in a controlled way ______ a finer, smoother layer than the few large crystals produced at low current.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'clusters'이고, 'that appear ... controlled way'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 관계절이다. 따라서 문장에는 복수 주어와 수가 일치하는 정동사가 필요하므로 D 'tend to yield'가 정답이다. A와 C는 정동사이기는 하지만 단수형이어서 관계절 끝의 단수 명사 'way'나 'density'에 잘못 맞춘 것이다. B는 분사일 뿐이라 문장에 정동사가 없게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "clusters," and the long relative clause "that appear ... in a controlled way" just describes it. That means the sentence needs a main verb that agrees with a plural subject, so D, "tend to yield," is correct. A and C are main verbs, but they're singular, so they wrongly match the nearby singular nouns "way" or "density" at the end of the clause. B is only a participle, which would leave the sentence with no main verb at all.

hardJudge.note: 주어 'clusters'(복수)와 긴 관계절 뒤 정동사 수 일치 문제. D만 복수 정동사로 옳음. A·C는 근접 단수 명사(way/density)에 끌리는 오답, B는 비정동사. 한·영 해설 모두 정확하고 일관됨. 전기도금 내용도 사실에 부합. 표준 SAT medium 수준에 적합.

advisory.note: 주어 'clusters'와 동사 사이에 긴 관계절이 끼어 수 일치를 판단해야 하는 전형적인 medium 문항이다. 끼어든 단수 명사(current density, way)가 오답을 유도한다. C의 현재완료 단수형도 시제 문제가 아니라 수 일치 때문에 배제되므로 정답은 D 하나다.

problem.stimulus: Calcite, a transparent form of calcium carbonate, can split a single beam of light into two separate rays. This phenomenon, known as birefringence, occurs because the orderly arrangement of flat carbonate groups within the crystal's stacked atomic layers ______ light differently depending on the direction in which the light is polarized. As a result, a printed word viewed through a clear calcite rhomb appears doubled, a property that nineteenth-century scientists exploited to build some of the first polarizing prisms.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸은 because절의 동사 자리이며, 주어는 'the orderly arrangement'(단수)이다. 'of flat carbonate groups within the crystal's stacked atomic layers'는 주어를 꾸미는 긴 수식어구일 뿐이므로 단수 동사 A 'slows'가 맞다. B 'slow'는 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'layers'나 'groups'에 맞춘 것이라 주어-동사 일치가 틀린다. C 'slowing'과 D 'to slow'는 정동사가 아니어서 because절에 동사가 없게 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The blank needs the main verb of the "because" clause, and that clause's subject is the singular noun "arrangement." The long phrase "of flat carbonate groups within the crystal's stacked atomic layers" only modifies the subject, so the singular verb in A, "slows," is correct. B, "slow," agrees with the nearby plural nouns "groups" or "layers" instead of the real subject. C, "slowing," and D, "to slow," aren't finite verbs, so with either one the clause would have no main verb.

hardJudge.note: because절의 주어 'the orderly arrangement'(단수)에 맞는 정동사는 'slows'로 A가 정답임을 직접 확인. 중간에 'groups', 'layers' 등 복수 명사가 끼어 있어 B가 강한 유인 오답으로 작동하고, C는 분사처럼 보여 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯하며 D도 문법적 형태로 말이 됨. 방해석의 복굴절(탄산염 평면 구조 기인), 19세기 니콜 프리즘 등 사실 관계 문제 없음. 한·영 해설 모두 결론과 선택지 참조가 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 난이도 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 주어와 동사 사이에 긴 수식어구가 끼어 있고, 단수 주어 arrangement 뒤에 복수 명사 groups와 layers가 미끼로 놓여 있다. 그래서 훑어 읽으면 B를 고르기 쉽고, 문장 구조를 파악한 뒤 수 일치까지 확인하는 두 단계 판단이 필요하다. C와 D는 정동사가 아니어서 비교적 쉽게 지워지지만, 이 유형에서는 흔한 구성이다. 복굴절에 관한 과학적 설명(편광 방향에 따라 굴절률이 다르고, 니콜 프리즘을 만드는 데 쓰였다는 점)은 정확하다.

problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 "The formation"이고, "of these ordered clusters"와 "which ... warmer water" 절은 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 문장에는 단수 정동사가 필요하므로 B "causes"가 정답이다. problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The formation." The phrase "of these ordered clusters" and the clause "which ... warmer water" only modify that subject. So the sentence needs a singular main verb, which makes B, "causes," the correct answer. A, "cause," is a main verb, but it's plural: it agrees with the nearby plural nouns "clusters" and "molecules," not with the actual subject. C, "causing," and D, "having caused," are participles, so neither one can work as the main verb, and the sentence is left incomplete.

hardJudge.note: 주어 "The formation"(단수)과 동사 사이에 "of these ordered clusters" 및 "which ... warmer water" 관계절이 끼어 있어 복수 명사(clusters, molecules)에 이끌릴 수 있는 전형적 medium 수일치 문항. B "causes"가 유일한 단수 정동사로 정답 확인. advisory.note: 주어 'The formation'과 동사 사이에 전치사구와 관계절이 끼어 있어, 바로 앞 복수 명사(clusters, molecules)에 이끌려 A를 고르기 쉽다. 정동사인지 판단하고 수 일치까지 확인하는 두 단계가 필요하므로 medium에 적합하다. 물이 4°C 부근에서 밀도가 가장 높고 그 아래에서는 수소결합 네트워크 때문에 팽창한다는 과학적 서술은 사실에 맞다.

problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence gives an advantage of clay's fine pores: they lift water higher. The next sentence gives a drawback of that same narrowness: water flows slowly. This is a concession followed by a reversal, so A is correct. B is tempting because narrowness does cause the slow flow, but the slowness is not a result of the higher lift described just before. C fails because the two effects of narrow pores contrast with each other instead of matching. D fails because the second sentence presents an opposing trait, not an example of the first claim.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(미세 공극 → 더 높은 모세관 상승, 장점)과 뒷 문장(같은 좁음 → 점성 저항으로 느린 흐름, 단점)은 양보·대조 관계이므로 'Even so'가 가장 논리적임. B는 '좁음이 원인'이라는 점에서 부분적으로 그럴듯하나 느린 흐름이 '더 높은 상승'의 결과가 아니므로 배제되고, C는 같은 원인의 두 효과를 다루지만 방향이 상반되어 배제됨. D도 문맥상 말이 됨(사례 제시 형태)이나 내용이 반대 특성이라 틀림. 모세관 현상 관련 과학적 내용(점토가 더 높이 올리나 투수성이 낮아 느림) 정확함. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 A를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치. 표준 SAT medium 수준에 적합.

advisory.note: 앞 문장은 장점, 뒷 문장은 같은 원인에서 오는 단점이라 양보 전환어 'Even so'가 맞다. B(인과)는 '같은 좁음'이라는 단서 때문에 그럴듯한 오답이다. C는 '같은 성질'에 끌려 고를 수 있다. 과학적 내용(모세관 상승 높이와 투수성의 상충 관계)도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
When sunlight strikes a silicon solar cell, the absorbed energy frees electrons almost immediately, so charges can flow to the electrodes with little extra help. In the carbon-based materials used in organic photovoltaic devices, however, photoexcitation produces excitons: an excited electron and the positive "hole" it leaves behind, held together by a strong mutual attraction that ordinary room-temperature energy cannot overcome. ______ a device made from a single organic material yields very little current, and researchers instead blend two materials whose interface pulls each exciton's electron and hole apart.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When sunlight strikes a silicon solar cell, the absorbed energy frees electrons almost immediately, so charges can flow to the electrodes with little extra help. In the carbon-based materials used in organic photovoltaic devices, however, photoexcitation produces excitons: an excited electron and the positive "hole" it leaves behind, held together by a strong mutual attraction that ordinary room-temperature energy cannot overcome. ______ a device made from a single organic material yields very little current, and researchers instead blend two materials whose interface pulls each exciton's electron and hole apart.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 유기 반도체에서 빛이 강하게 결합된 엑시톤을 만들고, 상온의 에너지로는 이를 분리할 수 없다고 말한다. 뒤 문장의 '단일 재료 소자는 전류가 거의 없고, 그래서 두 재료를 섞는다'는 그 결과이므로 C가 정답이다. A는 지문 앞부분의 실리콘 대 유기물 대비에 끌리게 하는 오답이지만, 빈칸 앞뒤 문장은 서로 대조되지 않는다. B는 강한 결합에도 불구하고 무언가가 일어난다는 뜻인데, 낮은 전류는 결합 때문에 생긴 예상된 결과이다. D는 앞 문장과 비슷한 다른 사례를 덧붙일 때 쓰지만, 뒤 문장은 비슷한 현상이 아니라 결과를 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank says that light in organic semiconductors creates tightly bound excitons that room-temperature energy cannot separate. The sentence after it says a single-material device gives little current and that researchers therefore blend two materials. That is a result of the binding problem, so C is correct. A may tempt you because the passage contrasts silicon with organic materials earlier, but the two sentences around the blank do not contrast with each other. B suggests that something happens despite the strong binding, yet the low current is the expected outcome of that binding. D would add a parallel example, but the second sentence describes a consequence, not a similar case.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 문장(엑시톤이 강하게 결합되어 상온 에너지로 분리 불가)과 뒤 문장(단일 재료 소자의 낮은 전류 → 두 재료 혼합)은 원인-결과 관계이므로 C 'Consequently'가 유일한 정답. A는 지문 초반의 실리콘/유기물 대비 때문에 매력적인 오답이며, B도 표면적으로 그럴듯해 비교가 필요함. D는 말이 되는 수준의 오답. 해설(한/영)은 결론·글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 엑시톤·OPV 벌크 헤테로접합 관련 과학적 내용도 정확. 전체 지문 맥락과 국소 문장 관계를 구분해야 하는 두 단계 판단이 요구되어 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 인과 관계가 분명하다(결합을 깰 수 없음 → 전류가 낮음). A는 앞부분의 실리콘 대 유기물 대비를 이용한 그럴듯한 함정이고, B도 정답 자리를 판별해야 배제된다. 중간 난이도로 적절하다.

problem.passage:
When certain materials are cooled below a critical temperature, their electrical resistance drops to zero, allowing current to circulate indefinitely without losing energy. Early researchers assumed that such a material was simply a "perfect conductor," an ordinary metal with its resistance removed. A perfect conductor, however, would merely trap whatever magnetic field was already inside it at the moment of cooling. In 1933, Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld found that a superconductor does something different: it actively pushes an existing magnetic field out of its interior as it crosses the critical temperature. ______ superconductivity came to be understood as a distinct state of matter rather than just an extreme case of high conductivity.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: When certain materials are cooled below a critical temperature, their electrical resistance drops to zero, allowing current to circulate indefinitely without losing energy. Early researchers assumed that such a material was simply a "perfect conductor," an ordinary metal with its resistance removed. A perfect conductor, however, would merely trap whatever magnetic field was already inside it at the moment of cooling. In 1933, Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld found that a superconductor does something different: it actively pushes an existing magnetic field out of its interior as it crosses the critical temperature. ______ superconductivity came to be understood as a distinct state of matter rather than just an extreme case of high conductivity.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 초전도체가 완전 도체와 달리 자기장을 밀어낸다는 발견을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그 발견 때문에 초전도성이 별개의 물질 상태로 이해되었다는 결과를 말하므로 인과 관계인 D가 정답이다. A는 지문에 '가정 vs 발견'의 대조가 있어 그럴듯하지만, 마지막 문장은 발견과 반대되는 내용이 아니라 발견에서 나온 결론이다. B는 마지막 문장이 앞 내용의 구체적 예시가 아니라 일반화된 결론이므로 맞지 않다. C는 두 문장이 유사한 별개의 사례를 나열하는 관계가 아니므로 배제된다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence reports the discovery that a superconductor actively expels a magnetic field, unlike a perfect conductor. The final sentence gives the consequence: because of that, superconductivity was seen as a distinct state of matter, so D, a cause-effect transition, is correct. A might seem tempting because the passage does contrast an early assumption with a later finding, but the final sentence isn't opposed to the discovery; it follows from it. B doesn't work because the last sentence is a broad conclusion, not a specific example. C doesn't fit because the sentence doesn't give a second, parallel case.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검산 완료: 앞 문장(마이스너 효과 발견) → 뒤 문장(초전도성을 별개의 물질 상태로 이해)은 명확한 인과 관계. 1933년 Meissner·Ochsenfeld 발견, 완전 도체가 기존 자기장을 가둔다는 설명 모두 사실에 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 난이도: 지문 전반의 '가정 vs 발견' 대조 구조 때문에 A(Nevertheless)가 훑어 읽는 학생에게 강한 매력 오답으로 작동하며, 마지막 문장이 '결론'임을 정독해야 D가 확정되므로 medium에 부합. 다만 B·C는 매력도가 다소 낮아 상위 medium보다는 중하 수준에 가까움(판정에는 영향 없음).

advisory.note: 마이스너 효과 관련 사실 기술이 정확하다. 정답은 인과 관계의 연결어다. 오답 A는 가정과 발견의 대조 때문에 그럴듯하게 보이는 오답으로 기능한다. 다만 B와 C는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다. 중간 난이도에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Graphene, a sheet of carbon atoms bonded in a hexagonal honeycomb pattern and measuring just one atom ______ conducts electricity more efficiently than copper at room temperature. Researchers at the University of Manchester, who first isolated the material in 2004, also found it to be roughly two hundred times stronger than steel by weight.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Graphene, a sheet of carbon atoms bonded in a hexagonal honeycomb pattern and measuring just one atom ______ conducts electricity more efficiently than copper at room temperature. Researchers at the University of Manchester, who first isolated the material in 2004, also found it to be roughly two hundred times stronger than steel by weight.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: "a sheet of ... one atom thick"는 주어 Graphene을 설명하는 비필수 동격구이며, 쉼표로 시작했으므로 같은 쉼표로 닫아야 동사 conducts로 이어진다. 그래서 C가 정답이다. A는 세미콜론이 주어와 동사를 갈라놓아 앞부분이 독립절이 되지 못한다. B는 동격구를 닫는 문장부호가 없어서 삽입구가 끝나는 지점이 불분명하다. D의 대시도 삽입구를 닫을 수 있지만, 이 삽입구는 쉼표로 열렸으므로 문장부호가 짝을 이루지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The phrase "a sheet of ... one atom thick" is a nonessential appositive describing the subject, Graphene. It opens with a comma, so it has to close with a comma before the verb "conducts." That makes C correct. A puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, but the words before it aren't an independent clause. B leaves the appositive unclosed, so it's unclear where the interruption ends. D uses a dash, which can close an interruption, but this one opened with a comma, so the punctuation doesn't match.

hardJudge.note: 주어 Graphene 뒤 쉼표로 열린 긴 동격구를 쉼표로 닫고 동사 conducts로 이어가는 구조. C만 짝을 이룬 문장부호. A는 세미콜론 앞이 독립절이 아니고, B는 삽입구 미종결, D는 대시가 쉼표와 짝이 맞지 않음. 해설(한·영) 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 그래핀 사실 관계(2004년 맨체스터 분리, 강도·전도성 비교)도 통상적 서술과 부합. 긴 삽입구 추적 + 여는 부호 확인의 두 단계 판단이 필요하고 A·D가 부분적으로 그럴듯해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구로 주어-동사 사이 거리를 벌려 훑어 읽기 오답(B)을 유도함. D는 짝 불일치로 배제해야 하므로 비교가 필요함. medium에 적합함.

problem.passage:
Thermochromic liquid crystals, compounds whose twisted, helical molecular arrangement tightens or loosens as temperature shifts, reflect different wavelengths of light at different temperatures______ a thin film of these crystals that looks red at 30°C may appear blue only a few degrees higher, a property engineers exploit to map heat across circuit boards and turbine blades.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Thermochromic liquid crystals, compounds whose twisted, helical molecular arrangement tightens or loosens as temperature shifts, reflect different wavelengths of light at different temperatures______ a thin film of these crystals that looks red at 30°C may appear blue only a few degrees higher, a property engineers exploit to map heat across circuit boards and turbine blades.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 주어 Thermochromic liquid crystals와 동사 reflect는 하나의 독립절을 이루고, 빈칸 뒤 a thin film ... may appear blue도 독립절이다. consequently는 접속사가 아니라 접속부사이므로 두 독립절을 이으려면 앞에 세미콜론, 뒤에 쉼표가 필요하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어서 comma splice가 된다. B는 부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. C는 세미콜론이 consequently 뒤에 놓여 접속부사가 앞 절에 붙어 버리므로 논리적 연결이 어색하고 관례에도 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Look past the long appositive: the subject "Thermochromic liquid crystals" and the verb "reflect" form a complete independent clause, and "a thin film ... may appear blue" after the blank is another independent clause. Because "consequently" is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction, joining two independent clauses with it requires a semicolon before it and a comma after it, so D is correct. A joins the clauses with only a comma, creating a comma splice. B uses no punctuation, creating a run-on sentence. C puts the semicolon after "consequently," attaching the transition to the first clause instead of introducing the result in the second.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞(긴 동격구를 포함한 주어 + reflect)과 뒤(a thin film ... may appear blue) 모두 독립절이며, 접속부사 consequently로 연결하려면 '; consequently,'가 필요하므로 D 정답 확인. A는 comma splice, B는 run-on, C는 세미콜론이 접속부사 뒤에 와 전환어가 앞 절에 붙는 비관례적 구조. 해설(한·영) 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조로 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 열변색 액정이 저온에서 적색, 고온에서 청색으로 변하는 서술도 사실에 부합. 긴 동격구로 절 경계를 숨기고 마지막 'a property engineers exploit' 동격구가 추가 혼란 요소로 작용해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 문장 앞부분의 긴 동격구 때문에 주절을 찾는 단계가 하나 더 필요하다. A와 C는 그럴듯한 오답이어서 표준 medium 수준의 접속부사 문항으로 적합하다.

problem.passage:
Nitinol, a nickel-titanium alloy that can be bent into a new shape at room temperature and will hold that shape indefinitely, behaves unusually when it is gently warmed ______ its crystal structure shifts from the low-temperature martensite phase back to the austenite phase, and the deformed wire springs back to its original form.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Nitinol, a nickel-titanium alloy that can be bent into a new shape at room temperature and will hold that shape indefinitely, behaves unusually when it is gently warmed ______ its crystal structure shifts from the low-temperature martensite phase back to the austenite phase, and the deformed wire springs back to its original form.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Nitinol ... behaves unusually when it is gently warmed'는 동격구가 길게 들어가 있어도 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'its crystal structure shifts ...'도 독립절이다. 뒤 절은 앞에서 말한 '특이한 거동'이 무엇인지 구체적으로 설명하므로, 독립절 뒤에 설명을 이어 주는 콜론을 쓴 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속 오류가 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 'and'를 붙였는데, 세미콜론은 그 자체로 두 절을 잇기 때문에 등위접속사가 필요 없으므로 관례에 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Even with the long appositive in the middle, "Nitinol ... behaves unusually when it is gently warmed" is a complete independent clause, and "its crystal structure shifts ..." is also an independent clause. The second clause explains what the "unusual" behavior actually is, so a colon, which joins an independent clause to an explanation that follows, works perfectly here. That makes D correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, so it's a run-on sentence. C adds "and" after a semicolon, but a semicolon already joins the clauses on its own, so the conjunction doesn't belong there under standard conventions.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞 'Nitinol ... behaves unusually when it is gently warmed'는 독립절, 뒤 'its crystal structure shifts ...'도 독립절이며 뒤 절이 앞의 '특이한 거동'을 설명하므로 콜론(D)이 정답으로 성립. A 쉼표 접속 오류, B 무종지문은 명확한 오답. 니티놀의 마르텐사이트→오스테나이트 전이 및 형상기억 서술은 사실에 부합. 다만 유의점: C ';' + 'and'는 SAT 관례상 오답으로 처리되지만, 뒤 절에 내부 쉼표(', and the deformed wire ...')가 있어 일부 스타일 가이드(Chicago 등)에서는 세미콜론+등위접속사가 허용되는 상황이라 논쟁 여지가 약간 있음. 정답 판정 자체는 유지되나 변별력 측면에서 참고. 난이도는 긴 동격구로 독립절 판단을 흐리게 하고 콜론 용법 확인이 필요해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 동격구 때문에 앞부분이 독립절인지 판단하는 단계와, 뒤 절이 '특이한 거동'을 설명하는지 확인하는 단계가 모두 필요해 medium에 맞음. C의 '; and'를 오답으로 보는 것은 SAT 관례와 일치함. 사실 관계(마텐자이트에서 오스테나이트로의 상변태와 형상 기억)에도 문제 없음.

problem.stimulus: Ferrofluids, liquids containing nanoscale iron oxide particles coated with a surfactant that keeps them from clumping, behave like ordinary oils until a magnet is brought near. When a current passes through the damper's coil, the suspended particles align into chains along the magnetic field ______ the fluid thickens within milliseconds, allowing the damper to absorb sudden vibrations.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞뒤는 각각 독립절이므로 쉼표+등위접속사 and로 연결해야 하고, 뒤따르는 도입 부사구 as a result 뒤에는 쉼표가 와야 한다. A는 두 조건을 모두 충족한다. B는 and 뒤에 쉼표를 두고 as a result 뒤 쉼표를 빼서 삽입구를 한쪽만 닫아 오류다. C는 두 독립절을 잇는 and 앞 쉼표가 없다. D는 접속사 없이 쉼표만으로 독립절을 이어 쉼표 접속(comma splice)이 된다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before and after the blank is an independent clause on each side, so you need a comma plus the coordinating conjunction "and" to join them, and the introductory phrase "as a result" that starts the second clause should be followed by a comma. Choice A does both. Choice B puts a comma after "and" but leaves out the comma after "as a result," so the interrupting phrase is set off on only one side. Choice C leaves out the comma before "and" that should come between the two independent clauses. Choice D joins the clauses with commas only and no conjunction, which makes a comma splice.

hardJudge.note: 빈칸 앞("the suspended particles align into chains along the magnetic field lines")과 뒤("the fluid thickens within milliseconds...")는 모두 독립절. A는 쉼표+and로 연결하고 도입구 "as a result" 뒤에 쉼표를 두어 올바름. B는 "and," 뒤 쉼표가 있으나 "as a result" 뒤 쉼표가 없어 삽입구 처리가 불균형. C는 독립절 사이 and 앞 쉼표 누락. D는 접속사 없는 쉼표 접속. 해설(한/영) 모두 정답과 일치하고 글자 참조 정확, 영어 자연스러움. 페로플루이드·MR 댐퍼 관련 사실 설명도 정확. 두 단계 판단(독립절 식별 + 부사구 구두점)이 필요하며 B·C가 부분적으로 그럴듯해 medium에 적합.

advisory.note: C의 오답 근거(독립절을 잇는 and 앞 쉼표 누락)는 SAT 관례상 받아들일 수 있다. B와 D는 오류가 분명하다. 지문의 과학적 서술도 정확하다.

problem.passage:
