problem.passage:
Flexoelectricity is the generation of electric polarization by a strain gradient, as when a material is bent so that one surface is stretched while the opposite surface is compressed. Unlike ordinary piezoelectricity, which responds to uniform strain, flexoelectric output depends on how sharply strain changes across a material's thickness, and because bending a thinner film produces a steeper gradient, the effect should grow stronger as films get thinner. Materials engineer Hana Okafor and colleagues built bending sensors from ultrathin films of a polymer that is only weakly piezoelectric. They argue that in their thinnest films, the voltage the sensors produce comes mainly from flexoelectricity rather than from the polymer's piezoelectric response.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor and colleagues' argument?
problem.stimulus: Flexoelectricity is the generation of electric polarization by a strain gradient, as when a material is bent so that one surface is stretched while the opposite surface is compressed. Unlike ordinary piezoelectricity, which responds to uniform strain, flexoelectric output depends on how sharply strain changes across a material's thickness, and because bending a thinner film produces a steeper gradient, the effect should grow stronger as films get thinner. Materials engineer Hana Okafor and colleagues built bending sensors from ultrathin films of a polymer that is only weakly piezoelectric. They argue that in their thinnest films, the voltage the sensors produce comes mainly from flexoelectricity rather than from the polymer's piezoelectric response.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor and colleagues' argument?
options: Under the same bending, the sensors' voltage output stayed roughly the same whether the films were 500 nanometers or 50 nanometers thick.
When the films were stretched uniformly along their length without being bent, the sensors produced a small but measurable voltage.
Sensors made from a strongly piezoelectric ceramic produced more voltage under bending than the polymer sensors did at every film thickness tested.

As film thickness was reduced from 500 nanometers to 50 nanometers under the same bending, voltage output per unit of applied bending rose sharply, while output under uniform stretching stayed nearly constant.
problem.explanation: 이 주장은 가장 얇은 필름에서 나오는 전압이 주로 압전 효과가 아니라 굴곡 전기(flexoelectricity)에서 온다는 것이다. 굴곡 전기는 변형 기울기에 반응하므로 필름이 얇아질수록 강해져야 하고, 균일한 변형에 반응하는 압전 효과는 두께와 상관없이 비슷해야 한다. D는 굽힘에 대한 출력은 두께가 줄수록 크게 늘었지만 균일 인장에 대한 출력은 거의 그대로였음을 보여 주므로, 늘어난 출력이 굴곡 전기에서 왔다는 것을 직접 뒷받침한다. A는 두께에 따라 출력이 변하지 않았다는 결과이므로 오히려 주장을 약화한다. B는 압전 반응이 존재한다는 것만 보여 줄 뿐 어느 효과가 주도하는지는 알려 주지 않고, C는 이 고분자 안에서 두 효과를 비교하지 않으므로 관련이 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The claim is that in the thinnest films, the voltage comes mainly from flexoelectricity rather than piezoelectricity. Flexoelectricity responds to strain gradients, so it should get stronger as films get thinner. Piezoelectricity responds to uniform strain, so it should stay about the same at any thickness. D shows that the bending output rose sharply as the films got thinner while the output from uniform stretching barely changed, which points directly to flexoelectricity as the source of the extra voltage. A actually weakens the claim, since the output didn't change with thickness. B only shows that some piezoelectric response exists, not which effect dominates. C compares the polymer to a different material, so it says nothing about the two effects inside the polymer.

quality.seed: technology and engineering — Flexoelectric effect mechanical bending strain and electric polarization in ultrathin polymer piezoelectric sensor devices

hardJudge.note: 정답 D 검증: 지문 논리(굴곡전기는 두께 감소 시 강화, 압전은 균일 변형에 반응)에 따라 '굽힘 출력 급증 + 균일 인장 출력 불변'은 주장을 직접 뒷받침함. A는 반대 결과(약화), B는 압전 존재만 입증, C는 타 재료 비교로 무관. 두 조건(굽힘 변화 vs. 인장 불변)을 연결해야 하므로 medium 적합. 다만 정답 선택지가 가장 길고 지문 논리를 거의 그대로 반영해 다소 쉬운 편(경계선). 해설 한·영 일치, 영어 자연스러움, 한글 혼입 없음, 사실 오류 없음.

advisory.note: 정답 D는 두 가지(두께에 따른 굽힘 출력 증가, 균일 인장 출력 일정)를 연결해야 하므로 medium 수준의 2단계 판단에 해당한다. 다만 D만 유독 길고 상세해서 길이 단서가 될 수 있다. A는 반대 결과, B·C는 그럴듯하지만 관련성이 부족해 오답 비교는 적절하다.

problem.passage:
Thermoelectric generators convert heat directly into electricity through the Seebeck effect: when one side of a semiconductor junction is hotter than the other, charge carriers drift from the hot side toward the cold side, producing a voltage. Engineers have proposed attaching such modules to factory exhaust pipes to recover waste heat. Materials scientist Lena Okafor argues, however, that in many industrial installations the main limit on power output is not the semiconductor material itself but the heat sink on the cold side. Because heat flows through the module continuously, she contends, a poorly cooled cold side warms up until the temperature difference across the junction shrinks, and the voltage falls with it.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's claim?

Engineers have proposed attaching such modules to factory exhaust pipes to recover waste heat. Materials scientist Lena Okafor argues, however, that in many industrial installations the main limit on power output is not the semiconductor material itself but the heat sink on the cold side. Because heat flows through the module continuously, she contends, a poorly cooled cold side warms up until the temperature difference across the junction shrinks, and the voltage falls with it.
problem.question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's claim?
options: When identical modules on the same exhaust pipe were fitted with larger fins on the side away from the pipe, the gap in temperature between their two faces grew and their power output rose substantially.
When modules made of a newer semiconductor alloy replaced older modules on the same exhaust pipe, their power output rose substantially even though the cooling hardware was unchanged.
When identical modules were placed on exhaust pipes carrying hotter gas, the temperature of the face touching the pipe rose and the modules produced more voltage than those on cooler pipes.
When identical modules on the same exhaust pipe were fitted with larger fins on the side away from the pipe, the factory's overall energy costs declined over the following year.
problem.explanation: Okafor는 출력의 주된 한계가 반도체 재료가 아니라 냉각 측 방열에 있다고 주장한다. A는 같은 모듈에서 냉각 측 방열만 개선했더니 온도차가 커지고 출력이 늘었다는 것으로, 주장의 인과 고리 전체를 직접 뒷받침한다. B는 재료를 바꿔 출력이 늘었다는 것이므로 오히려 재료가 한계라는 쪽을 시사해 주장을 약화한다. C는 온도차가 클수록 전압이 높다는 일반 원리만 보여 줄 뿐 냉각 측이 한계라는 점과는 관련이 없다. D는 같은 개입이지만 공장 전체 에너지 비용은 다른 요인에도 좌우되므로 모듈 출력이나 온도차에 관해 직접 알려 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Okafor claims that the main limit on output is the cold-side heat sink, not the semiconductor material. Choice A changes only the cooling on identical modules and shows that the temperature difference grew and power rose, which confirms every link in her reasoning. Choice B shows that changing the material raised output, which suggests the material is the limit, so it actually weakens her claim. Choice C only confirms the general rule that a bigger temperature difference gives more voltage; it says nothing about the cold side being the bottleneck. Choice D uses the same fix, but a factory's overall energy costs depend on many other factors, so it tells you nothing direct about the modules' output or temperature difference.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Engineers have long relied on strain gauges glued to steel bridge girders to detect dangerous loads. Researchers now propose exploiting magnetostriction instead: when a ferromagnetic material such as structural steel is stressed, its internal magnetic domains shift, measurably altering the field around it. Because the girder itself becomes the sensor, proponents argue, bridges could be monitored continuously without attaching fragile gauges that peel or corrode, making the approach ready to replace conventional methods on existing spans.

Text 2
Field trials of magnetostrictive monitoring on older steel bridges have produced encouraging but uneven results. The magnetic signal does track stress, yet it also drifts with temperature and with the steel's prior loading history, so identical stresses can yield different readings on cold and warm days or before and after a heavy truck passes. Until engineers can separate these influences, the method is best treated as a supplement to established gauges rather than a substitute for them.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the proponents' conclusion described in Text 1?

For much of the twentieth century, connoisseurs judged paintings from Pietro Perugino's workshop by asking a single question: which panels did the master paint himself? Works with less refined faces or stiffer drapery were often set aside as "school pieces" and treated as lesser objects. Recent technical studies, however, have complicated this approach. Infrared imaging of several altarpieces shows that Perugino frequently drew the underlying design himself, while assistants carried out large areas of the painting, sometimes reusing the same cartoon for figures in different commissions.

Art historian Giulia Ferrante argues that these findings make the old question misleading. Because contracts of the period usually named Perugino as responsible for a work's overall design and quality rather than for every brushstroke, she contends, a panel painted largely by assistants could still be a fully legitimate "Perugino" by the standards of his clients. Scholars, in her view, should therefore study how tasks were divided within the workshop rather than sort paintings into authentic and inauthentic categories.

For centuries, the glassmakers of Murano, an island in the Venetian lagoon, have passed on their craft through long apprenticeships in which a novice may spend years merely fetching tools and tending the furnace before being allowed to shape molten glass. Yet master glassblowers argue that the waiting period is itself the lesson: by watching the furnace for thousands of hours, apprentices learn to judge the temperature and workability of glass from its color and the way it moves on the pipe, knowledge that no written manual has managed to capture. Recently, several Murano workshops experimented with shortening apprenticeships by teaching techniques in classroom courses. Trainees from these programs mastered individual steps quickly, but masters reported that they struggled to adjust when a batch of glass behaved unexpectedly, a skill that apprentices trained in the traditional way seemed to develop almost without noticing.

B gives only the view of some observers, which the author pushes back on with "Yet." C goes against the text's statement that no manual has captured this knowledge, and the author never says the apprenticeships could be replaced. D gets one detail right, since trainees did learn individual steps quickly, but the text concludes that this wasn't enough.

B는 지문에 등장하는 견해지만 저자 입장이 아니고, D는 세부 사실(개별 단계 빠른 습득)은 맞지만 결론을 뒤집으며, C는 '어떤 매뉴얼도 담지 못했다'와 충돌. 두 단계 판단(저자 vs 관찰자 구분 + 실험 결과 연결) 필요하여 medium 적합. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 글자와 일치하고 모순 없음. 무라노 유리공예 견습 전통은 실재하며 실험 내용은 SAT식 서술 범위 내로 사실 오류로 보지 않음.

advisory.note: B, C, D 모두 지문의 세부(길드 관습, 문서화되지 않은 지식, 개별 단계를 빨리 익힘)를 근거로 삼고 있어 정독해서 비교해야 배제됨. A의 'so far'는 'recently experimented'와 잘 맞음. 중간 난이도로 적절함.

problem.passage:
In salt-glazing, potters do not coat stoneware with a prepared liquid glaze before firing. Instead, when the kiln reaches roughly 1,200°C, they throw ordinary salt into the firebox, where it vaporizes and the sodium reacts with silica in the clay surface to form a thin glassy layer. Because the vapor settles unevenly, beading in some places and thinning in others, the finished surface often shows a pitted, dimpled texture known as "orange peel." Many collectors prize this texture as a sign of authentic salt firing. ______ some contemporary potters deliberately avoid it, adjusting the amount and timing of the salt so that their pots come out with a smoother, more uniform sheen.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank says collectors value the orange-peel texture as a sign of authentic salt firing. The final sentence says some potters avoid that texture on purpose. A trait is valued, yet some people reject it, so this is a concession followed by a contrast, and B is correct. A would mean the collectors' preference causes potters to avoid the texture, which gets the cause and effect backward. C would make the last sentence a restatement of the one before it, but the two sentences describe opposite attitudes. D says the attitudes are alike, when in fact they contrast.

advisory.note: '높이 평가된다'와 '일부러 피한다'의 대조가 분명해서 B가 명확한 정답이다. 대조 선택지가 하나뿐이라 medium 중에서도 쉬운 쪽에 가깝지만, A(For this reason)는 훑어 읽으면 그럴듯해 보이는 오답이라 medium으로 허용 가능하다. 소금유 소성 온도와 오렌지 껍질 질감에 대한 서술은 사실과 맞는다.

problem.passage:
Nigerian potter Ladi Kwali grew up in the Gbari village of Kwali, where women built large water jars by coiling ropes of clay and smoothing the surfaces by hand. In 1954 she joined the Abuja Pottery Training Centre, where she was trained to throw vessels on a potter's wheel and to fire them at high temperatures with glazes. ______ the pieces that made her internationally famous were not wheel-thrown: she kept coiling her jars by hand, bringing traditional Gbari forms into the new stoneware clay and carving them with images of lizards, fish, and scorpions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Nigerian potter Ladi Kwali grew up in the Gbari village of Kwali, where women built large water jars by coiling ropes of clay and smoothing the surfaces by hand. In 1954 she joined the Abuja Pottery Training Centre, where she was trained to throw vessels on a potter's wheel and to fire them at high temperatures with glazes. ______ the pieces that made her internationally famous were not wheel-thrown: she kept coiling her jars by hand, bringing traditional Gbari forms into the new stoneware clay and carving them with images of lizards, fish, and scorpions.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 Kwali가 Abuja에서 물레 성형 기술을 배웠다고 말하고, 뒤 문장은 그런데도 그녀의 대표작이 물레가 아니라 손으로 코일을 쌓아 만든 것이었다고 말한다. 이는 앞의 내용에서 예상되는 결과를 뒤집는 양보 후 반전 관계이므로 C가 정답이다. B는 훈련이 명성으로 이어졌다는 인과로 읽힐 수 있지만, 뒤 문장은 훈련받은 기술을 쓰지 않았다는 내용이라 결과가 될 수 없다. A는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 사례로 만들지만 뒤 문장은 앞 내용과 대비된다. D는 단순 추가를 나타내므로 두 문장 사이의 대조를 놓친다.
problem.explanationEn: The first sentence says that Kwali was trained at Abuja to throw pots on a wheel. The next sentence says that her most famous pieces were still coiled by hand instead. That reverses what the training would lead you to expect, so you need a contrast transition, and C is correct. B is tempting because her training might seem to explain her fame, but the second sentence describes her not using the wheel technique, so it can't be a result of learning it. A would make the second sentence an example of the first, but the two sentences actually contrast with each other. D just adds information and misses the contrast completely.

hardJudge.note: 앞 문장(물레 성형 훈련)과 뒤 문장(대표작은 물레가 아닌 손 코일링)의 반전 관계가 명확하여 C 'Nevertheless'가 유일한 정답. 해설 한·영 모두 동일 결론·글자 참조, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 'were not wheel-thrown'이 다소 강한 단서라 medium 하한에 가깝지만 두 문장 연결 판단이 필요해 목표 난이도에 적합.

advisory.note: Ladi Kwali의 Abuja Pottery Training Centre(1954, Michael Cardew) 경력과 손으로 코일을 쌓는 기법 유지는 사실과 맞다. 대조 관계는 문장 뒤쪽의 'were not wheel-thrown' 단서를 읽어야 확인된다. 오답들도 그럴듯하게 짜여 있어 B는 인과로 오독하게 만들고 D는 단순 나열처럼 보인다. 다만 A는 비교적 쉽게 배제된다.

problem.passage:
Early critics often dismissed Ruth Asawa's looped-wire sculptures as decorative craft, linking the technique to basket weaving she had observed in Mexico rather than to the ambitions of postwar abstraction. Asawa herself acknowledged that she had learned the looping method from villagers in Toluca. ______ she used that humble technique to pursue a distinctly sculptural problem: by suspending interlocking lobes of wire within one another, she made forms whose inside and outside are visible at the same time, so that the surrounding space becomes part of the work.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.stimulus: Early critics often dismissed Ruth Asawa's looped-wire sculptures as decorative craft, linking the technique to basket weaving she had observed in Mexico rather than to the ambitions of postwar abstraction. Asawa herself acknowledged that she had learned the looping method from villagers in Toluca. ______ she used that humble technique to pursue a distinctly sculptural problem: by suspending interlocking lobes of wire within one another, she made forms whose inside and outside are visible at the same time, so that the surrounding space becomes part of the work.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 Asawa가 멕시코 마을 사람들에게서 기법을 배웠다고 인정했다는 내용으로, 비평가들의 '공예' 평가를 일부 받아들이는 양보에 해당한다. 뒤 문장은 그 소박한 기법으로 본격적인 조각적 문제를 탐구했다고 반전하므로 양보 후 대조를 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 기법을 배운 것이 원인처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 뒤 문장의 핵심은 비평가의 평가를 뒤집는 것이지 그 결과가 아니다. B는 두 문장이 같은 방향의 주장을 한다고 보지만 실제로는 방향이 반대이다. C는 뒤 문장이 기법 습득의 구체적 사례가 아니므로 맞지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The previous sentence is a concession: Asawa admitted she learned the looping method from villagers, which seems to support the critics' view that her work was craft. The next sentence reverses that impression by showing she used the technique to explore a serious sculptural problem, so a concession-then-contrast transition, D, is correct. A is tempting because learning the technique did make the sculptures possible, but the sentence's point is to push back against the critics, not to describe a simple consequence. B wrongly treats the two sentences as making parallel points when they actually pull in opposite directions. C doesn't work because the second sentence isn't an example of her learning the technique.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

problem.explanation: 앞 문장은 방문객들이 곡선을 실용적 목적 없는 장식으로 여긴다는 통념을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 곡선이 실제로는 채광을 위해 설계되었다고 그 통념을 뒤집으므로 통념과 실제를 대비하는 A가 정답이다. B는 뒤 문장에 구체적 세부(타일, 창문)가 나와 그럴듯하지만, 이 세부는 '순수 장식'이라는 견해의 예가 아니라 반박 근거다. C는 방문객의 인식이 공학적 설계의 원인이 될 수 없어 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. D는 두 문장이 비슷한 내용이 아니라 상반된 내용이므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence before the blank gives a common belief: visitors see the curves as pure ornament with little practical purpose. The sentence after the blank overturns that belief by showing the curves were engineered to spread daylight evenly, so A, which sets a misconception against the actual facts, is correct. B looks tempting because specific details (tiles, windows) follow, but those details argue against the "pure ornament" view instead of illustrating it. C doesn't work because visitors' impressions can't have caused Gaudí's engineering, so the cause-and-effect direction is wrong. D is wrong because the two sentences contrast with each other instead of making similar points.

It describes a weakness in Higgins's argument that Fluxus should be treated as a separate movement.
It identifies a difference between two movements that sets up the claim presented in the final sentence.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 시작해 개념미술은 아이디어 자체를 완성작으로 본 반면 플럭서스는 실행을 중시했다는 차이를 제시하고, 마지막 문장은 "For this reason"으로 이 차이에 기대어 Higgins의 주장을 내놓는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 아이디어 중시라는 공통점을 언급하지만, 밑줄 문장은 그 견해를 뒷받침하는 예시가 아니라 오히려 그것을 제한한다. B는 비평가들이 두 운동을 묶은 이유를 말하는데, 그 이유는 앞 문장에 나오고 밑줄 문장은 두 운동을 구분한다. C는 반대로 말한다. 밑줄 문장은 Higgins의 주장을 약화하지 않고 뒷받침한다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence begins with "Yet." It points out that conceptual artists treated the idea as the finished work, while Fluxus needed the score to be performed. The final sentence then starts with "For this reason" and builds Higgins's claim on that difference, so D is correct. A is tempting because it mentions valuing ideas over objects, but the underlined sentence limits that view instead of giving an example that supports it. B describes why critics grouped the two movements, but that reason is in the previous sentence, and the underlined sentence separates the movements. C gets it backward: the sentence supports Higgins's argument rather than pointing out a weakness in it.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Fluxus movement anti-art philosophy and performance-based experimentation challenging conceptual art definition boundaries

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 "Yet"으로 두 운동의 차이를 제시하고, 마지막 문장이 "For this reason"으로 그 차이를 근거로 Higgins의 주장을 전개하므로 D가 정답임을 직접 확인함. A(아이디어 중시 언급)와 B(비평가의 분류 이유)는 지문 요소를 부분적으로 차용해 비교가 필요하고, C는 방향이 반대이나 말이 되는 오답. 두 단계 판단(대조 파악 + 결론과의 연결)이 요구되어 medium에 적합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 결론·글자 참조가 일치하고 영어가 자연스러우며 한글 혼입 없음. George Brecht의 "Exit" 이벤트 스코어, Hannah Higgins의 Fluxus 해석은 실제 사실과 부합하며 지문은 독창적 서술로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: D는 'Yet'으로 제시된 대조와 'For this reason'으로 이어지는 결론을 정확히 짚는다. A와 B는 지문의 일부 내용(아이디어 중시, 비평가들의 분류)에 기대고 있어 부분적인 근거를 가진 오답이다. C는 명백히 반대 방향이라 쉽게 배제되므로 난이도는 medium 범위의 낮은 쪽에 해당한다. Brecht의 'Exit' 카드와 Higgins의 관점(Fluxus Experience)은 사실 관계에 문제가 없다.

problem.passage:
Unlike most plainchant of her era, which tended to move in small steps within a narrow range, the monophonic chants of Hildegard von Bingen, the twelfth-century Benedictine abbess of Rupertsberg, frequently span more than two ______ one antiphon, "O quam mirabilis," rises and plunges so dramatically that the nuns of her convent would have needed exceptional breath control to sing it.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: Unlike most plainchant of her era, which tended to move in small steps within a narrow range, the monophonic chants of Hildegard von Bingen, the twelfth-century Benedictine abbess of Rupertsberg, frequently span more than two ______ one antiphon, "O quam mirabilis," rises and plunges so dramatically that the nuns of her convent would have needed exceptional breath control to sing it.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 긴 삽입구(which절, 동격 the twelfth-century...)를 걷어내면 주절은 "the chants ... frequently span more than two octaves"이고, 빈칸 뒤 "one antiphon ... rises and plunges ..."도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결하고 전환어 in fact 뒤에 쉼표를 두는 A가 맞다. B는 전환어를 쉼표로 감쌌을 뿐 두 독립절을 쉼표만으로 이은 쉼표 오류(comma splice)다. C는 두 독립절 사이에 아무 부호도 없는 무종지문(run-on)이다. D는 which를 넣어 뒷부분을 관계절로 만들려 하지만, 그러면 "one antiphon"이 들어갈 자리가 없어 문장 구조가 깨진다.
problem.explanationEn: If you strip out the long modifiers (the "which" clause and the appositive "the twelfth-century Benedictine abbess of Rupertsberg"), the main clause is "the chants ... frequently span more than two octaves," and the part after the blank, "one antiphon ... rises and plunges ...," is also an independent clause. Choice A is correct because it joins the two independent clauses with a semicolon and puts a comma after the transition "in fact." Choice B sets off "in fact" with commas, but it still joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. Choice C has no punctuation between the clauses at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. Choice D adds "which" to make a relative clause, but then "one antiphon" has no grammatical role, so the sentence falls apart.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 삽입구 제거 시 "the chants ... span more than two octaves" + "one antiphon ... rises and plunges ..." 두 독립절. A(세미콜론 + in fact,)만 적법. B는 comma splice, C는 run-on, D는 which 삽입으로 "one antiphon"의 문법적 역할이 사라짐. 역사 사실(힐데가르트, 12세기 베네딕토회 수녀원장, 루페르츠베르크, 넓은 음역, 안티폰 "O quam mirabilis")도 타당. 해설 한/영 일치, 글자 참조 정확, 한글 혼입 없음. 긴 수식어구로 주절 식별 단계가 필요하고 B·D가 그럴듯해 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 긴 삽입 수식어 때문에 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, B와 D가 그럴듯한 오답이라 medium에 맞음. 사실 관계: Hildegard의 성가가 '자주' 두 옥타브를 넘는다는 서술은 다소 과장일 수 있음(보통은 한 옥타브를 넘는 경우가 많고, 일부 곡이 두 옥타브 이상). 'O quam mirabilis'의 음역에 대한 묘사도 검증이 필요함. 다만 문항의 정답성에는 영향이 없음.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 'a viewer did not need to read…'는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며, 앞 절의 주장(기하학적 형태가 더 직접적으로 의미를 전달한다)을 구체적으로 설명한다. 따라서 독립절 뒤에서 설명을 도입하는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 비교절의 주어 'realistic illustration'과 동사 'could' 사이에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣고, 두 절 사이에는 아무 경계도 두지 않는다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
problem.explanationEn: The words after the blank, "a viewer did not need to read a slogan…," form an independent clause with its own subject and verb, and that clause explains the claim made before it. A colon is the right way to introduce an explanation after an independent clause, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C puts an unnecessary comma between the subject "realistic illustration" and its verb "could," and it still leaves no boundary between the two clauses. D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence.

A는 comma splice, D는 run-on, C는 주어-동사 사이 쉼표 + run-on. 한·영 해설 모두 B를 일관되게 뒷받침하며 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 사실관계(1919–20년 제작, 독일 다름슈타트 건축 수학, 비텝스크 교수)도 무리 없음. 비교절 뒤 콜론 위치를 파악해야 하는 2단계 판단으로 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 비교절 'than realistic illustration could' 뒤에 오는 독립절이라는 경계를 찾아야 하고, 긴 삽입구 때문에 두 단계로 판단해야 한다. 오답 A는 쉼표, C는 위치가 틀린 쉼표, D는 run-on이다. 사실관계(1919–20년 작품, 비텝스크에서 가르침, 다름슈타트 유학)도 대체로 맞다. 중간 난이도에 맞다.

problem.stimulus: Phonaesthemes, which are sound clusters that recur across words with related meanings even though they cannot be separated out as true morphemes, have long puzzled linguists. The English onset "gl-," heard in glitter, gleam, glow, and glimmer, is a widely cited case______ a third of the common English words beginning with those two letters refer in some way to light or vision, a proportion that researchers argue is too high to be coincidental.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The English onset ... is a widely cited case"는 삽입된 수식어 때문에 길지만 그 자체로 완전한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 "more than a third ... refer ..." 역시 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이며, 앞 절의 '사례'를 구체적으로 설명한다. 따라서 설명을 이끄는 콜론을 쓰는 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 세미콜론 뒤에 "because"가 와서 뒷부분이 독립절이 아닌 종속절이 되므로 세미콜론을 쓸 수 없다. D는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절이 붙은 무종지문(run-on)이다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank, "The English onset ... is a widely cited case," is long because of the inserted modifier, but it is still a complete independent clause. The part after the blank, "more than a third ... refer ...," is also an independent clause, and it explains why "gl-" counts as a case. A colon is the right way to introduce that explanation, so C is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B puts "because" after a semicolon, so what follows is a dependent clause, and a semicolon can't be used that way. D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation, which makes a run-on sentence.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 "The English onset 'gl-,' ... is a widely cited case"는 독립절, 뒤 "more than a third ... refer ..."도 독립절이며 앞 절의 '사례'를 설명하므로 콜론(C)이 맞다. A는 comma splice, B는 세미콜론 뒤 because 종속절(세미콜론 오용), D는 run-on. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 C를 일관되게 뒷받침하고 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 'gl-' 단어의 약 1/3이 빛·시각 관련이라는 진술은 음성상징 연구(Bergen 등)에서 보고된 수치와 부합해 사실 오류 없음. 난이도: 긴 삽입 수식어 때문에 앞부분이 독립절임을 판별한 뒤 연결 방식을 고르는 두 단계 판단이 필요하고, A·B가 부분적 타당성을 가진 오답이라 medium 기준 충족. 사소: 선택지 D 앞 공백 두 칸은 표기상 정리 여지가 있으나 판정에 영향 없음.

advisory.note: 빈칸 앞 절에 분사구 삽입이 있고 빈칸 뒤 절은 'more than'으로 시작해 주어 파악이 어렵다. 또 동격 구문이 이어져 있어 독립절인지 판단하는 데 두 단계가 필요하므로 medium 난이도에 맞다. 오답 B(세미콜론+because)는 그럴듯한 함정이다.

problem.explanationEn: The words before the blank ("Performers rely ... head") form an independent clause, and so do the words after it ("this tilting technique ... allows ..."), since that part has its own verb, allows. Two independent clauses need a semicolon between them, so A is correct. B joins the two clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C puts no punctuation between them at all, which makes a run-on sentence. D adds "being" so that the second part looks like a modifier of the first clause, but the verb "allows" is still left without a proper clause around it, so the sentence breaks down.

problem.explanation: 목표는 특정 필사본의 지워진 층이 오늘날 학자들에게 왜 중요한지 강조하는 것이다. D는 아르키메데스 팔림프세스트의 지워진 텍스트가 다른 사본이 없는 유일한 논문 'The Method'를 담고 있다는 점을 들어 그 가치를 분명히 보여 준다. A는 팔림프세스트가 생긴 일반적 이유만 설명할 뿐 특정 필사본의 중요성은 다루지 않는다. B는 연구 방법은 제시하지만 무엇이 발견되었고 왜 중요한지는 말하지 않는다. C는 두 층의 연대를 나열할 뿐 지워진 층이 학자들에게 갖는 가치를 드러내지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to emphasize why the erased layer of a specific manuscript matters to scholars today. D does this: it points out that the recovered text includes "The Method," a treatise that survives nowhere else, so this layer is the only source for it. A only explains why palimpsests were made in general and doesn't address any particular manuscript's value. B describes the imaging technique but never says what was found or why it matters. C gives the dates of the two layers but doesn't show why the hidden layer is valuable.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Palimpsest medieval manuscript overwriting and textual layering revealing historical document conservation analysis

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 지워진 층이 'The Method'의 유일한 사본을 담고 있다는 점으로 학자적 중요성을 직접 드러내며 노트 내용과 정확히 일치한다. 오답 B·C는 해당 필사본을 다루지만 '왜 중요한가'를 빠뜨려 비교 판단이 필요하고, A는 일반적 배경만 제시해 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. 노트의 역사적 사실(13세기 기도서/10세기 아르키메데스 사본, 다중분광 영상, 'The Method' 유일본)은 정확하다. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 동일 결론과 선택지 참조를 가지며 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 난이도 medium 적합.

advisory.note: 사실관계 정확(1999~2008 영상화, The Method 유일 사본). 오답 B·C는 특정 필사본을 다뤄 부분적으로 그럴듯하고, A도 말이 되므로 medium에 맞음. 정답만 유독 길고 구체적이어서 약간 쉬워질 여지는 있음.

problem.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- French critic Roland Barthes (1915–1980) analyzed everyday images and objects as systems of signs.
- In his essay collection Mythologies (1957), he distinguished between denotation, the literal content of a sign, and connotation, the cultural meanings attached to it.
- In "Rhetoric of the Image" (1964), Barthes examined an advertisement for Panzani pasta.
- Literally, the ad shows pasta, tomatoes, peppers, and a string bag.
- Barthes argued that the ad's red, green, and white colors and its fresh produce suggest "Italianicity," an idealized idea of Italian culture.
- Barthes claimed that connotations often seem natural to viewers, which hides the fact that they come from culture.

The student wants to use an example to show how Barthes's two levels of meaning can operate within a single image. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
problem.stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- French critic Roland Barthes (1915–1980) analyzed everyday images and objects as systems of signs.
- In his essay collection Mythologies (1957), he distinguished between denotation, the literal content of a sign, and connotation, the cultural meanings attached to it.
- In "Rhetoric of the Image" (1964), Barthes examined an advertisement for Panzani pasta.
- Literally, the ad shows pasta, tomatoes, peppers, and a string bag.
- Barthes argued that the ad's red, green, and white colors and its fresh produce suggest "Italianicity," an idealized idea of Italian culture.
- Barthes claimed that connotations often seem natural to viewers, which hides the fact that they come from culture.
problem.question: The student wants to use an example to show how Barthes's two levels of meaning can operate within a single image. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: On one level, a Panzani pasta ad simply shows pasta, tomatoes, peppers, and a string bag; on another, Barthes argued, its colors and fresh produce suggest an idealized "Italianicity."
In Mythologies, Barthes distinguished denotation, a sign's literal content, from connotation, the cultural meanings attached to that sign.
Barthes examined a Panzani pasta ad in "Rhetoric of the Image" (1964), several years after publishing his essay collection Mythologies (1957).
On one level, Barthes treated everyday images as systems of signs; on another, he claimed that connotations seem natural to viewers and hide their cultural origins.
problem.explanation: 목표는 한 이미지의 예를 통해 두 의미 층위(외연과 공시)가 함께 작동함을 보이는 것이다. A는 Panzani 광고 하나를 들어 문자 그대로의 내용(파스타, 토마토 등)과 문화적 의미("Italianicity")를 함께 제시하므로 목표에 맞는다. B는 두 층위를 정확히 정의하지만 구체적인 이미지 예시가 없다. C는 광고를 언급하지만 두 의미 층위는 설명하지 않고 출판 연도만 비교한다. D는 A와 같은 문장 틀을 쓰지만 일반적 주장 두 가지를 나열할 뿐 하나의 이미지 사례는 보여 주지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: Your goal is to use one example to show both levels of meaning, denotation and connotation, working inside a single image. Choice A does this with the Panzani ad: it gives the literal content (pasta, tomatoes, peppers, a string bag) and the cultural meaning ("Italianicity") of that same image. Choice B defines the two levels correctly, but it gives no image as an example. Choice C mentions the ad, but it only compares publication dates and never explains the two levels of meaning. Choice D uses the same sentence frame as A, but it just lists two general claims and never shows a single image working on both levels.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Semiotics visual sign systems and symbolic interpretation in Roland Barthes cultural critique methodology

hardJudge.note: 정답 A 검증: 목표(한 이미지 안에서 외연·공시 두 층위가 작동함을 예로 보이기)에 A만 부합. B는 정의만 있고 예시 없음, C는 광고 언급하되 연도 비교에 그침, D는 A와 같은 "On one level… on another" 틀을 써 매력적 오답 역할을 하나 단일 이미지 사례가 아님. 해설(국/영) 모두 정답·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 사실 확인: Barthes 생몰(1915–1980), Mythologies(1957), "Rhetoric of the Image"(1964), Panzani 광고 분석, "Italianicity" 모두 정확. 사소한 점: 원문에서 Barthes는 포스터의 삼색을 "yellow, green, red"로 기술했는데 노트는 이탈리아 국기 색인 "red, green, white"로 적음—학생 노트의 근사 표현으로 보아 치명적 오류로는 보지 않으나 참고 요망. 난이도: 규칙(목표 파악)+선택지 비교 두 단계가 필요하고 D·B가 부분적 근거를 가져 medium 적합.

advisory.note: B(정의만 있고 예시 없음), D(같은 문장 틀이지만 일반적 주장만 있음)가 그럴듯한 오답이라 비교해야 배제됨. C는 약한 오답. 사실관계도 정확함(Mythologies 1957, Rhetoric of the Image 1964, Panzani, Italianicity).

problem.passage:
In Hindustani classical music, a raga is not a fixed composition but a melodic framework: it prescribes ascending and descending note patterns, characteristic phrases, and even an associated time of day for performance. Having absorbed these constraints through years of study under a guru, ______ the alap, an unmetered opening section in which the notes of the raga are introduced one by one, freely yet without violating the framework.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In Hindustani classical music, a raga is not a fixed composition but a melodic framework: it prescribes ascending and descending note patterns, characteristic phrases, and even an associated time of day for performance. Having absorbed these constraints through years of study under a guru, ______ the alap, an unmetered opening section in which the notes of the raga are introduced one by one, freely yet without violating the framework.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the raga's characteristic phrases guide a sitarist improvising
Hindustani music allows a sitarist to improvise
the guru's teachings let a sitarist improvise
problem.explanation: 분사구문 'Having absorbed these constraints through years of study under a guru'는 바로 뒤에 오는 주절의 주어를 수식한다. 구루 밑에서 수년간 공부하며 제약을 익힌 존재는 연주자뿐이므로 주어는 'a sitarist'여야 한다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 수식어구와 가장 가까운 무생물 명사인 'phrases'를 주어로 삼아, 악구가 공부했다는 말이 된다. B는 지문 앞부분의 배경 명사인 'Hindustani music'을 주어로 삼아, 음악이 제약을 익혔다는 말이 된다. C는 사람과 관련된 'the guru's teachings'를 주어로 삼았다. 사람처럼 보이지만 이 경우 가르침이 '구루 밑에서' 공부한 셈이 되므로 논리에 맞지 않는다. A~C는 모두 행위자인 sitarist를 목적어 자리에 두어 수식어가 엉뚱한 대상을 가리키는 현수 수식어 오류이다.
problem.explanationEn: The opening phrase "Having absorbed these constraints through years of study under a guru" modifies whatever comes right after it as the subject of the main clause. Only a performer could have studied under a guru and absorbed the raga's rules, so the subject has to be "a sitarist." That makes D correct. A makes "the raga's characteristic phrases" the subject. That's the closest inanimate noun, but phrases can't study anything. B uses "Hindustani music," the background noun from the start of the passage, and music doesn't absorb constraints either. C picks "the guru's teachings," which sounds connected to a person, but teachings can't study under a guru. In A, B, and C, the real agent (the sitarist) is pushed into an object position, so the modifier dangles.

hardJudge.note: 문두 분사구문 'Having absorbed these constraints ... under a guru'의 의미상 행위자는 sitarist이며 D만 이를 주절 주어로 둔다. A·B·C는 모두 문법적으로 완결되지만 sitarist를 목적어 자리에 두어 현수 수식어가 된다. 특히 C는 인접 명사 'guru'를 활용한 'the guru's teachings'로 사람 관련 명사처럼 보이게 하여, 단순 인접 일치가 아닌 '구루 밑에서 공부한 주체' 판별을 요구하므로 medium 이상의 의미 판단이 필요하다. 라가·알랍 설명은 사실에 부합. 다만 해설의 '가장 가까운 명사' 서술 오류는 수정 권고 대상(판정에는 미반영).

advisory.note: 전형적인 현수 수식어 문항임. 오답 셋이 모두 무생물 주어라서 '사람이 공부했다'는 점만 알아도 곧바로 D가 남음. 행위자를 추적하는 데 추가 사고가 거의 필요 없고, 난이도는 지문 길이와 배경 어휘에서만 나옴.

problem.passage:
In the 1950s, French composer Pierre Schaeffer urged listeners of his musique concrète to practice what he called "reduced listening," attending to a recorded sound's texture, grain, and contour rather than to the object that produced it. A clattering train or a creaking door, he argued, could become pure sonic material once its source was mentally set aside. Many of his early audiences, ______ they kept naming the trains and doors they heard, treating the compositions less as abstract music than as puzzles of identification.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the 1950s, French composer Pierre Schaeffer urged listeners of his musique concrète to practice what he called "reduced listening," attending to a recorded sound's texture, grain, and contour rather than to the object that produced it. A clattering train or a creaking door, he argued, could become pure sonic material once its source was mentally set aside. Many of his early audiences, ______ they kept naming the trains and doors they heard, treating the compositions less as abstract music than as puzzles of identification.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: however, struggled to listen this way;
however, struggled to listen this way,
therefore, struggled to listen this way;
however, struggled to listen this way, and yet
problem.explanation:
먼저 논리 관계를 봐야 한다. 셰페르는 음원을 지우고 소리 자체를 들으라고 했지만, 청중은 그렇게 듣지 못했다. 그러니 두 내용은 대조 관계다. 빈칸 뒤의 'they kept naming…'은 독립절이므로, 앞의 독립절과 이으려면 세미콜론이 필요하다. 접속부사 however는 주어 뒤에 콤마로 끼워 넣을 수 있다. 따라서 정답은 A다.
B: 세미콜론 자리에 콤마만 써서 두 독립절을 이었으므로 콤마 스플라이스다.
C: 구두점 구조는 맞지만, therefore는 인과를 나타내므로 문맥의 대조 관계와 반대다.
D: 이미 however로 대조를 표시했는데 and yet을 또 써서 대조 표현이 중복된다.
problem.explanationEn:
Start with the logic. Schaeffer wanted listeners to set aside a sound's source, but his audiences couldn't do that. That's a contrast. The words after the blank, "they kept naming…," form an independent clause, so you need a semicolon to join it to the clause before it. "However" is a conjunctive adverb, and it can sit after the subject, set off by commas. That makes A correct.
B: It joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which is a comma splice.
C: The punctuation works, but "therefore" signals cause and effect, which is the opposite of the contrast the passage needs.
D: "However" already marks the contrast, so adding "and yet" says the same thing twice.

hardJudge.note: A는 두 독립절을 세미콜론으로 연결하고 주어 뒤 삽입된 however가 앞 문장(셰페르의 주장)과의 대조를 올바르게 표시함. B 콤마 스플라이스, C 인과 접속부사로 논리 역행, D 'and yet'이 두 절 사이에 존재하지 않는 대조를 부여해 오답. 피에르 셰페르·musique concrète·reduced listening 관련 사실 기술은 정확함. 선행 문장의 논리 관계 판단 후 구두점·접속어를 선택해야 하는 hard 특성(clause_relation_punctuation)을 충족하나, 난이도 자체는 hard 중 하단 수준.

advisory.note: 정답 A가 맞다. 이 문항은 대조 관계(however와 therefore 중 무엇인가)와 구두점 구조(세미콜론과 콤마 스플라이스)를 함께 판단하게 한다. C의 therefore는 엄밀히 말하면 접속사가 아니라 접속부사다. 그래도 반대 논리관계를 담은 오답이라는 역할은 한다. D는 however와 and yet이 겹치는 중복 오답으로 성립한다. 다만 오답들이 모두 전형적인 유형이라 hard로서의 난도는 중간 수준을 약간 넘는 정도다.

problem.passage:
In his 1752 treatise on flute playing, the German composer Johann Joachim Quantz warned that a performer who "smothers every melody in trills" was mistaking display for taste. To avoid that error, he urged players to study the expressive restraint of good singers, ______ ornaments sparingly in slow movements, and to save their most elaborate figuration for the repeated sections of a piece.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In his 1752 treatise on flute playing, the German composer Johann Joachim Quantz warned that a performer who "smothers every melody in trills" was mistaking display for taste. To avoid that error, he urged players to study the expressive restraint of good singers, ______ ornaments sparingly in slow movements, and to save their most elaborate figuration for the repeated sections of a piece.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 정답 B: 'urged players' 뒤에 'to study ..., ______ ..., and to save ...'라는 부정사 세 개가 병렬로 이어지므로 빈칸도 'to reserve'가 와야 한다. A 'reserves'는 인용문 속 현재형 'smothers'에 시제를 맞춘 것이지만, 인용문은 별개의 문장이라 병렬 구조와 상관이 없고, 이렇게 되면 주어 없이 정형동사만 남는다. C 'reserving'은 세 항목 중 하나만 동명사/분사로 바꾸어 병렬 구조를 깬다. D 'reserved'는 주절의 과거형 'urged'와 시제는 맞지만, 'urged'와 병렬인 동사로 읽으면 'and to save'와 연결되지 않고, 앞의 'to study'와도 형태가 어긋난다.
problem.explanationEn: B is correct. After "urged players," the sentence lists three parallel infinitives: "to study ..., ______ ..., and to save ...." So the blank needs the same form: "to reserve." A, "reserves," copies the present tense of "smothers" from the quotation. But the quotation is a separate clause and has nothing to do with this list, and "reserves" would leave a finite verb with no subject. C, "reserving," turns just one item of the list into an -ing form, which breaks the parallel structure. D, "reserved," matches the past tense of the main verb "urged." If you read it as a second past-tense verb alongside "urged," though, it doesn't fit with "to study" or "and to save," so the series falls apart.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 'urged players to study ..., ______ ..., and to save ...' 구조에서 세 번째 항목이 'to save'로 고정되어 있으므로 빈칸은 to부정사 'to reserve'만 병렬을 완성함. A는 주어 없는 정형동사(인용문 현재형 'smothers'에 이끌린 함정), C는 세 항목 중 하나만 분사형으로 병렬 파괴, D는 주절 과거형 'urged'와 국소적으로 맞아 보이나 'and to save'와 연결 불가. 해설의 네 선택지 분석 모두 정확하고 모순 없음. 체크리스트 3항은 A가 '인용문과 어긋나는' 시제라기보다 '인용문에 이끌려 주절 시제와 어긋나는' 시제이나, 인용문-주절 간 시제 간섭 함정이라는 취지에는 부합하므로 충족으로 판정. Quantz 1752년 플루트 논고(Versuch)는 실존하며 서술 내용은 일반적 수준으로 사실 오류 없음. 인용문의 현재형과 주절 과거형, 병렬 구조를 동시에 추적해야 하므로 단순 병렬 일치 medium 문항보다 추가 사고를 요구함.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 맞다. 'urged players to study ..., to reserve ..., and to save ...'에서 to부정사 세 개가 병렬을 이룬다. 다만 병렬 항목이 'to study'와 'and to save'로 앞뒤에서 명시되어 있어, 이 유형의 전형적인 medium 문항과 사고 깊이가 같다. 오답 A가 인용문 시제를 끌어오는 함정이지만 인용문이 별개의 문장이라 쉽게 걸러진다. D도 'and to save'와 바로 충돌하므로 판별에 추가 추론이 필요 없다. 그 밖의 위험 요소: 'smothers every melody in trills'는 Quantz(1752, Versuch)의 실제 문구인지 확인되지 않아 지어낸 직접 인용일 수 있다. 'reserve ornaments sparingly'는 연어가 다소 어색하다.

problem.passage:
In the medieval French aube, or dawn song, two lovers who have spent the night together in secret are parted at daybreak, often warned by a watchman or the song of a lark. Scholars have long described the genre as a lyric of private emotion, centered on the lovers' grief at separation. Literary historian Hélène Marcoux, however, notes that in most surviving aubes the voice that speaks longest is not either lover's but the watchman's, and that his speech is mostly about practical dangers: jealous husbands, gossiping courtiers, and the risk of being discovered once it is light. Because the genre gives so much of its space to these warnings, Marcoux argues that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
problem.stimulus: In the medieval French aube, or dawn song, two lovers who have spent the night together in secret are parted at daybreak, often warned by a watchman or the song of a lark. Scholars have long described the genre as a lyric of private emotion, centered on the lovers' grief at separation. Literary historian Hélène Marcoux, however, notes that in most surviving aubes the voice that speaks longest is not either lover's but the watchman's, and that his speech is mostly about practical dangers: jealous husbands, gossiping courtiers, and the risk of being discovered once it is light. Because the genre gives so much of its space to these warnings, Marcoux argues that ______
problem.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: the watchman figure was probably added to aubes by later copyists who wanted to make the poems longer and more dramatic.
the lovers' grief at separation was likely a minor theme that medieval audiences of the aube hardly noticed.
the aube may have been as concerned with the social risks around a secret love as with the lovers' private feelings.
the aube was most likely written to warn real courtiers against forming secret attachments at court.
problem.explanation: 지문은 기존 견해(사적 감정의 서정시)를 제시한 뒤, 가장 긴 발화가 파수꾼의 것이고 그 내용이 발각 위험 같은 사회적 위협이라는 근거를 든다. 따라서 이 장르가 연인의 감정만큼 사회적 위험에도 관심을 두었다는 C가 기존 견해를 보완하는 결론으로 가장 적절하다. A는 파수꾼이 후대에 추가되었다는 주장인데, 지문에는 필사 과정에 관한 근거가 없다. B는 이별의 슬픔을 사소하다고 보아 지나치게 나아간 것으로, 지문은 그 주제를 부정하지 않고 다른 관심사를 덧붙일 뿐이다. D는 경고를 실제 궁정인에게 주는 교훈으로 보지만, 지문은 시의 내용만 다룰 뿐 그런 교훈적 목적을 뒷받침하지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The passage first gives the traditional view that the aube is a lyric of private emotion. It then offers evidence against that view: the watchman speaks the longest, and he talks mostly about social dangers like being discovered. C draws the logical conclusion that the genre cared about these social risks as much as about the lovers' feelings, which adds to the traditional view without throwing it out. A claims the watchman was added later by copyists, but the passage says nothing about how the poems were copied. B goes too far by calling the lovers' grief a minor theme, since the evidence only shows that another concern shared the space. D claims the poems were written to warn real courtiers, but the passage describes what the poems contain, not any teaching purpose behind them.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Aubade dawn song genre and romantic morning departure trope in medieval French courtly lyric poetry

hardJudge.note: Passage logic is sound: evidence (watchman speaks longest, about social dangers) + "because the genre gives so much space to these warnings" leads naturally to the hedged C ("may have been as concerned... as"). B and D are partially grounded (both pick up the social/warning content) but overreach—B dismisses grief, D infers real-world didactic purpose; A is the weakest but still coherent. Requires two-step reasoning (identify evidence + calibrate strength against the traditional view), appropriate for medium. Marcoux appears fictional, which is acceptable for SAT-style items; genre description of the aube is accurate.

advisory.note: C는 'however'가 보여 주는 대조와 경고 내용을 정확히 연결한다. B와 D는 부분적인 근거가 있어 그럴듯하지만 지나치게 나아간 선택지이고, A는 근거가 없다. 지정 정답이 맞다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Abecedarian works, in which each successive sentence or word begins with the next letter of the alphabet, are often treated as mere puzzles. Critic Lena Moravec argues otherwise: because the constraint dictates order in advance, she claims, it strips the writer of any control over sequence, so such texts cannot build genuine narrative momentum and should be read only as displays of verbal ingenuity.

Text 2
Walter Abish's novel Alphabetical Africa is constrained so that its first chapter uses only words beginning with "a," the second adds "b," and so on before the process reverses. Readers have noticed that the expanding and shrinking vocabulary shapes the story itself: characters and events can appear only once their initial letters become available, and the gradual loss of letters in the second half creates a sense of mounting confinement. Here the constraint does not replace narrative design; it becomes one of its chief instruments.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Moravec's claim in Text 1?

Text 2

Readers have noticed that the expanding and shrinking vocabulary shapes the story itself: characters and events can appear only once their initial letters become available, and the gradual loss of letters in the second half creates a sense of mounting confinement. Here the constraint does not replace narrative design; it becomes one of its chief instruments.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Moravec's claim in Text 1?
options: By suggesting that an alphabetical constraint can itself generate the progression of a story rather than preventing it
By suggesting that an alphabetical constraint is valued by readers mainly for the verbal ingenuity it displays
By suggesting that an alphabetical constraint gives writers full control over sequence once the rule is reversed

problem.explanation: Moravec는 알파벳 제약이 순서를 미리 정해 진정한 서사적 추진력을 만들 수 없다고 주장한다. Text 2는 Abish의 소설에서 어휘의 확장·축소가 인물 등장 시점과 점증하는 압박감을 만들어 제약이 서사의 도구가 된다고 말하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Moravec의 입장을 반영할 뿐 Text 2의 요지가 아니다. C는 역전 구조를 언급하지만 Text 2는 작가가 순서를 완전히 통제한다고 하지 않으며 역전도 제약의 일부다. D는 제약이 후반에도 유지되어 오히려 압박감을 만든다는 Text 2 내용과 반대다.
problem.explanationEn: Moravec claims that because an alphabetical constraint fixes order in advance, it cannot produce real narrative momentum. Text 2 shows Abish's expanding and shrinking vocabulary controlling when characters appear and building a sense of confinement, so the constraint drives the story; that makes A correct. B echoes Moravec's own view, not Text 2's point. C picks up the reversal detail, but Text 2 never says the writer gains full control; the reversal is still part of the rule. D contradicts Text 2, where the constraint stays in force in the second half and creates the confinement.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Abecedarian constraint narrative alphabetical ordering and textual puzzle structure in conceptual writing

hardJudge.note: Text 2의 결론("the constraint does not replace narrative design; it becomes one of its chief instruments")은 Moravec의 "cannot build genuine narrative momentum" 주장과 정면으로 대립하므로 A가 유일하게 타당함. B는 Text 1의 어휘(verbal ingenuity)를 그대로 가져온 오답, C는 역전(reverses) 세부를 왜곡("full control"), D는 후반부 세부를 왜곡("abandoned")한 오답으로, 두 지문의 연결과 세부 확인이 필요한 구조라 medium에 적합. Alphabetical Africa(1974)의 구조 기술도 사실과 일치. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 선택지 글자 참조 및 결론이 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음.

advisory.note: Abish의 Alphabetical Africa(1974)에 대한 설명은 사실과 맞다. Moravec는 가상의 인물로 보인다. B와 C는 그럴듯한 오답이고, 정답을 고르려면 두 텍스트를 연결해야 하므로 medium 난이도에 맞다.

problem.passage:
Text 1
Scholars of sixteenth-century Scottish verse often treat the orison, a short devotional prayer-poem, as a casualty of the Reformation. Because Reformed preachers condemned prayers to saints and elaborate Latin liturgy, the argument goes, poets abandoned the orison altogether, and private religious feeling in Scottish verse largely fell silent until the following century.

Text 2
Manuscript miscellanies compiled in Scotland during the 1560s and 1570s tell a different story. Copyists kept writing orisons, but they stripped out invocations of the Virgin and the saints and addressed Christ directly in plain Scots. The intimate, first-person pleading that had defined the form survived; what changed was whom the speaker addressed and in what language.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the scholars' view described in Text 1?
problem.stimulus:
Text 1
Scholars of sixteenth-century Scottish verse often treat the orison, a short devotional prayer-poem, as a casualty of the Reformation. Because Reformed preachers condemned prayers to saints and elaborate Latin liturgy, the argument goes, poets abandoned the orison altogether, and private religious feeling in Scottish verse largely fell silent until the following century.

Text 2
Manuscript miscellanies compiled in Scotland during the 1560s and 1570s tell a different story. Copyists kept writing orisons, but they stripped out invocations of the Virgin and the saints and addressed Christ directly in plain Scots. The intimate, first-person pleading that had defined the form survived; what changed was whom the speaker addressed and in what language.
problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the scholars' view described in Text 1?
options: By agreeing that Reformed objections drove poets to stop composing orisons, while noting that the manuscripts show copyists preserving older Latin prayers
By arguing that the evidence from manuscript collections shows the form was reshaped to suit Reformed doctrine rather than given up
By contending that Reformed preachers in fact encouraged prayers to saints, so their objections could not have affected the form
By suggesting that private religious feeling disappeared from Scottish verse, though for reasons unrelated to the Reformation
problem.explanation: Text 1의 학자들은 종교개혁 이후 오리즌이 버려졌고 개인적 신앙 감정이 침묵했다고 본다. Text 2는 필사본에서 성인 호칭을 빼고 그리스도에게 스코츠어로 직접 호소하는 오리즌이 계속 쓰였음을 보여 주므로, 형식이 사라진 것이 아니라 개혁 교리에 맞게 바뀌었다고 반박할 것이다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 오리즌 작성이 중단되었다는 데 동의하고 라틴어 기도가 보존되었다고 하는데, Text 2는 라틴어와 성인 호칭이 오히려 제거되었다고 말한다. C는 설교자들이 성인 기도를 장려했다고 하지만, 이는 두 지문 어디에도 근거가 없다. D는 신앙 감정이 사라졌다고 하는데, Text 2는 1인칭의 친밀한 호소가 살아남았다고 분명히 말한다.
problem.explanationEn: The scholars in Text 1 claim that orisons were abandoned after the Reformation and that private religious feeling went silent. Text 2 points to manuscripts in which orisons kept being written, now addressed directly to Christ in Scots and without saints, so the form was adapted to Reformed doctrine rather than dropped. That makes B the answer. A agrees that composition stopped and says Latin prayers were preserved, but Text 2 says copyists removed the old invocations and wrote in Scots. C claims preachers encouraged prayers to saints, which neither text supports. D says private feeling disappeared, but Text 2 says the intimate first-person pleading survived.

quality.seed: arts and humanities nonfiction — Orison Scottish devotional prayer form and religious sentiment expression in Reformation-era spiritual verse composition

hardJudge.note: Text 2 explicitly states the form survived with changed addressee and language, directly supporting B. A borrows Text 2's manuscript/copyist framing but inverts the Latin detail and concedes abandonment; D borrows the 'private feeling' thread but contradicts Text 2's final sentence; C is unsupported but plausible-sounding. Two-step reasoning (identify Text 1 claim, then map Text 2's qualified rebuttal) is required. Explanations in both languages match the key and option letters, with no Korean in the English version. Content appears original.

advisory.note: B는 Text 2의 근거(성인 호칭 제거, 스코츠어로 그리스도에게 직접 호소, 1인칭 호소 형식 유지)에서 바로 도출된다. A와 D는 Text 1의 주장을 일부 되풀이하므로 비교해야 배제된다. C는 지문에 근거가 없어 약한 오답이지만 medium 난이도 범위 안에 있다.

problem.passage:
In a well-known 1960s study, researchers told teachers that certain students were likely to make rapid intellectual gains, even though those students had actually been chosen at random. By the end of the year, many of the selected students had improved more than their classmates. Later researchers wanted to know how teachers' beliefs could produce such a change. __Classroom observations showed that teachers gave the "promising" students more praise, called on them more often, and waited longer for their answers.__ These findings suggest that expectations shape student performance through everyday teacher behavior.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In a well-known 1960s study, researchers told teachers that certain students were likely to make rapid intellectual gains, even though those students had actually been chosen at random. By the end of the year, many of the selected students had improved more than their classmates. Later researchers wanted to know how teachers' beliefs could produce such a change. __Classroom observations showed that teachers gave the "promising" students more praise, called on them more often, and waited longer for their answers.__ These findings suggest that expectations shape student performance through everyday teacher behavior.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes how the students in the original study were chosen for the experiment.
It presents evidence that the original study's results were caused by chance.
It provides details that help explain how teachers' beliefs led to student improvement.
It introduces a criticism of the researchers who carried out the original study.
problem.explanation: 바로 앞 문장은 교사의 믿음이 어떻게 변화를 낳았는지라는 질문을 던지고, 밑줄 문장은 칭찬·발표 기회·기다림 시간이라는 구체적 행동으로 그 질문에 답한다. 마지막 문장도 기대가 교사 행동을 통해 작용한다고 정리하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 학생 선발 방식(무작위)을 말하는데, 이는 첫 문장의 내용이다. B는 결과가 우연이라고 하지만 밑줄 문장은 결과를 뒷받침하는 원인을 설명한다. D의 비판은 지문 어디에도 없다.
problem.explanationEn: The sentence just before the underlined one asks how teachers' beliefs could cause the change, and the underlined sentence answers that question with specific behaviors: more praise, more chances to speak, and longer wait time. The final sentence then sums this up by saying expectations work through teacher behavior, so C is correct. A describes how students were chosen (at random), but that information is in the first sentence. B says the results happened by chance, but the underlined sentence explains a cause that supports the results. D is wrong because the text never criticizes the original researchers.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 직전 문장의 '어떻게' 질문에 구체적 교사 행동으로 답하고 마지막 문장이 이를 일반화하므로 C가 정답. A는 첫 문장 내용, B는 지문과 반대, D는 근거 없음. 한국어·영어 해설 결론 및 글자 참조 일치, 영어 해설 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 로젠탈·제이콥슨 연구를 일반 지식 수준에서 재서술한 원문으로 저작권 문제 없음. 단서가 명시적이고 추론 한 단계로 easy에 적합.

advisory.note: Rosenthal-Jacobson(Pygmalion) 연구를 일반적으로 서술함. 앞 문장의 질문에 답하는 구조라 단서가 직접적이고, 오답(무작위 선발, 우연, 비판)은 지문 표면 요소를 활용한 전형적 오답이다.

problem.passage:
In the 1960s and 1970s, British sociologist Basil Bernstein studied how children from different social classes used language. He described two patterns of speech. A "restricted code" relies on shared background knowledge and short, familiar phrases, so speakers often leave meanings unstated. An "elaborated code" spells meanings out in full, using more varied vocabulary and complex sentences. __Bernstein argued that schools mainly reward the elaborated code, which middle-class children were more likely to learn at home.__ In his view, this helped explain why working-class children, who were just as capable, often received lower marks in school.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: In the 1960s and 1970s, British sociologist Basil Bernstein studied how children from different social classes used language. He described two patterns of speech. A "restricted code" relies on shared background knowledge and short, familiar phrases, so speakers often leave meanings unstated. An "elaborated code" spells meanings out in full, using more varied vocabulary and complex sentences. __Bernstein argued that schools mainly reward the elaborated code, which middle-class children were more likely to learn at home.__ In his view, this helped explain why working-class children, who were just as capable, often received lower marks in school.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It defines the restricted code by listing the features that make it different from the elaborated code.
It presents a criticism that later researchers raised against the two speech patterns Bernstein described.
It offers evidence that working-class children had less ability than middle-class children.
It states a claim that links the two speech patterns to the difference in school results described afterward.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 학교가 정교한 코드를 보상하며 중산층 아이들이 이를 집에서 배운다는 Bernstein의 주장으로, 앞서 소개된 두 언어 코드를 뒤 문장의 성적 격차 설명과 연결한다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 제한된 코드의 정의가 밑줄 앞 문장에서 이미 제시되었으므로 틀리다. B는 밑줄 문장이 후대 연구자의 비판이 아니라 Bernstein 자신의 주장이므로 틀리다. C는 지문이 노동계급 아이들도 똑같이 능력이 있다고 말하므로 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence gives Bernstein's claim that schools reward the elaborated code, which middle-class children tend to learn at home. That claim connects the two speech patterns to the gap in school marks explained in the next sentence, so D is correct. A is wrong because the restricted code is already defined in an earlier sentence. B is wrong because the sentence is Bernstein's own argument, not a criticism from later researchers. C is wrong because the text says working-class children were just as capable.

quality.seed: social science research — Bernstein language codes restricted versus elaborated speech patterns and social class educational achievement disparities

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 두 코드 설명과 뒤이은 성적 격차 설명을 잇는 Bernstein의 주장이므로 D가 정답. A(정의는 앞 문장), B(후대 비판 아님), C(지문이 '똑같이 능력 있다'고 명시)는 지문 단서로 즉시 배제 가능하되 전형적 오개념으로 그럴듯함. Bernstein의 restricted/elaborated code 서술은 사실에 부합. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. 지문은 자체 작성된 설명문으로 저작권 우려 없음.

advisory.note: Bernstein의 코드 이론 서술은 사실과 맞다. 오답들은 각각 위치 혼동, 출처 혼동, 내용 반대라는 전형적 오개념이고, 지문의 단서로 바로 배제된다.

problem.passage:
In the early 1990s, anthropologist Jean Lave and educational theorist Etienne Wenger studied how tailors, midwives, and butchers learn their trades. Their theory of situated learning, based on these case studies, ______ that newcomers gain skills mainly by taking part in the daily work of a community of practice. At first, apprentices handle simple tasks at the edges of the group, and they slowly move toward more central roles.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In the early 1990s, anthropologist Jean Lave and educational theorist Etienne Wenger studied how tailors, midwives, and butchers learn their trades. Their theory of situated learning, based on these case studies, ______ that newcomers gain skills mainly by taking part in the daily work of a community of practice. At first, apprentices handle simple tasks at the edges of the group, and they slowly move toward more central roles.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'theory'이고, 'based on these case studies'는 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어든 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사 A 'argues'가 맞다. B, C, D는 모두 복수 주어에 쓰는 동사형('argue', 'are arguing', 'have argued')으로, 'case studies'나 'Lave and Wenger'를 주어로 잘못 본 경우에 고르기 쉽다. 단수 주어 'theory'와 수가 일치하지 않으므로 모두 틀리다.
problem.explanationEn: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "theory." The phrase "based on these case studies" is just a modifier sitting between the subject and the verb. So the sentence needs a singular verb, and that's choice A, "argues." Choices B, C, and D are all plural verb forms ("argue," "are arguing," "have argued"), which might look right if you mistake "case studies" or "Lave and Wenger" for the subject. None of them agrees with the singular subject "theory," so they're all wrong.

problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "these speakers arranged ... from east to west"와 뒤 "English speakers ... arranged the cards from left to right"는 각각 완전한 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 잇는 데는 세미콜론이 맞으므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만 써서 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 문장부호가 아예 없어 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. C의 "meanwhile"은 접속부사라 등위접속사가 아니므로, 쉼표만으로는 여전히 쉼표 스플라이스이다.
problem.explanationEn: The text before the blank ("these speakers arranged ... from east to west") and the text after it ("English speakers ... arranged the cards from left to right") are both independent clauses. When two independent clauses are joined without a conjunction, a semicolon is the right punctuation, so D is correct. A uses only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B has no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C adds "meanwhile," but that word is a conjunctive adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so a comma before it still gives you a comma splice.

C and D are participles, not finite verbs, so either one would leave the sentence without a main verb.

Since the 1990s, psychologists have documented a phenomenon called stereotype threat: when people are reminded of a negative stereotype about a group they belong to, their performance on tasks related to that stereotype often declines. Early explanations held that the reminder simply lowered motivation, but later studies complicated that view. In one line of research, participants under threat reported trying just as hard as others, yet scored lower on a demanding math test. Measures taken during the test showed that these participants were spending mental effort monitoring their own performance and suppressing worried thoughts. This effort drew on working memory, the same limited resource needed to hold and manipulate numbers. When researchers gave participants a brief strategy for reframing their anxiety before the test, the gap shrank considerably, even though the stereotype had still been made salient.

Based on the text, what is the main point the researchers' findings support?
problem.stimulus: Since the 1990s, psychologists have documented a phenomenon called stereotype threat: when people are reminded of a negative stereotype about a group they belong to, their performance on tasks related to that stereotype often declines. Early explanations held that the reminder simply lowered motivation, but later studies complicated that view. In one line of research, participants under threat reported trying just as hard as others, yet scored lower on a demanding math test. Measures taken during the test showed that these participants were spending mental effort monitoring their own performance and suppressing worried thoughts. This effort drew on working memory, the same limited resource needed to hold and manipulate numbers. When researchers gave participants a brief strategy for reframing their anxiety before the test, the gap shrank considerably, even though the stereotype had still been made salient.
problem.question: Based on the text, what is the main point the researchers' findings support?
options: Stereotype threat lowers test scores mainly because participants who are reminded of a stereotype stop trying as hard on the task.
Stereotype threat can be eliminated entirely by preventing negative stereotypes from becoming salient before a test begins.
Stereotype threat appears to impair performance largely by consuming mental resources that the task itself requires.
Stereotype threat affects performance on math tests more strongly than it affects performance on other demanding tasks.
problem.explanation: 지문은 위협을 받은 참가자들이 노력은 똑같이 했지만, 자기 감시와 걱정 억제에 작업 기억을 써서 수학 과제에 쓸 자원이 줄었다고 설명하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 초기 설명을 그대로 옮긴 것이고, 지문은 이 설명을 반박했다. B는 고정관념이 여전히 부각된 상태에서도 재구성 전략으로 격차가 줄었다는 내용과 맞지 않으며, '완전히 제거'된다는 말도 지나치다. D는 수학을 예로 들었을 뿐 다른 과제와 비교한 적이 없으므로 근거가 없다.
problem.explanationEn: C is correct. The text says threatened participants tried just as hard as the others. Their scores dropped because monitoring themselves and suppressing worry used up working memory, which the math task also needed. A repeats the early explanation that the text goes on to challenge. B doesn't fit the finding that the gap shrank even though the stereotype was still salient, and "eliminated entirely" goes too far. Early research on the bystander effect suggested a simple pattern: the more people who witness an emergency, the less likely any one of them is to help. Psychologists explained this through diffusion of responsibility, the idea that each witness feels less personally obligated when others are present. In real public conflicts, at least one bystander intervened in roughly nine out of ten cases, and larger crowds were actually associated with a higher chance that someone would step in. In his well-known Bobo doll studies of the early 1960s, psychologist Albert Bandura had children watch an adult hit and kick an inflatable doll. In a 1965 follow-up, he changed what happened to the adult afterward: some children saw the model praised, some saw the model scolded, and some saw no consequence at all. Children who had watched the scolded model later copied fewer of the aggressive acts on their own. When Bandura then offered every child a small reward for showing what the model had done, however, the differences between the groups mostly disappeared, and nearly all the children performed the aggressive acts accurately. In 1950, Theodor Adorno and his colleagues published The Authoritarian Personality, a study that sought to explain why some ordinary people might be drawn to fascist movements. Using questionnaires such as the F-scale, the researchers identified a cluster of traits—rigid, black-and-white thinking, deference to strong leaders, and hostility toward outsiders—that they argued formed a stable personality type rooted in strict childhood discipline. Later scholars, however, criticized the F-scale's design: because every item was worded so that agreeing indicated authoritarianism, respondents who simply tended to agree with statements could score high regardless of their actual views. Even so, many researchers have retained the study's core insight. Subsequent work using better-balanced measures has continued to find that rigid thinking, submission to authority, and intolerance tend to occur together, suggesting that Adorno's team identified a real pattern even if their original tools for detecting it were flawed.

problem.passage:
Prospect theory, developed by psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky, holds that people judge outcomes as gains or losses relative to a reference point rather than in terms of final wealth. A central claim of the theory is that losses carry more psychological weight than gains of the same size: losing $100 feels worse than winning $100 feels good. Researchers have often tested this idea with coin-flip gambles, and many participants turn down a bet offering an equal chance of winning $150 or losing $100, even though the bet's expected value is positive. Later studies, however, have complicated the picture. When the amounts at stake are very small, such as a few cents, or when participants routinely handle such trades, as experienced market traders do, the gap between the weight of losses and the weight of gains often shrinks or disappears. These findings suggest that loss aversion is real but not fixed, since its strength depends on the size of the stakes and on the decision maker's familiarity with the situation.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 초기 해석(덮어쓰기)에 반하는 증거를 제시하고 다음 문장의 출처 혼동 설명으로 연결되므로 B가 옳다. A는 방향 반대, C는 효과의 강도가 아닌 원인 재해석이라는 점에서 배제, D는 실험 참가자와 법정 증인을 혼동하며 지문 내용과도 모순. Loftus & Palmer 실험 묘사는 정확하고 자체 서술이다. 전후 문장 연결이 필요하고 C가 그럴듯한 근접 오답이어서 medium에 적합.

problem.passage:
Anthropologist Victor Turner argued that initiation rites do more than announce that a child has become an adult. In his account, initiates pass through a "liminal" phase in which ordinary ranks are suspended: novices are often stripped of names, dressed identically, and made to share hardships. __Out of this leveling, Turner claimed, arises "communitas," an intense sense of equality and solidarity among those undergoing the rite together.__ Researchers studying contemporary adolescent ceremonies have found Turner's framework useful but incomplete. In a study of summer-camp induction rituals, sociologist Mara Delgado observed that campers did report strong bonds during the ritual, yet older counselors deliberately preserved certain hierarchies throughout, suggesting that liminal phases may reshape social structure rather than erase it.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
problem.stimulus: Anthropologist Victor Turner argued that initiation rites do more than announce that a child has become an adult. In his account, initiates pass through a "liminal" phase in which ordinary ranks are suspended: novices are often stripped of names, dressed identically, and made to share hardships. __Out of this leveling, Turner claimed, arises "communitas," an intense sense of equality and solidarity among those undergoing the rite together.__ Researchers studying contemporary adolescent ceremonies have found Turner's framework useful but incomplete. In a study of summer-camp induction rituals, sociologist Mara Delgado observed that campers did report strong bonds during the ritual, yet older counselors deliberately preserved certain hierarchies throughout, suggesting that liminal phases may reshape social structure rather than erase it.
problem.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents evidence from Delgado's study that challenges Turner's account of the liminal phase.
It explains why initiates are stripped of names and dressed identically during initiation rites.
It introduces a criticism of Turner's framework that later researchers have accepted without qualification.
It identifies a consequence Turner attributed to the liminal phase, which a later study partly complicates.
problem.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 리미널 단계의 평등화에서 '코뮤니타스'가 생긴다는 Turner의 주장, 즉 그 단계의 결과를 제시하고, 뒤의 Delgado 연구는 유대는 확인하면서도 위계가 유지됨을 보여 이를 부분적으로 복잡하게 만든다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 밑줄 문장이 Delgado의 증거가 아니라 Turner의 주장이므로 틀리다. B는 이름 박탈 등은 원인(평등화)으로 앞 문장에 나오고 밑줄 문장은 그 결과를 말할 뿐 이유를 설명하지 않는다. C는 밑줄 문장이 비판이 아니며, 후속 연구도 '조건 없이' 받아들인 것이 아니다.
problem.explanationEn: The underlined sentence states Turner's claim that communitas arises from the leveling of the liminal phase, which is a result he attributed to that phase. Delgado's study later confirms the bonds but shows that hierarchies persisted, so it partly complicates the claim, making D correct. A is wrong because the sentence reports Turner's view, not Delgado's evidence. B is wrong because the sentence describes what follows from the stripping of names and identical dress, not why those practices happen. C is wrong because the sentence is not a criticism, and later researchers called the framework incomplete instead of accepting a criticism without qualification.

hardJudge.note: 밑줄 문장은 Turner가 리미널 단계의 결과로 본 '코뮤니타스'를 제시하며, 뒤의 Delgado 연구(유대 확인 + 위계 유지)가 이를 부분적으로 복잡하게 하므로 D가 정확함. A(Delgado 증거 아님), B(이유 설명 아님), C(비판 아님·'조건 없이 수용' 아님) 모두 배제 가능. 한·영 해설 결론·글자 참조 일치, 영어 자연스럽고 한글 없음. Turner의 liminality/communitas 개념 서술 정확(Delgado는 가상 연구자로 보이나 사실 오류 아님). 밑줄 문장의 역할을 뒤 문단과 연결해 판단해야 하는 두 단계 구조로 medium에 적합하며, A·C는 후반부 키워드(연구·불완전함)를 차용한 부분적 근거를 가짐.

advisory.note: D가 명확한 정답이다. A(Delgado의 증거로 오인)와 B(원인-결과 혼동)는 그럴듯한 오답이고, C는 약하지만 말은 된다. 난이도는 medium에 적합하다.

problem.passage:
In Solomon Asch's 1951 conformity study, participants judged which of three comparison lines matched a reference line, a task so easy that people working alone almost never erred. When seated among confederates who unanimously gave a wrong answer, however, participants went along with the group on roughly a third of the critical ______ Asch attributed this pattern largely to normative influence, the wish to avoid standing out from others, rather than to any genuine change in what participants saw.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.stimulus: In Solomon Asch's 1951 conformity study, participants judged which of three comparison lines matched a reference line, a task so easy that people working alone almost never erred. When seated among confederates who unanimously gave a wrong answer, however, participants went along with the group on roughly a third of the critical ______ Asch attributed this pattern largely to normative influence, the wish to avoid standing out from others, rather than to any genuine change in what participants saw.
problem.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
problem.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'When seated ... critical trials'는 'participants went along'을 주절로 갖는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'Asch attributed this pattern ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오류(comma splice)가 된다. B는 관계사 which를 넣으면 뒤 절에 이미 목적어 'this pattern'이 있어 관계절이 성립하지 않는다. D는 등위접속사 and 앞에 쉼표가 없어 두 독립절이 제대로 구분되지 않는다.
problem.explanationEn: The part before the blank is an independent clause whose main verb is "participants went along," and the part after the blank, "Asch attributed this pattern...," is also an independent clause with its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so C is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B adds "which," but the clause after it already has its own object ("this pattern"), so it can't work as a relative clause. D uses "and" with no comma in front of it, so the two independent clauses aren't properly separated.

hardJudge.note: 검산: 빈칸 앞 'When seated..., however, participants went along with the group on roughly a third of the critical trials'는 종속절+독립절 구조이고, 빈칸 뒤 'Asch attributed this pattern largely to normative influence...'도 독립절이므로 세미콜론(C)이 유일하게 옳다. A는 comma splice, B는 'which'가 뒤 절에서 문법적 역할이 없어(이미 주어·목적어 완비) 성립 불가, D는 등위접속사 앞 쉼표 누락으로 SAT 관례상 오답(공식 해설 관례 "Without a comma preceding it, 'and' can't be used to join two independent clauses"와 일치). 다만 D는 일반 문법상 가장 논쟁 여지가 있는 오답이지만 SAT 기준에서는 수용 가능. 사실 관계: Asch 1951 실험, 약 1/3(약 32~37%) 동조, 규범적 영향 귀인 모두 타당. 긴 도입구와 삽입된 'however' 때문에 독립절 경계 파악이 필요해 medium에 적합. 저작권 의심 없음(독창적 서술).

advisory.note: 독립절 두 개를 연결하는 표준 문항이다. 빈칸 앞에 도입 종속절이 있고 빈칸 뒤 절은 길어서 훑어 읽으면 틀리기 쉽다. D(쉼표 없는 and)와 B(which)는 그럴듯한 오답이어서 중간 난이도에 맞다. Asch의 연구 내용(약 1/3 동조, 규범적 영향)도 사실과 일치한다.
